`README.md`:

```md
# Corvus

ML-based anti-cheat data collector and scorer for the OneLiteFeather network.

A Velocity plugin passively records player packets via PacketEvents, an ingest service stores them
pseudonymised in a data lake (Parquet on S3/MinIO, catalog in PostgreSQL), curated pools feed model
training, and a CPU-only scoring service publishes a per-player "likely cheating" score.

Corvus never sanctions players on its own; the score is a decision aid for staff.

## Layout

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `proto/` | Protobuf schemas shared by Java and Python |
| `plugin/` | Velocity capture plugin (Java) |
| `services/` | Python services: ingest, enrich, score |
| `ml/` | Python: evaluation, training, pilot analysis |
| `ui/` | Management UI (Nuxt, Material Design 3) |
| `deploy/` | Docker Compose (pilot/standalone), Helm |

Requirements and architecture decisions (ADR-CORV-*) live in the OneLiteFeather Outline wiki.

## License

Apache License 2.0, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

```

`api/src/main/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/api/CorvusApi.java`:

```java
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

import java.util.Collection;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.UUID;

/**
 * Read access to the player scores received by the Corvus plugin. Obtain it with {@link CorvusProvider#get()}.
 *
 * <p><strong>Scores are decision aids.</strong> Only {@link ScoreStage#ENFORCE} scores are meant for automated
 * actions; canary scores are informational and shadow scores are never exposed. Corvus never sanctions players.
 *
 * <p>Scores exist only for players that are currently online on this proxy and only after the scoring service
 * published one; they are forgotten when the player disconnects. All methods are thread-safe and non-blocking.
 */
public interface CorvusApi {

    /** The latest score of {@code player} in {@code gameContext}; if several domains exist, the most recent one. */
    Optional<PlayerScore> latestScore(UUID player, String gameContext);

    /** The latest score per (game context, domain) of {@code player}. Empty if none; the result is a snapshot. */
    Collection<PlayerScore> latestScores(UUID player);

    /**
     * Registers a listener for score updates. Listeners are invoked asynchronously, see {@link ScoreListener}.
     *
     * @return a handle to remove the listener again; plugins should do that when they are disabled
     */
    Registration registerScoreListener(ScoreListener listener);

    /** Handle returned by {@link #registerScoreListener(ScoreListener)}. */
    interface Registration {

        /** Removes the listener; calling it again has no effect. */
        void unregister();
    }
}

`api/src/main/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/api/CorvusProvider.java`:

```java
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference;

/**
 * Static access point to the {@link CorvusApi} of the running Corvus plugin. Velocity has no service registry,
 * so this holder is the lookup. Declare a dependency on the plugin id {@code corvus} so it is loaded first.
 *
 * <p>Corvus scores are decision aids; see {@link CorvusApi}.
 */
public final class CorvusProvider {

    private static final AtomicReference<CorvusApi> INSTANCE = new AtomicReference<>();

    private CorvusProvider() {
    }

    /**
     * The API of the running Corvus plugin.
     *
     * @throws IllegalStateException if Corvus is not loaded or not started yet
     */
    public static CorvusApi get() {
        CorvusApi api = INSTANCE.get();
        if (api == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Corvus is not available (plugin not loaded or not started yet)");
        }
        return api;
    }

    /** Like {@link #get()} but empty instead of throwing. */
    public static Optional<CorvusApi> find() {
        return Optional.ofNullable(INSTANCE.get());
    }

    /** Called by the Corvus plugin on start. Other plugins must not call this. */
    public static void register(CorvusApi api) {
        INSTANCE.set(Objects.requireNonNull(api, "api"));
    }

    /** Called by the Corvus plugin on shutdown (and by tests); only removes {@code api} if it is registered. */
    public static void unregister(CorvusApi api) {
        INSTANCE.compareAndSet(api, null);
    }
}

```

`api/src/main/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/api/PlayerScore.java`:

```java
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.UUID;

/**
 * The latest judgement of one Corvus model about one online player. Immutable.
 *
 * <p><strong>Decision aid, not a verdict.</strong> A score is a probability-like model output in [0, 1]; higher
 * means more likely cheating. Only scores whose {@link #stage()} is {@link ScoreStage#ENFORCE} are meant for
 * automated actions; {@link ScoreStage#CANARY} scores are informational. Corvus never sanctions players, any
 * consequence is the decision of the plugin that reads the score.
 *
 * @param player        the online player the score is about
 * @param gameContext   game context tag of the backend server, e.g. {@code lobby} or {@code pvp}
 * @param domain        model domain, e.g. {@code movement}, {@code combat}
 * @param score         score of the latest window, in [0, 1]
 * @param smoothedScore score smoothed over the player's recent windows, in [0, 1]
 * @param windows       number of windows behind {@code smoothedScore}
 * @param modelName     name of the model that produced the score
 * @param modelVersion  version of that model
 * @param stage         rollout stage of the model, never shadow
 * @param scoredAt      when the score was produced
 */
public record PlayerScore(
        UUID player,
        String gameContext,
        String domain,
        float score,
        float smoothedScore,
        int windows,
        String modelName,
        String modelVersion,
        ScoreStage stage,
        Instant scoredAt) {

    public PlayerScore {
        Objects.requireNonNull(player, "player");
        Objects.requireNonNull(gameContext, "gameContext");
        Objects.requireNonNull(domain, "domain");
        Objects.requireNonNull(modelName, "modelName");
        Objects.requireNonNull(modelVersion, "modelVersion");
        Objects.requireNonNull(stage, "stage");
        Objects.requireNonNull(scoredAt, "scoredAt");
        requireUnit(score, "score");
        requireUnit(smoothedScore, "smoothedScore");
        if (windows < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("windows must not be negative: " + windows);
        }
    }

    private static void requireUnit(float value, String name) {
        if (!(value >= 0f && value <= 1f)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(name + " must be in [0, 1]: " + value);
        }
    }
}

```

`api/src/main/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/api/ScoreListener.java`:

```java
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

/**
 * Receives score updates for players that are online on this proxy.
 *
 * <p>Invoked asynchronously on a Corvus worker thread, never on a Netty or Velocity event thread, so it may do
 * light work but should not block for long: a bounded queue sits in front of the workers and updates are dropped
 * when it is full. An exception thrown by one listener does not affect other listeners.
 *
 * <p>Scores are decision aids. Only {@link ScoreStage#ENFORCE} scores are meant for automated actions, and
 * Corvus never sanctions players.
 */
@FunctionalInterface
public interface ScoreListener {

    /** Called when a newer score for (player, game context, domain) arrived. */
    void onScore(PlayerScore score);
}

```

`api/src/main/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/api/ScoreStage.java`:

```java
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

/**
 * Rollout stage of the model that produced a score. Scores of shadow models are never published to the proxy and
 * therefore have no constant here.
 *
 * <p>Corvus scores are decision aids and Corvus never sanctions players. Only {@link #ENFORCE} scores are meant
 * for automated actions in other plugins.
 */
public enum ScoreStage {

    /** Model on trial: informational only, must not drive any automated action. */
    CANARY,

    /** Model approved for automated decisions in other systems. Still a decision aid, not a verdict. */
    ENFORCE;

    /** True when a score of this stage may drive automated actions. */
    public boolean mayDriveAutomatedActions() {
        return this == ENFORCE;
    }
}

 * verdict. Only scores of stage {@link net.onelitefeather.corvus.api.ScoreStage#ENFORCE} are meant to drive
 * automated actions in other plugins; {@link net.onelitefeather.corvus.api.ScoreStage#CANARY} scores are
 * informational. Corvus itself never sanctions players, it only reports scores.
 */
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

`api/src/test/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/api/CorvusProviderTest.java`:

```java
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.util.Collection;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.UUID;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertSame;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertThrows;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

class CorvusProviderTest {

    private final CorvusApi api = new CorvusApi() {
        @Override
        public Optional<PlayerScore> latestScore(UUID player, String gameContext) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }

        @Override
        public Collection<PlayerScore> latestScores(UUID player) {
            return List.of();
        }

        @Override
        public Registration registerScoreListener(ScoreListener listener) {
            return () -> { };
        }
    };

    @AfterEach
    void reset() {
        CorvusProvider.unregister(api);
    }

    @Test
    void getFailsBeforeRegistration() {
        assertThrows(IllegalStateException.class, CorvusProvider::get);
        assertTrue(CorvusProvider.find().isEmpty());
    }

    @Test
    void getReturnsTheRegisteredApi() {
        CorvusProvider.register(api);

        assertSame(api, CorvusProvider.get());
    }

    @Test
    void unregisterOnlyRemovesTheSameInstance() {
        CorvusProvider.register(api);
        CorvusProvider.unregister(new CorvusApi() {
            @Override
            public Optional<PlayerScore> latestScore(UUID player, String gameContext) {
                return Optional.empty();
            }

            @Override
            public Collection<PlayerScore> latestScores(UUID player) {
                return List.of();
            }

            @Override
            public Registration registerScoreListener(ScoreListener listener) {
                return () -> { };
            }
        });

        assertSame(api, CorvusProvider.get());
    }
}

`api/src/test/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/api/PlayerScoreTest.java`:

```java
package net.onelitefeather.corvus.api;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.lang.reflect.Modifier;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.UUID;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertThrows;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

class PlayerScoreTest {

    private static final UUID PLAYER = new UUID(1, 2);
    private static final Instant AT = Instant.parse("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z");

    private static PlayerScore score(float score, float smoothed, int windows) {
        return new PlayerScore(PLAYER, "pvp", "combat", score, smoothed, windows, "m", "1", ScoreStage.ENFORCE, AT);
    }

    @Test
    void equalComponentsGiveEqualScores() {
        assertEquals(score(0.5f, 0.4f, 3), score(0.5f, 0.4f, 3));
    }

    @Test
    void allFieldsAreFinalSoTheRecordCannotBeMutated() {
        for (var field : PlayerScore.class.getDeclaredFields()) {
            assertTrue(Modifier.isFinal(field.getModifiers()), field.getName() + " must be final");
        }
        assertTrue(PlayerScore.class.isRecord());
    }

    @Test
    void scoreOutsideUnitIntervalIsRejected() {
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> score(1.01f, 0.5f, 1));
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> score(0.5f, -0.1f, 1));
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> score(Float.NaN, 0.5f, 1));
    }

    @Test
    void negativeWindowsAreRejected() {
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> score(0.5f, 0.5f, -1));
    }

    @Test
    void nullComponentsAreRejected() {
        assertThrows(NullPointerException.class, () -> new PlayerScore(null, "pvp", "combat", 0.5f, 0.5f, 1,
                "m", "1", ScoreStage.ENFORCE, AT));
        assertThrows(NullPointerException.class, () -> new PlayerScore(PLAYER, "pvp", "combat", 0.5f, 0.5f, 1,
                "m", "1", null, AT));
    }

    @Test
    void shadowIsNotAnExposedStage() {
        for (ScoreStage stage : ScoreStage.values()) {
            assertFalse(stage.name().contains("SHADOW"), "shadow must never be exposed");
        }
    }

    @Test
    void onlyEnforceMayDriveAutomatedActions() {
        assertTrue(ScoreStage.ENFORCE.mayDriveAutomatedActions());
        assertFalse(ScoreStage.CANARY.mayDriveAutomatedActions());
    }
}

`deploy/dev/compose.yaml`:

```yaml
# Local development stack for the Corvus ingest service, online scoring and control-plane API.
# See docs/how-to/run-ingest-locally.md.
#   cp .env.example .env   (fill in the generated values; credentials are read from .env)
#   cp .env.api.example .env.api   (optional, only for the api service; holds its tokens and keys)
#   docker compose up --build   (the ui service is then served on http://127.0.0.1:8081)

x-ingest-env: &ingest-env
  CORVUS_NATS_URL: nats://nats:4222
  # The password comes from PGPASSWORD (libpq/psycopg), set in .env.
  CORVUS_PG_DSN: postgresql://corvus@postgres:5432/corvus
  CORVUS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL: http://s3:9000
  CORVUS_S3_BUCKET: corvus-lake

services:
  nats:
    image: nats:2.11.17-alpine
    command: ["-js", "-sd", "/data", "-m", "8222"]
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:4222:4222"
    volumes:
      - nats-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:8222/healthz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1.0"
          memory: 512M

  # S3-compatible object store. MinIO no longer publishes container images, so the dev stack uses RustFS.
  s3:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:1.0.1
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      RUSTFS_VOLUMES: /data
      RUSTFS_ADDRESS: ":9000"
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ADDRESS: ":9001"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:9000:9000"
      - "127.0.0.1:9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - s3-data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1.0"
          memory: 1G

  # Creates the bucket; retries until the object store accepts requests.
  s3-init:
    image: amazon/aws-cli:2.27.63
    env_file: .env
    depends_on:
      - s3
    environment:
      AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
    command:
      - |
        export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$$CORVUS_S3_ACCESS_KEY" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$$CORVUS_S3_SECRET_KEY"
        for i in $$(seq 1 30); do
          aws --endpoint-url http://s3:9000 s3api head-bucket --bucket corvus-lake 2>/dev/null && exit 0
          aws --endpoint-url http://s3:9000 s3api create-bucket --bucket corvus-lake 2>/dev/null && exit 0
          sleep 2
        done
        exit 1
    restart: "no"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 256M

  postgres:
    image: postgres:17.6-alpine
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: corvus
      POSTGRES_DB: corvus
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U corvus -d corvus"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1.0"
          memory: 512M

  migrate:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: services/Dockerfile
    image: corvus-services:dev
    command: ["corvus-migrate"]
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      <<: *ingest-env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 256M

  ingest:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: services/Dockerfile
    image: corvus-services:dev
    command: ["corvus-ingest"]
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      <<: *ingest-env
      CORVUS_WORKERS: "2"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:9464:9464"
    depends_on:
      nats:
        condition: service_healthy
      s3-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2.0"
          memory: 1G

  # Online scoring (docs/how-to/run-scoring-locally.md). One replica owns every partition; with more
  # replicas set CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS and give each its own CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICA_INDEX.
  score:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: services/Dockerfile
    image: corvus-services:dev
    command: ["corvus-score"]
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      <<: *ingest-env
      CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS: "1"
      CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICA_INDEX: "0"
      CORVUS_SCORE_CPUS: "2"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:9465:9464"
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:size=512M,uid=10001,gid=10001
    depends_on:
      nats:
        condition: service_healthy
      s3-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    restart: unless-stopped
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2.0"
          memory: 1G

  # Control-plane API (docs/reference/control-plane-api.md). Its secrets (dev token, pseudonym key, proxy
  # tokens) live in .env.api so that the other services never see them.
  api:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: services/Dockerfile
    image: corvus-services:dev
    command: ["corvus-api"]
    env_file:
      - .env
      - path: .env.api
        required: false
    environment:
      CORVUS_PG_DSN: postgresql://corvus@postgres:5432/corvus
      CORVUS_API_PORT: "8080"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz', timeout=3)"
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 6
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1.0"
          memory: 512M

  # Management UI (docs/how-to/run-the-ui.md). It proxies /api/ to the api service on its own origin, so the
  # browser needs no CORS. It holds no secrets: log in with the dev token from .env.api (CORVUS_API_DEV_TOKEN).
  ui:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: ui/Dockerfile
    image: corvus-ui:dev
    environment:
      CORVUS_UI_BASE_PATH: /
      CORVUS_UI_API_UPSTREAM: http://api:8080
    volumes:
      - ./ui-config.json:/usr/share/nginx/html/config.json:ro
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8081:8080"
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 128M

volumes:
  nats-data:
  s3-data:
  postgres-data:

```

  mountPath: /etc/corvus/nats
  readOnly: true
{{- end }}

{{/* Call with (dict "root" $ "credsKey" ...): only this component's key is mounted. */}}

- name: nats-creds
  secret:

{{- end }}
{{- end }}

{{/* Origin (scheme://host[:port]) of an absolute URL; empty for anything else. */}}
{{- define "corvus.origin" -}}
{{- regexFind "^https?://[^/?#]+" (toString .) -}}
{{- end }}

{{/* Upstream the UI proxies /api/ to: ui.apiUpstream, else the in-cluster api Service. */}}
{{- define "corvus.uiApiUpstream" -}}
{{- if .Values.ui.apiUpstream -}}
{{- .Values.ui.apiUpstream -}}
{{- else if and .Values.ui.proxyApi .Values.api.enabled -}}
{{- printf "http://%s-api:%v" (include "corvus.fullname" .) .Values.api.port -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- end }}

{{- end }}

{{/* Plain extra env map. Call with the map. */}}
{{- define "corvus.extraEnv" -}}

  value: {{ $v | quote }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

{{/* Ingress spec. Call with (dict "cfg" .Values.api.ingress "svc" "name" "port" 8080) */}}

{{- end }}
{{- with .cfg.tls }}

  {{- toYaml . | nindent 2 }}
{{- end }}
rules:
  {{- $svc := .svc }}
  {{- $port := .port }}
  {{- range .cfg.hosts }}
  - host: {{ .host | quote }}
    http:
      paths:
        {{- range .paths }}
        - path: {{ .path }}
          pathType: {{ .pathType | default "Prefix" }}
          backend:
            service:
              name: {{ $svc }}
              port:
                number: {{ $port }}
        {{- end }}
  {{- end }}

`deploy/helm/corvus/templates/networkpolicy.yaml`:

```yaml
{{- if .Values.networkPolicy.enabled }}
{{- $metricsPeer := dict }}
{{- if .Values.networkPolicy.metricsNamespaceSelector }}
{{- $metricsPeer = dict "namespaceSelector" .Values.networkPolicy.metricsNamespaceSelector }}
{{- else }}
{{- $metricsPeer = dict "podSelector" dict }}
{{- end }}
{{- /* The UI pods proxy /api/ to the api pods, in-cluster only. */}}
{{- $uiProxiesToApi := and .Values.ui.enabled .Values.api.enabled .Values.ui.proxyApi (not .Values.ui.apiUpstream) }}
{{- $uiPeers := list }}
{{- if $uiProxiesToApi }}
{{- $uiPeers = list (dict "podSelector" (dict "matchLabels" (include "corvus.componentSelectorLabels" (dict "root" . "component" "ui") | fromYaml))) }}
{{- end }}
{{- /* component -> (enabled, ingress port, extra peers) */}}
{{- $components := dict
  "ingest" (dict "enabled" .Values.ingest.enabled "port" .Values.ingest.metricsPort "from" (list $metricsPeer))
  "score" (dict "enabled" .Values.score.enabled "port" .Values.score.metricsPort "from" (list $metricsPeer))
  "api" (dict "enabled" .Values.api.enabled "port" .Values.api.port "from" (concat .Values.networkPolicy.apiFrom (list $metricsPeer) $uiPeers) "open" (empty .Values.networkPolicy.apiFrom))
  "ui" (dict "enabled" .Values.ui.enabled "port" 8080 "from" .Values.networkPolicy.uiFrom "open" (empty .Values.networkPolicy.uiFrom))
  "housekeeping" (dict "enabled" .Values.housekeeping.enabled)
  "compact" (dict "enabled" .Values.compact.enabled)
  "migrate" (dict "enabled" .Values.migrate.enabled)
}}
{{- range $component, $cfg := $components }}
{{- if $cfg.enabled }}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ include "corvus.fullname" $ }}-{{ $component }}
  labels:
    {{- include "corvus.componentLabels" (dict "root" $ "component" $component) | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "corvus.componentSelectorLabels" (dict "root" $ "component" $component) | nindent 6 }}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  {{- if $cfg.port }}
  ingress:
    - ports:
        - port: {{ $cfg.port }}
          protocol: TCP
      {{- if not $cfg.open }}
      from:
        {{- toYaml $cfg.from | nindent 8 }}
      {{- end }}
  {{- else }}
  ingress: []
  {{- end }}
  egress:
    # DNS
    - ports:
        - port: 53
          protocol: UDP
        - port: 53
          protocol: TCP
    # NATS, PostgreSQL, object store, OIDC provider and (api) the Kubernetes API.
    - ports:
        {{- range $.Values.networkPolicy.egressPorts }}
        - port: {{ . }}
          protocol: TCP
        {{- end }}
    {{- if and (eq $component "ui") $uiProxiesToApi }}
    # The same-origin proxy to the api pods.
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              {{- include "corvus.componentSelectorLabels" (dict "root" $ "component" "api") | nindent 14 }}
      ports:
        - port: {{ $.Values.api.port }}
          protocol: TCP
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

`deploy/helm/corvus/templates/score.yaml`:

{{- if .Values.score.enabled }}
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: {{ include "corvus.fullname" . }}-score
  labels:
    {{- include "corvus.componentLabels" (dict "root" . "component" "score") | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  # replicas and CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS below come from the same value on purpose: replica i of n owns
  # the partitions p with p mod n == i, so the two must never differ.
  replicas: {{ .Values.score.replicas }}
  serviceName: {{ include "corvus.fullname" . }}-score
  # Every replica owns its own partitions; there is no ordering between pods.
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "corvus.componentSelectorLabels" (dict "root" . "component" "score") | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "corvus.podLabels" (dict "root" . "component" "score") | nindent 8 }}
      annotations:
        # A changed replica count changes the partition assignment of every pod.
        corvus.onelitefeather.net/score-replicas: {{ .Values.score.replicas | quote }}
        {{- with .Values.podAnnotations }}
        {{- toYaml . | nindent 8 }}
        {{- end }}
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: {{ include "corvus.serviceAccountName" (dict "root" . "component" "score") }}
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: {{ .Values.score.terminationGracePeriodSeconds }}
      {{- include "corvus.podCommon" . | nindent 6 }}
      containers:
        - name: score
          image: {{ include "corvus.image" . }}
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.image.pullPolicy }}
          command: ["corvus-score"]
          securityContext:
            {{- toYaml .Values.securityContext | nindent 12 }}
          env:
            {{- include "corvus.natsEnv" (dict "root" . "credsKey" .Values.nats.creds.scoreKey) | nindent 12 }}
            {{- include "corvus.pgEnv" . | nindent 12 }}
            {{- include "corvus.s3Env" . | nindent 12 }}
            - name: CORVUS_METRICS_PORT
              value: {{ .Values.score.metricsPort | quote }}
            - name: CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS
              value: {{ .Values.score.replicas | quote }}
            # The StatefulSet ordinal, exposed by Kubernetes as a pod label (1.28+).
            - name: CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICA_INDEX
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.labels['apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index']
            - name: CORVUS_SCORE_RAW_MAX_BUFFERED_FRAMES
              value: {{ .Values.score.rawMaxBufferedFrames | quote }}
            - name: CORVUS_SCORE_P99_BUDGET_MS

            {{- toYaml .Values.score.resources | nindent 12 }}

            {{- include "corvus.tmpMount" . | nindent 12 }}
            {{- include "corvus.natsCredsMount" . | nindent 12 }}

        {{- include "corvus.tmpVolume" . | nindent 8 }}
        {{- include "corvus.natsCredsVolume" (dict "root" . "credsKey" .Values.nats.creds.scoreKey) | nindent 8 }}
---
# Headless: stable per-pod identity and the metrics target of every replica.
apiVersion: v1

  name: {{ include "corvus.fullname" . }}-score

    {{- include "corvus.componentLabels" (dict "root" . "component" "score") | nindent 4 }}

            - name: CORVUS_UI_EXTRA_CONNECT
              value: {{ join " " . | quote }}
            {{- end }}
          ports:
            - name: http
              # Fixed by ui/docker/default.conf.template.
              containerPort: 8080
              protocol: TCP
          startupProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 15
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 20
          resources:
            {{- toYaml .Values.ui.resources | nindent 12 }}
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html/config.json
              subPath: config.json
              readOnly: true
            {{- include "corvus.tmpMount" . | nindent 12 }}
            - name: nginx-cache
              mountPath: /var/cache/nginx
            # The entrypoint renders the server block from the template into this directory.
            - name: nginx-conf
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/conf.d
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: {{ include "corvus.fullname" . }}-ui
        {{- include "corvus.tmpVolume" . | nindent 8 }}
        - name: nginx-cache
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: nginx-conf
          emptyDir:
            sizeLimit: 1Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ include "corvus.fullname" . }}-ui
  labels:
    {{- include "corvus.componentLabels" (dict "root" . "component" "ui") | nindent 4 }}

  selector:
    {{- include "corvus.componentSelectorLabels" (dict "root" . "component" "ui") | nindent 4 }}

{{- if .Values.ui.ingress.enabled }}

    {{- toYaml . | nindent 4 }}
  {{- end }}

  {{- include "corvus.ingressSpec" (dict "cfg" .Values.ui.ingress "svc" (printf "%s-ui" (include "corvus.fullname" .)) "port" .Values.ui.port) | nindent 2 }}

      - contains:
          path: spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env
          content:
            name: CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_MAX_DAYS
            value: "365"

  - it: gives the api the same two values so it validates against what housekeeping applies
    template: api.yaml
    documentSelector:
      path: kind
      value: Deployment
    asserts:
      - contains:
          path: spec.template.spec.containers[0].env
          content:
            name: CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS
            value: "21"
      - contains:
          path: spec.template.spec.containers[0].env
          content:
            name: CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_MAX_DAYS
            value: "365"

  - it: follows the configured values in both workloads
    set:
      rawRetention.defaultDays: 14
      rawRetention.maxDays: 90
    template: housekeeping.yaml
    asserts:
      - contains:
          path: spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env
          content:
            name: CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS
            value: "14"
      - contains:
          path: spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env
          content:
            name: CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_MAX_DAYS
            value: "90"

  - it: refuses a default above the maximum
    template: housekeeping.yaml
    set:
      rawRetention.defaultDays: 400
      rawRetention.maxDays: 365
    asserts:
      - failedTemplate:
          errorMessage: rawRetention.defaultDays must not exceed rawRetention.maxDays

  - it: rejects a retention below one day in the schema
    template: housekeeping.yaml
    set:
      rawRetention.defaultDays: 0
    asserts:
      - failedTemplate: {}

`deploy/helm/corvus/values.schema.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "definitions": {
    "image": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["repository"],
      "properties": {
        "repository": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1},
        "tag": {"type": "string"},
        "pullPolicy": {"enum": ["Always", "IfNotPresent", "Never"]}
      }
    },
    "pdb": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {"type": "boolean"},
        "maxUnavailable": {"type": ["integer", "string"]}

# Secrets that are referenced by name (see docs/how-to/deploy-with-helm.md for the full list).

  tag: ""

  host: ""

  name: ""

  existingSecret: corvus-s3
  accessKeyKey: access-key
  secretKeyKey: secret-key
  # Optional: name of the ConfigMap an ObjectBucketClaim creates (BUCKET_NAME, BUCKET_HOST,
  # BUCKET_PORT). The bucket name is then read from it instead of `bucket`; the endpoint too,
  # unless `endpointUrl` is set (then that wins, for example an in-cluster service URL).
  bucketConfigMap: ""

# Key encryption key (base64, 32 bytes) wrapping every player data key. Losing it makes all raw
# payloads unreadable. Needed by ingest only.

  existingSecret: corvus-kek
  key: kek
  id: kek-1

# Pseudonym key, identical to the one the proxies use (base64, at least 16 bytes). Needed by the
# api only; without it lookup and erasure by UUID answer 503.
pseudonym:
  enabled: true
  existingSecret: corvus-pseudonym
  key: key
  keyId: k1

# Retention of raw payloads (NFR-018). The same two values reach housekeeping, which applies them,
# and the api, which validates a pool's `raw_retention_days` against `maxDays`. A pool without its
# own value keeps raw payloads for `defaultDays`; housekeeping also deletes the raw-derived feature
# artefacts of a snapshot once the retention of its pool has passed.
rawRetention:

  maxDays: 365

# Online scoring. A StatefulSet: replica i of n owns the partitions p with p mod n == i, so the
# pod ordinal is the replica index and CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS must equal the replica count. Scale by
# changing `score.replicas` only (never with kubectl scale or an HPA); the value feeds both.
score:
  enabled: true
  replicas: 2
  metricsPort: 9464
  # Raw-byte models (ADR-CORV-0008). The scorer tokenizes plaintext frames on arrival and buffers
  # token ids for about one window per session, segment and windowing (roughly 0.3 KiB per frame,
  # so a 10 s window at 300 frames/s is about 1 MiB per session): size `resources.limits.memory`
  # for the concurrent players and lower CORVUS_SCORE_SESSIONS_MAX (via `env`) if needed.
  # Frames buffered per session, segment and windowing at most; the oldest are dropped and counted.
  rawMaxBufferedFrames: 16384
  # p99 budget in ms of one raw-byte window. A model whose max_packets is estimated to exceed it is
  # still served but logs a warning at load time. 0 disables the check. Keep it in line with the
  # registry gate (CORVUS_GATE_MAX_P99_LATENCY_MS of the api).
  p99BudgetMs: 10
  env: {}
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: "1", memory: 512Mi}
    limits: {cpu: "4", memory: 1Gi}
  podDisruptionBudget:
    enabled: true
    maxUnavailable: 1
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60

  backoffLimit: 1
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3

  batchRows: 65536
  # Erasure requests younger than this are left alone so late frames of the player have landed.
  graceSeconds: 600
  env: {}

    enabled: false

# in front of two Paper backends. See docs/pilot.md.
#
# Requires: deploy/pilot/.env (copy .env.example) and the plugin jar built with
#   ./gradlew :plugin:shadowJar

name: corvus-pilot

x-paper: &paper
  image: itzg/minecraft-server:2026.10.0-java25
  restart: "no"
  # Keep the stack from hogging the developer machine.
  cpus: 1.5
  mem_limit: 2g
  pids_limit: 512
  environment: &paper-env
    EULA: ${EULA:-FALSE}
    TYPE: PAPER
    VERSION: "26.2"
    PAPER_BUILD: "134"
    # Authentication happens on the proxy; backends trust modern forwarding.
    ONLINE_MODE: "FALSE"
    ENABLE_RCON: "FALSE"
    MEMORY: 1536M
    VIEW_DISTANCE: "6"
    SIMULATION_DISTANCE: "4"
    REPLACE_ENV_DURING_SYNC: "true"
    SYNC_SKIP_NEWER_IN_DESTINATION: "false"
    CFG_VELOCITY_FORWARDING_SECRET: ${VELOCITY_FORWARDING_SECRET:?set VELOCITY_FORWARDING_SECRET in .env}
  volumes:
    - ./paper/paper-global.yml:/config/config/paper-global.yml:ro

services:
  stage-corvus:
    # One-shot: copies exactly one corvus-velocity-*.jar (no -sources/-plain/-javadoc)
    # into a volume that the proxy mounts as /plugins, and makes the capture directory
    # writable for the proxy user (a bind mount that Docker creates would belong to root).
    image: alpine:3.22
    restart: "no"
    cpus: 0.25
    mem_limit: 64m
    volumes:
      - ../../plugin/build/libs:/src:ro
      - corvus-plugin:/dst
      - ./data/captures:/captures
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -eu
        # 1000:1000 is the default user of the itzg images
        chown 1000:1000 /captures
        rm -f /dst/*.jar
        n=0
        for f in /src/corvus-velocity-*.jar; do
          [ -e "$$f" ] || break
          case "$$f" in *-sources.jar|*-plain.jar|*-javadoc.jar) continue ;; esac
          cp "$$f" /dst/
          n=$$((n + 1))
        done
        if [ "$$n" -ne 1 ]; then
          echo "expected exactly one corvus-velocity-*.jar in plugin/build/libs, found $$n; run ./gradlew :plugin:shadowJar" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "staged corvus plugin jar"

  proxy:
    image: itzg/mc-proxy:2026.10.0-java25
    restart: "no"
    cpus: 1.0
    mem_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 512
    depends_on:
      stage-corvus:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      lobby:
        condition: service_healthy
      pvp:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      TYPE: VELOCITY
      VELOCITY_VERSION: 4.2.0
      VELOCITY_BUILD_ID: "30"
      MEMORY: 512M
      # Pinned, immutable Modrinth CDN URLs (version id is part of the path).
      # PacketEvents 2.14.0 (sha256 0772f64b51aaf79132c76bb1503707ea0d35433713d5312e67401eaa599d271b), ViaVersion 5.12.1, ViaBackwards 5.12.1; see docs/pilot.md.
      PLUGINS: "https://github.com/retrooper/packetevents/releases/download/v2.14.0/packetevents-velocity-2.14.0.jar,https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/P1OZGk5p/versions/5WgnasGG/ViaVersion-5.12.1.jar,https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/NpvuJQoq/versions/dWw67APC/ViaBackwards-5.12.1.jar"
      VELOCITY_FORWARDING_SECRET: ${VELOCITY_FORWARDING_SECRET:?set VELOCITY_FORWARDING_SECRET in .env}
      CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY: ${CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY:?set CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY in .env}
    ports:
      - "${PROXY_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${PROXY_PORT:-25565}:25577"
    volumes:
      - proxy-server:/server
      - corvus-plugin:/plugins:ro
      - ./proxy/velocity.toml:/config/velocity.toml:ro
      # Velocity's data directory for the plugin id "corvus" is plugins/corvus. The plugin reads
      # config.toml there and writes captures/<yyyy-MM-dd>/<session-id>.cvc below it.
      - ./proxy/corvus-config.toml:/server/plugins/corvus/config.toml:ro
      - ./data/captures:/server/plugins/corvus/captures

  lobby:
    <<: *paper
    environment:
      <<: *paper-env
      PVP: "false"
    volumes:
      - lobby-data:/data
      - ./paper/paper-global.yml:/config/config/paper-global.yml:ro

  pvp:
    <<: *paper
    environment:
      <<: *paper-env
      PVP: "true"
    volumes:
      - pvp-data:/data
      - ./paper/paper-global.yml:/config/config/paper-global.yml:ro

volumes:
  corvus-plugin:
  proxy-server:
  lobby-data:
  pvp-data:

```

`deploy/pilot/proxy/corvus-config.toml`:

```toml
# Corvus plugin configuration for the pilot. Mounted read-only as plugins/corvus/config.toml.
# Key names follow CorvusConfig.DEFAULT_TOML of the plugin (CorvusConfigTest guards this file).
# Captures are written to plugins/corvus/captures (mounted from deploy/pilot/data/captures).

proxy_id = "pilot-proxy"

[pseudonym]
# The base64 HMAC key comes from the CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY environment variable (set in .env).
# Without it the plugin loads but captures nothing.
key_file = ""
key_id = "pilot-1"

[players]
mode = "all"
allowlist = []
blocklist = []

[capture]
# Privacy: "serverbound" records payload bytes of serverbound play packets (minus text-bearing types
# such as signs, books, anvil names, plugin messages) and of a few clientbound motion packets.
# Clientbound payloads would contain names and UUIDs of other players and are not kept.
# Use "none" to record no payload bytes at all. "all" is for local debugging only.
raw_payloads = "serverbound"
max_payload_bytes = 2048
queue_max_bytes = 67108864
batch_size = 200
flush_interval_seconds = 5

[sink]
# "file" (pilot): captures are written to plugins/corvus/captures.
# "nats": publish every envelope to NATS JetStream instead (contract: docs/reference/data-lake.md, section 1).
# The stream CORVUS_CAPTURE (subjects corvus.capture.v1.>) must already exist; the plugin never creates it.
# To switch, set type = "nats" and add a [nats] table with these keys (all optional):
#   [nats]
#   url = ["nats://nats.example:4222"]      # required for type = "nats": one URL or a list
#   creds_file = "/path/to/corvus.creds"    # empty = no authentication
#   subject_prefix = "corvus.capture.v1"    # published to <subject_prefix>.<proxy_id>.<partition>
#   partitions = 16                         # partition = first 4 bytes of session id (big-endian) mod this,
#                                           # two digits (00..15); identical on all proxies and the scorers
#   max_in_flight_bytes = 33554432          # unacknowledged bytes; beyond this batches are dropped
#   publish_timeout_seconds = 5             # no ack after this long = failed, counted as dropped_transport
#   reconnect_buffer_bytes = 8388608        # bytes buffered while reconnecting
type = "file"

[scores]
# Online scores for other plugins (corvus-api, docs/reference/plugin-api.md). Off here because the pilot uses the
# file sink. With sink.type = "nats" this defaults to on and subscribes to corvus.score.v1.> (core NATS, needs the
# [nats] url and the pseudonym key). To enable it without the nats sink, uncomment:
#   enabled = true
# Scores are decision aids; only ENFORCE scores are meant for automated actions, Corvus never sanctions players.
subject = "corvus.score.v1.>"
listener_threads = 2
listener_queue = 1024

[blocklist_sync]
# Periodically fetch the blocklist of the control plane (GET <url>/api/v1/plugin/blocklist, proxy API token from
# CORVUS_API_PLUGIN_TOKENS) and never capture the listed pseudonyms; players blocked while online lose their
# session. The token is read from CORVUS_PLUGIN_API_TOKEN or token_file (relative to plugins/corvus). A failed
# sync keeps the last good list. Off in the pilot, which runs without the control plane.
enabled = false
url = ""
token_file = ""
interval_seconds = 300
timeout_seconds = 10

[tls]
# Extra PEM CA bundle (e.g. a private step-ca) trusted in addition to the JVM default CAs for NATS (tls://, wss://)
# and blocklist_sync (https://); relative to plugins/corvus or absolute. Empty = JVM default only. The pilot does
# not need it. An unreadable file stops the NATS sink, scores and blocklist sync (ERROR in the log).
ca_file = ""

[game_context]
default = "unknown"
# CloudNet services are named <Task>-<n> (Lobby-1, Team-Build-2). Lookup: exact server name, then the name without
# one trailing "-<digits>" (Lobby-2 -> lobby), then default; case-insensitive. false = exact names only.
strip_instance_suffix = true

# server name (see velocity.toml) or CloudNet task name = game context tag
[game_context.servers]
lobby = "lobby"
pvp = "pvp"

```

`docs/how-to/deploy-with-helm.md`:

```md
# How to deploy Corvus with Helm

Deploys the Corvus backend to Kubernetes with the chart in `deploy/helm/corvus`. NATS JetStream, PostgreSQL and an S3
bucket are external dependencies: the chart does not install them, it only references them through values and
existing Secrets.

| Component | Kind | Image command |
|---|---|---|
| migrate | Job, Helm `pre-install,pre-upgrade` hook | `corvus-migrate` |
| ingest | Deployment (+ optional HPA), metrics Service | `corvus-ingest` |
| api | Deployment, Service, optional Ingress, RBAC for jobs | `corvus-api` |
| score | StatefulSet, headless Service | `corvus-score` |
| housekeeping | CronJob (`concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`) | `corvus-housekeeping` |
| compact | CronJob (hourly, `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, toggle `compact.enabled`) | `corvus-compact` |
| ui | optional Deployment, Service, Ingress, `config.json` ConfigMap | static nginx image |

## Images and versions

Release-please keeps `version` and `appVersion` in `Chart.yaml` equal to the release version, and the release workflow
publishes `harbor.onelitefeather.dev/onelitefeather/corvus-services` and `.../corvus-ui` with that same version as the
tag (without a leading `v`). The chart defaults every image tag to `appVersion`, so a chart release always deploys the
images of the same release. Override `image.tag` / `uiImage.tag` to pin something else.

## Prerequisites

- Kubernetes 1.28 or newer (the score StatefulSet reads its ordinal from the `apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index` label).
- A JetStream-enabled NATS, PostgreSQL (CloudNativePG works out of the box) and an S3 bucket.
- The Secrets below, created in the release namespace before the first install (the migrate hook runs first).

## Secrets

The chart never contains secret values. Create these Secrets yourself (for example with the External Secrets
Operator or SealedSecrets) and point the values at them:

| Value | Default Secret / key | Content | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `database.existingSecret`, `database.dsnKey` | `corvus-database` / `uri` | libpq DSN incl. password (the CNPG app secret key `uri` fits) | migrate, ingest, api, score, housekeeping, compact |
| `s3.existingSecret`, `s3.accessKeyKey`, `s3.secretKeyKey` | `corvus-s3` / `access-key`, `secret-key` | object store credentials | ingest, score, housekeeping, compact |
| `kek.existingSecret`, `kek.key` | `corvus-kek` / `kek` | key encryption key, base64 of 32 random bytes (`openssl rand -base64 32`) | ingest |
| `pseudonym.existingSecret`, `pseudonym.key` | `corvus-pseudonym` / `key` | pseudonym key shared with the proxies, base64, at least 16 bytes | api (`pseudonym.enabled: false` disables it) |
| `api.extraSecret` (optional) | none | every key becomes an env var, e.g. `CORVUS_API_PLUGIN_TOKENS` (comma separated proxy tokens) | api |
| `api.jobs.envSecret` (optional) | none | S3 / database credentials exposed to training job pods | jobs started by the api |

Raw payload retention is not a secret: `rawRetention.defaultDays` (21) and `rawRetention.maxDays` (365) reach
housekeeping, which applies them, and the api, which validates a pool's `raw_retention_days` against them
(`CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS`, `CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_MAX_DAYS`). The default must not exceed the maximum.

**Database, object store and NATS variants.**

- *CloudNativePG with separate keys:* set `database.host` (for example `corvus-db-rw`), `database.name`,
  `database.port` and `database.passwordKey` (plus `database.userKey`, or a plain `database.user`). The password is
  read from `database.existingSecret` and reaches psycopg as `PGPASSWORD` (user and host as `PGUSER` and `PGHOST`);
  `database.dsnKey` is then ignored.
- *Rook-Ceph ObjectBucketClaim:* the claim's Secret uses the keys `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, so set
  `s3.existingSecret`, `s3.accessKeyKey: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `s3.secretKeyKey: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. Its ConfigMap
  (`BUCKET_NAME`, `BUCKET_HOST`, `BUCKET_PORT`) can replace `s3.bucket` and the endpoint: set `s3.bucketConfigMap` to its
  name. `s3.endpointUrl` still wins when set (for example an in-cluster service URL).
- *NATS:* `nats.streamReplicas` (default 1; 3 on a three-node cluster) sets the replicas of the JetStream stream, and an
  existing stream with fewer replicas is updated. `nats.creds.existingSecret` holds one `.creds` file per component
  (`nats.creds.ingestKey`, `nats.creds.scoreKey`, because ingest and score are different NATS users); each pod mounts only
  its own key read-only and gets `CORVUS_NATS_CREDS_FILE`. This needs a services image that supports those settings.

Losing the KEK makes every stored player key, and with it all raw payloads, unreadable. Back it up.

## Install

```sh
helm upgrade --install corvus deploy/helm/corvus -n corvus --create-namespace -f my-values.yaml
```

A minimal `my-values.yaml`:

```yaml
nats:
  url: nats://nats.nats.svc:4222
s3:
  endpointUrl: http://rook-ceph-rgw.rook-ceph.svc:80
  bucket: corvus-lake
api:
  oidc:
    issuer: https://idp.example.org/realms/olf
    audience: corvus
    jwksUrl: https://idp.example.org/realms/olf/protocol/openid-connect/certs
    rolesClaim: realm_access.roles
  ingress:
    enabled: true
    className: nginx
    hosts:
      - host: corvus-api.example.org
        paths:
          - path: /
```

The `values.schema.json` rejects unknown top-level keys and wrong types, and the hardened defaults cannot be switched
off (non-root, read-only root filesystem, no capabilities, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp). `/tmp` is a per-pod emptyDir.

## Scaling

- **ingest** scales horizontally: raise `ingest.replicas` or enable `ingest.autoscaling`. Defaults are 1 to 4 CPUs and
  at most 1 GiB per pod.
- **score** is a StatefulSet. Replica `i` of `n` owns the partitions `p` with `p mod n == i`, so the chart sets
  `CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS` from `score.replicas` (the same value that sets the StatefulSet replicas) and
  `CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICA_INDEX` from the pod ordinal. Change the count only through `score.replicas`; never use
  `kubectl scale` or an HPA, because the two values would drift and partitions would be dropped or scored twice.
- **api** training jobs: with `api.jobs.runner: kubernetes` (default) the chart creates a Role that allows
  `create`, `get`, `list` and `watch` on `batch/jobs` in the release namespace and binds it to the api ServiceAccount;
  that is the only component whose pod mounts a ServiceAccount token. Set `api.jobs.image` to the ML image.

## Optional parts

- `ui.enabled: true` deploys the UI. `ui.config` is rendered as `/usr/share/nginx/html/config.json` and uses the keys
  the UI reads (`apiBaseUrl`, `auth.mode`, `auth.rolesClaim`, `auth.roleMapping`, `oidc.issuer`, `oidc.clientId`,
  `oidc.scopes`, see [run-the-ui.md](run-the-ui.md)); the schema rejects other keys. `basePath` comes from
  `ui.basePath`, which also sets `CORVUS_UI_BASE_PATH`. The container always listens on 8080 (`ui.port` is only the
  Service port) and runs as uid 101 (`ui.podSecurityContext`), the user of the nginx-unprivileged image.
  - **Same origin (default).** `ui.proxyApi: true` makes nginx proxy `/api/` to the in-cluster api Service
    (`CORVUS_UI_API_UPSTREAM`), so `ui.config.apiBaseUrl: /api/v1` needs neither CORS nor an extra CSP entry. With
    `networkPolicy.enabled` the chart lets the UI pods reach the api pods. Set `ui.apiUpstream` to proxy elsewhere.
  - **Separate origin.** Put the absolute URL into `ui.config.apiBaseUrl`, set `ui.proxyApi: false` and list the UI's
    origin in `api.cors.origins` (`CORVUS_API_CORS_ORIGINS`). The origins for the Content-Security-Policy are derived
    from `apiBaseUrl` and `oidc.issuer`; override them with `ui.apiOrigin`, `ui.oidcOrigin` and `ui.extraConnect`.
- `api.jobTokens.existingSecret` (key `api.jobTokens.key`, default `job-tokens`) provides `CORVUS_API_JOB_TOKENS`, the
  comma separated `<sha256 hex of the token>:<job name>` entries of the ML jobs (see
  [control-plane-api.md](../reference/control-plane-api.md)). The jobs themselves need `CORVUS_API_URL` and the plain
  `CORVUS_API_TOKEN`: put both into the Secret named by `api.jobs.envSecret`.
- `networkPolicy.enabled: true` restricts every component to DNS plus the ports in `networkPolicy.egressPorts`
  (NATS 4222, PostgreSQL 5432, HTTP(S), Kubernetes API) and to ingress on its own port.
- `serviceMonitor.enabled: true` creates Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitors for ingest, score and api.

## Deploy with Flux

When the chart is installed from a Git branch, set `reconcileStrategy: Revision` on the chart source. The default,
`ChartVersion`, only produces a new chart artifact when `Chart.yaml`'s version changes, so changes to templates or
values on the branch would silently never be redeployed.

```yaml
apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: corvus
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 5m
  url: https://github.com/OneLiteFeatherNET/Corvus
  ref:
    branch: main
---
apiVersion: helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2
kind: HelmRelease
metadata:
  name: corvus
  namespace: corvus
spec:
  interval: 10m
  chart:
    spec:
      chart: ./deploy/helm/corvus
      reconcileStrategy: Revision
      sourceRef:
        kind: GitRepository
        name: corvus
        namespace: flux-system
  install:
    remediation:
      retries: 3
  upgrade:
    remediation:
      retries: 3
  values:
    nats:
      url: nats://nats.nats.svc:4222
    s3:
      endpointUrl: http://rook-ceph-rgw.rook-ceph.svc:80
```

Because the chart tracks `main`, `appVersion` (and with it the default image tag) only moves when a release is cut.
Merging a change to the chart without a release redeploys the new templates with the previous images.

## Check the result

```sh
kubectl -n corvus get pods
kubectl -n corvus logs job/corvus-migrate        # only while the hook Job still exists
kubectl -n corvus port-forward svc/corvus-api 8080 &
curl -s localhost:8080/readyz
```

helm unittest deploy/helm/corvus     # needs the helm-unittest plugin
```

`docs/how-to/evaluate-models.md`:

```md
# How to evaluate models with `corvus-eval`

Run the stage 3 harness against feature windows and labels, and read the report. The code is in
`ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/`.

```
cd ml
uv run corvus-eval run --config eval.toml --out reports/<name>
```

The output directory gets `report.json`, `report.md` and `onnx/<game_context>/<candidate>.onnx`
with `<candidate>.calibration.json` and `<candidate>.raw.onnx` (the graph without the calibration;
torch models also get `.int8.onnx`). `ml/eval.synthetic.toml` is a ready-to-run smoke config.

The control plane runs the same harness as the `evaluate` and `train` jobs; see
[ml-jobs.md](../reference/ml-jobs.md). Models on raw packet bytes (`raw_hier_classifier`,
`raw_hier_anomaly`) and the Optuna search (`corvus-eval tune`) are covered in sections 6 and 7.

## 1. Inputs

| Table | Source | Needed columns |
|---|---|---|
| `windows` | `corvus-features build` | see [features.md](../reference/features.md) section 3 |
| `window_tokens` | `corvus-features build` | only for sequence candidates (`gru_autoencoder`, `cnn1d`) |
| `sessions` | catalog export (Parquet or CSV) | `session_id`, `pseudonym`, optional `started_at` |
| `labels` | honeypot runs, staff verdicts (Parquet or CSV) | `pseudonym` or `session_id`, `label`, `source`, `confidence`, `valid_from`, `valid_to` |

In CSV files ids are hex strings and times are ISO 8601. Empty `valid_from` / `valid_to` mean an
open bound. A label row sets exactly one of `pseudonym` and `session_id`; `label` is `legit` or
`cheat`.

**Label join.** A label applies to a window when the window start
(`sessions.started_at + windows.start_offset_nanos`) lies in `[valid_from, valid_to)`. Without
`started_at` only labels with no bounds apply. If several labels match, the highest `confidence`
wins; on a tie `cheat` wins. Rows below `run.min_confidence` are ignored. Windows without a valid
label stay unlabelled. Windows whose session has no pseudonym are dropped and logged.

**Unlabelled windows.** With `run.unlabelled = "exclude"` (default) they are neither trained on
nor scored. With `"assume_legit"` they count as legit everywhere (training and evaluation) and
the report states how many were assumed. Use it only when you accept that unlabelled traffic is
overwhelmingly legit; it biases recall at low FPR optimistically if cheaters hide in there.

**Split.** Players (pseudonyms) are split into train / val / test, never windows. The split is
stratified by player label (cheat, legit, unlabelled), shuffled with `run.seed`, and asserted to
have no player in two parts. The pipeline runs once per `game_context`, with its own split.

## 2. Config reference (`eval.toml`)

```toml
name = "pilot-2026-10"

[run]
seed = 1337              # numpy, torch, sklearn and the split
threads = 1              # torch.set_num_threads and ONNX Runtime intra-op threads
seq_len = 256            # frames per window fed to sequence models (longer: cut, shorter: padded)
unlabelled = "exclude"   # or "assume_legit"
calibration = "auto"     # auto | isotonic | platt | ecdf | none, see "Calibration" below
contexts = []            # empty = every game_context in the data
split = [0.6, 0.2, 0.2]  # train / val / test share of players
fpr_targets = [0.01, 0.001]
min_confidence = 0.0
learning_curve = [0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0]  # empty list disables it

[data]                   # paths relative to this file; or use [synthetic] instead
windows = "lake/windows"
tokens = "lake/window_tokens"
sessions = "catalog/sessions.parquet"
labels = "labels.csv"

[candidates.isolation_forest]    # one table per candidate; keys are that candidate's parameters
n_estimators = 200
[candidates.gradient_boosting]
max_iter = 200
learning_rate = 0.1
[candidates.gru_autoencoder]
epochs = 30
batch_size = 64
lr = "auto"              # or a number; "auto" runs the LR range test and uses its suggestion
hidden = 64
latent = 32
patience = 5
[candidates.cnn1d]
epochs = 30
batch_size = 64
lr = 0.002
channels = 32

[benchmark]
enabled = true
warmup = 20
iters = 200              # single-window timings behind p50 / p99
batch = 64               # batch for the throughput number
isolated = true          # one fresh process per model so peak RSS is that model's own
quantize = true          # int8 dynamic quantisation variant of the torch models
```

Unknown keys are errors. Candidate names: `isolation_forest`, `gradient_boosting`,
`gru_autoencoder`, `cnn1d`, and the raw-byte models `raw_hier_classifier` and `raw_hier_anomaly`
(section 6; they need a `[raw]` table and cannot share a run with the others).

Candidates train on different subsets: supervised ones (`gradient_boosting`, `cnn1d`) on labelled
windows and are skipped when the training split lacks one of the classes; unsupervised ones
(`isolation_forest`, `gru_autoencoder`) on windows that are legit (or assumed legit). Early
stopping uses the validation split. Scores are "higher = more likely cheat".

### Calibration

Every exported graph outputs a score in [0, 1], not the raw model output. The calibration is fitted
on the **validation** split and embedded in the ONNX graph, which then has one output named
`score`:

| Candidate | Method (`auto`) | Meaning of the score |
|---|---|---|
| supervised (`gradient_boosting`, `cnn1d`) | isotonic regression with at least 20 windows per class and 200 in total, else Platt scaling | estimated P(cheating, window) |
| unsupervised (`isolation_forest`, `gru_autoencoder`) | empirical CDF of the raw score of the legit (or assumed legit) validation windows | share of legit windows that score lower: 0.99 is higher than 99 % of legit windows |

The map is monotone, so it never reorders windows; isotonic regression and the CDF can merge
neighbouring raw values into ties. All metrics in the report (including ECE and the confusion
matrices) are computed on the calibrated score, the thing that is deployed. `none` exports the
raw graph (benchmark use only; the jobs refuse it). Without legit validation windows an
unsupervised candidate is calibrated on its training windows (`fit_on: "train"` in the report).
The calibration, its method and the number of windows it was fitted on are in
`<candidate>.calibration.json` and the `calibration` entry of the candidate in `report.json`.

## 3. Reading the report

Per `game_context` one table row per candidate, all on the **test** split:

- `ROC-AUC`, `PR-AUC` (average precision), per window.
- `R@1%`, `R@0.1%`: recall at a false-positive rate of 1 % / 0.1 %, per window (`win`) and per
  player (`player`, max window score per player; a player is a cheater if any window is). A `*`
  marks an operating point that the test split cannot resolve (fewer than 1 / FPR legit windows
  or players). Do not trust those cells beyond "upper bound".
- `ECE`: expected calibration error, 10 equal-width bins, supervised candidates only (the
  unsupervised scores are percentiles of the legit distribution, not probabilities).
- `p50 ms`, `p99 ms`: single-window ONNX Runtime CPU latency at the configured thread count; the
  target is under 10 ms p99. `batch w/s`: throughput at the batch size. `RSS MB`: peak resident
  set of the benchmark process (`model RSS delta` in the JSON is the growth caused by the model).
- `ONNX diff`: maximum absolute difference between ONNX and native (calibrated) scores on the test
  windows; `parity_ok` in the JSON applies `rtol=1e-3, atol=2e-3` (the calibration interpolates in
  float32 next to steep steps). The raw graph is checked separately (`onnx_raw`).

Further sections: the int8 variant (metric deltas against fp32, latency, file size), the confusion
matrix on test at the threshold that gives the target FPR **on validation**, and the learning
curve (metrics against the share of training players). A curve that is still rising at 100 % says
more data would help; use it to estimate how much labelled data is needed.

Latency and RSS depend on the host, load and thread count. Compare numbers only from the same
machine and config.

## 4. Synthetic data

`corvus_ml.eval.synthetic` generates windows, tokens, sessions and labels in the real schemas,
for tests and smoke runs. Put a `[synthetic]` table in the config instead of `[data]`
(`n_legit`, `n_cheat`, `n_unlabelled`, `sessions_per_player`, `windows_per_session`,
`frames_per_window`, `contexts`, `cheat_strength`, `cheat_window_frac`). The generator models
toy "human" and "cheat" input (Gaussian rotation noise with per-player sensitivity versus aim snaps,
steady packet cadence and click rhythm). **Its results prove the code runs; they say nothing about
real players**, and reports made from it carry a banner saying so.

## 5. Adding a candidate

Subclass `corvus_ml.eval.candidates.base.Candidate`, set `name`, `supervised`, `input_kind`
(`"agg"`, `"seq"` or `"raw_bytes"`), implement `fit`, `score`, `export_onnx`, `n_params` (and `onnx_to_score` if
the graph does not output the score first), decorate with `@register`, and import the module in
`candidates/__init__.py`. Config, split, metrics, ONNX parity, benchmark and report pick it up.

Optional class attributes: `tunable = True` makes the candidate searchable by `corvus-eval tune`
(its `fit` must pass `self.on_epoch` to the training loop and `corvus_ml.eval.tune.DEFAULT_SPACES` needs
an entry), `pretrains = True` hands `fit` the unlabelled windows of the training players as `pool`, and
`parity_rows` limits the number of test windows used for the ONNX parity check.

## 6. Raw-byte models

`raw_hier_classifier` (supervised) and `raw_hier_anomaly` (self-supervised, masked-prediction score)
read tokenised raw packet bytes instead of windows and token features; the format and the model are in
[raw-byte-tokenizer.md](../reference/raw-byte-tokenizer.md). A run uses either these candidates or the
others, because they cut their own time windows:

```toml
[raw]
dir = "lake/raw"          # features/<snapshot>/raw as built by build_features kind=raw_bytes
# or: [raw.synthetic] (below)
window_seconds = 10.0     # any window key overrides what the build recorded
stride_seconds = 5.0
max_packets = 1024
overflow = "recent"       # or "uniform"
min_packets = 8
# macro_window_seconds = 60.0   # second-level model over consecutive windows (stride == window)
max_windows = 100000      # random cap on the number of windows (memory)

[raw.tokenizer]           # only for [raw.synthetic]: the tokenizer is trained on the synthetic packets
vocab_size = 1024
[raw.packet]
max_tokens_per_packet = 48

[candidates.raw_hier_classifier]
epochs = 10
lr = "auto"
d_model = 64
layers = 2
pretrain_epochs = 5       # masked pretraining on all windows of the training players first
# init_from = "pretrain/pvp.pt"   # or start from a checkpoint (corvus-eval pretrain)
[candidates.raw_hier_anomaly]
epochs = 10

[benchmark]
raw_packets = [128, 512, 1024]    # extra single-window latency table at these packet counts
```

Without `[raw]` the labels come from `[data] labels`; with `dir` the build's `sessions.parquet`
(`session_id`, `pseudonym`, `started_at`, `client_protocol`) and `labels.parquet` are used. The report
states the tokenizer hash and the window configuration. Each exported model directory
(`onnx/<context>/`) holds `feature_spec.json` (version 2, `raw_bytes` section) and `tokenizer.json`
next to the graphs.

Pretraining on its own: `uv run corvus-eval pretrain --config eval.toml --out reports/pre` writes
`reports/pre/pretrain/<game_context>.pt`; finetune with `init_from`. The model shape comes from the
parameters of the first candidate in the config.

`ml/eval.synthetic-raw.toml` is a smoke config on synthetic packets with plausible movement layouts
(protocol differences, three cheat variants). Like every synthetic run it proves the code runs and says
nothing about real players. The anomaly model in particular does not separate the toy cheaters, which
are more regular than the toy legit players; a reconstruction loss does not see regularity.

## 7. Hyper-parameter search (`corvus-eval tune`)

```
uv run corvus-eval tune --config eval.toml --out reports/tuned [--trials 30]
```

For every game context and every tunable candidate (the raw-byte models, `gru_autoencoder`, `cnn1d`) an
Optuna study searches learning rate, weight decay and the size parameters (for the raw-byte models also
`d_model`, `layers`, `dropout`, `window_seconds` and `max_packets`) with a TPE sampler and a median pruner
and the seed `run.seed`. The objective is the best validation loss, so the search never sees the test
split. The candidate is then evaluated with the best parameters; the report gets a "Hyper-parameter
search" section with every trial, and `report.json` the same under `contexts.<ctx>.tune`.

```toml
[tune]
trials = 20               # trials per study
timeout_s = 600           # optional
storage = ""              # "" = CORVUS_OPTUNA_STORAGE, else sqlite file <out>/tune/optuna.db; or "memory", or a URL
tune_windows = true       # raw-byte models: also search the window (rebuilds the windows per trial)
[tune.space]              # optional: narrow or replace a range
lr = [0.0005, 0.005]      # [low, high] keeps the kind (log / int / float) of the default
d_model = [32, 64]        # any other list is a set of choices
```

Set small `epochs` in the candidate tables while searching; each trial is a full fit. With a persistent
storage an existing study is resumed until it holds `trials` trials. In a job, pass `"tune": true` or the
object above as a parameter of `evaluate` / `train` ([ml-jobs.md](../reference/ml-jobs.md); the API has no
separate job type).

```

# How to run the ingest service locally

Runs NATS JetStream, an S3-compatible object store (RustFS), PostgreSQL and the ingest service with Docker Compose. The contract the service
implements is in [data-lake.md](../reference/data-lake.md).

1. Create the environment file and fill in the secrets (the file explains how to generate each value):

   ```sh
   cd deploy/dev
   cp .env.example .env
   ```

2. Start the stack. `migrate` applies the catalog migrations once, `s3-init` creates the bucket, then `ingest` starts:

   ```sh
   docker compose up --build
   ```

3. Check that the service is ready and exporting metrics:

   ```sh
   curl -s localhost:9464/healthz
   curl -s localhost:9464/metrics | grep corvus_ingest
   ```

4. Point the capture plugin at `nats://localhost:4222`. Parquet files appear in the `corvus-lake` bucket (RustFS console:
   <http://localhost:9001>) under `lake/events/` and `lake/raw/`; the catalog is in the `corvus` schema of the
   PostgreSQL database (`localhost:5432`, user `corvus`).

Clean up housekeeping candidates once with:

```sh
docker compose run --rm ingest corvus-housekeeping
```

## Run the control-plane API locally

The `api` service of the same stack serves the management API on <http://localhost:8080> (reference:
[control-plane-api.md](../reference/control-plane-api.md)). It starts after `migrate`, which also creates its tables.

1. Create its environment file. It is read by the `api` service only and is optional for the other services:

   ```sh
   cd deploy/dev
   cp .env.api.example .env.api
   ```

2. For a quick local try-out set a development token in `.env.api` (never do this on a shared host), for example with
   `openssl rand -hex 24`. For anything else configure the OIDC issuer, audience and JWKS URL instead. Set
   `CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY` (the key the proxies use) if you want player lookup and erasure by UUID.

   ```sh
   CORVUS_API_DEV_TOKEN=<generated value>
   ```

3. Start the service and call it:

   ```sh
   docker compose up --build api
   curl -s localhost:8080/readyz
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CORVUS_API_DEV_TOKEN" localhost:8080/api/v1/pools
   ```

   The interactive OpenAPI documentation is at <http://localhost:8080/docs>. Without the `docker compose` stack, run
   `uv run corvus-api` in `services/` with `CORVUS_PG_DSN` set; jobs then start local subprocesses
   (`CORVUS_API_JOB_RUNNER=local`).

`docs/how-to/run-scoring-locally.md`:

```md
# How to run the scoring service locally

Runs `corvus-score` next to the dev stack of [run-ingest-locally.md](run-ingest-locally.md). The service consumes the
capture stream, featurizes the sessions with the same code as the offline build, scores the windows with the ONNX
models of the model registry and writes the scores to PostgreSQL (`shadow`, `canary`, `enforce`) and to the
`CORVUS_SCORE` stream (`canary`, `enforce` only). The contract is section 6 of
[data-lake.md](../reference/data-lake.md).

Prerequisites: the dev stack from the ingest how-to (`deploy/dev/.env` filled in) and at least one registered model in
a scored stage whose files are in the bucket: `<onnx_key>` (the ONNX file) and `feature_spec.json` in the same
directory, as the evaluation export writes them (see [evaluate-models.md](evaluate-models.md)).

1. Start the stack including the scorer. `migrate` creates the score tables (`0003_scores.sql`):

   ```sh
   cd deploy/dev
   docker compose up --build nats s3 s3-init postgres migrate ingest score
   ```

   The `score` service runs one replica that owns all 16 partitions (`CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS=1`).

2. Put a model into a scored stage with the control-plane API (role `data_scientist`; see
   [control-plane-api.md](../reference/control-plane-api.md)):

   ```sh
   curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"stage": "shadow", "reason": "local try-out"}' localhost:8080/api/v1/models/<id>/stage
   ```

   The scorer picks it up within `CORVUS_SCORE_REGISTRY_POLL_S` (30 s). A model whose `feature_spec.json` does not
   match the running code is not loaded; see `corvus_score_model_load_failures_total` and the error log.

3. Check readiness and metrics (the scorer uses host port 9465 so it does not clash with ingest):

   ```sh
   curl -s localhost:9465/healthz        # nats, postgres, registry
   curl -s localhost:9465/metrics | grep corvus_score
   ```

4. Point the capture plugin at `nats://localhost:4222`. Once players play, read the scores through the API
   (role `staff`, the pseudonym is the 64-hex form) or directly:

   ```sh
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" localhost:8080/api/v1/scores/players/<pseudonym>
   docker compose exec postgres psql -U corvus -c 'SELECT * FROM corvus.scores_latest'
   ```

   Published scores are on `corvus.score.v1.<game_context>` in the `CORVUS_SCORE` stream, for example
   `nats sub 'corvus.score.v1.>'`.

## Several replicas

Replica `i` of `n` owns the partitions `p` with `p mod n == i`. Give every replica `CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS=n` and its
own `CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICA_INDEX=i` (or a hostname ending in `-<i>`). The durable consumer `corvus-score-<i>` is
created, or its filters updated, at startup. Changing `n` or `CORVUS_CAPTURE_PARTITIONS` changes the assignment of every
replica; roll all replicas together and keep the partition count identical on all proxies.

## Tuning

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CORVUS_SCORE_CPUS` | cgroup limit | CPU budget for inference; split across the loaded models (intra-op threads), inter-op is always 1 |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_BATCH_MAX`, `CORVUS_SCORE_BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS` | `64`, `50` | Micro-batch size and maximum wait |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_EMA_ALPHA` | `0.3` | Smoothing of `score_smoothed` |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_SESSIONS_MAX`, `CORVUS_SCORE_SESSION_IDLE_S` | `20000`, `900` | Featurizer state bound and idle eviction |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_RAW_MAX_BUFFERED_FRAMES` | `16384` | Raw-byte models: frames buffered per session, segment and windowing; the oldest are dropped and counted (`corvus_score_raw_frames_dropped_total`) |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_P99_BUDGET_MS` | `10` | Raw-byte models: a model whose `max_packets` is estimated to exceed this p99 per window logs a warning at load; `0` disables |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_WRITE_QUEUE` | `20000` | History rows queued before they are dropped (latest scores are never dropped) |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_MODELS_DIR` | `/tmp/corvus-score/models` | Local model cache |
| `CORVUS_SCORE_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` | `14` | Applied by `corvus-housekeeping` |

## Raw-byte models

A model whose `model_card.json` has `input_kind: "raw_bytes"` is loaded with its `tokenizer.json`, which must hash to
the value in `feature_spec.json` (otherwise the model is rejected and the others keep running). The scorer needs the
plaintext payloads of the capture stream for it: they are tokenized when a batch arrives and only token ids are kept,
for about one window per session and segment. Payload bytes are never persisted or logged. The buffer costs roughly
0.3 KiB per buffered frame; with many concurrent players lower `CORVUS_SCORE_SESSIONS_MAX` or raise the memory limit.
See [raw-byte-tokenizer.md](../reference/raw-byte-tokenizer.md) section 10 for the contract and the measured cost.

```sh
cd services
uv run pytest tests/scoring                 # unit tests, no Docker needed
uv run pytest -m integration tests/scoring  # needs NATS and PostgreSQL from the compose stack
```
