`docs/how-to/run-the-ui.md`:

```md
# How to run the management UI

The UI (`ui/`) is a static Nuxt single-page app that talks to the control-plane API
([control-plane-api.md](../reference/control-plane-api.md)). One build serves every deployment: the API address, the
OIDC settings and the base path are read from `config.json` when the page loads, not at build time.

## Run it locally with the dev stack

1. Set `CORVUS_API_DEV_TOKEN` in `deploy/dev/.env.api` (see `.env.api.example`).
2. Start the stack. The `ui` service builds `ui/Dockerfile` and proxies `/api/` to the `api` service, so the browser needs no CORS:

   ```sh
   cd deploy/dev
   docker compose up --build
   ```

3. Open <http://127.0.0.1:8081>, paste the dev token and pick the roles the UI should assume. The roles only decide
   which actions the UI shows; the API enforces the roles of the token.

## Develop the UI

Requires Node 22.12 or newer (`ui/.nvmrc` pins 24) and pnpm (the version is in `package.json`).

```sh
cd ui
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # http://localhost:3000, reads public/config.json
pnpm lint
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test         # vitest, 2 workers
pnpm generate     # static build, as in the container image
```

For `pnpm dev` the API must be reachable from the browser: either point `apiBaseUrl` in `public/config.json` at an API with CORS
enabled (`CORVUS_API_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000`, off by default) or at a reverse proxy.

After the API schema changes, regenerate the types:

```sh
uv run --project services python ui/scripts/dump-openapi.py   # writes ui/openapi.json
cd ui && pnpm api:types                                      # writes app/types/api.d.ts
```

## Deploy the container

```sh
docker build -f ui/Dockerfile -t corvus-ui .   # from the repository root
docker run -p 8080:8080 \
  -v "$PWD/config.json:/usr/share/nginx/html/config.json:ro" \
  -e CORVUS_UI_BASE_PATH=/ \
  -e CORVUS_UI_API_ORIGIN=https://corvus.example.org \
  -e CORVUS_UI_OIDC_ORIGIN=https://sso.example.org \
  corvus-ui
```

The image is `nginx-unprivileged` (port 8080, no root). It contains no configuration of its own.

### `config.json`

```json
{
  "apiBaseUrl": "https://corvus.example.org/api/v1",
  "basePath": "/",
  "auth": { "mode": "oidc", "rolesClaim": "roles", "roleMapping": {} },
  "oidc": { "issuer": "https://sso.example.org/realms/olf", "clientId": "corvus-ui", "scopes": "openid profile" }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apiBaseUrl` | API root including `/api/v1`. An absolute URL (needs CORS on the API) or a path such as `/api/v1` behind a proxy. |
| `basePath` | Path the app is served under. Must equal `CORVUS_UI_BASE_PATH`; it is used for the OIDC redirect URIs. |
| `auth.mode` | `oidc` (Authorization Code with PKCE) or `token` (paste a bearer token, development only). |
| `auth.rolesClaim`, `auth.roleMapping` | Where the roles are in the token and how external names map to `admin`, `data_scientist`, `staff`, `viewer`. Use the same values as the API (`CORVUS_API_ROLES_CLAIM`, `CORVUS_API_ROLE_MAPPING`). |
| `oidc.*` | Issuer, public client id and scopes. Register `<origin><basePath>auth/callback` as redirect URI and `<origin><basePath>` as post-logout URI. Add `offline_access` if the IdP should issue refresh tokens for silent renewal. |

The login is stored in `localStorage` and shared by all tabs; every tab keeps its own view in the URL.

### Container variables

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CORVUS_UI_BASE_PATH` | `/` | Injected as `<base href>`. Set it when a reverse proxy publishes the UI under a prefix and forwards the request path unchanged, e.g. `/corvus/`. |
| `CORVUS_UI_API_ORIGIN` | empty | Origin added to the CSP `connect-src` when the API is on another origin. |
| `CORVUS_UI_OIDC_ORIGIN` | empty | Origin of the OIDC issuer (discovery and token endpoints) added to `connect-src`. |
| `CORVUS_UI_EXTRA_CONNECT` | empty | More space-separated origins for `connect-src`. |
| `CORVUS_UI_API_UPSTREAM` | empty | If set (e.g. `http://api:8080`), nginx proxies `/api/` to it on the same origin, which avoids CORS. |

Values that are not plain `http(s)` origins are ignored with a warning in the container log.

### Security headers

nginx sends a Content-Security-Policy that allows scripts only from the app itself plus the hashes of the two inline bootstrap
scripts (computed at build time), connections only to `self` and the configured origins, no framing, no objects and a fixed `base-uri`.
Styles allow `unsafe-inline` because Vuetify injects its theme styles at runtime. Also set: `X-Content-Type-Options`,
`X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`. `config.json` is served with `no-store`,
`/_nuxt/` assets are immutable, every other path falls back to `index.html`.

## How the UI uses the API

The UI works against the extended control-plane API ([control-plane-api.md](../reference/control-plane-api.md)) and
does not work around missing endpoints any more:

- **Roles:** after the login the UI calls `GET /me` and shows what the API reports (roles after the API's role
  mapping, display name). The roles read from the token claim (`auth.rolesClaim`, `auth.roleMapping`) are only the
  fallback if `/me` fails.
- **Dashboard:** one request, `GET /summary`, for the counts, the models per stage, the 10 newest jobs and the
  10 newest erasure requests.
- **Erasure requests:** the Players page lists `GET /erasure-requests` (admin, paginated) with the compaction
  status (`compaction_pending`, `compacted_at`). The UI no longer keeps request ids in the browser.
- **Models:** the registry filters (`name`, `version`, `game_context`, `domain`, `stage`) run on the server and need
  an exact match; the detail page loads `GET /models/{name}/{version}`.
- **Pool preview:** while a pool is edited, the UI previews the unsaved filter with `POST /pools/preview`. Requests
  are debounced (500 ms); a newer request aborts the one in flight.
- **Scores:** the Scores page (roles `staff` and `admin`) shows the latest scores of a pseudonym per model and game
  context and the score history as a chart, from `GET /scores/players/{pseudonym}` and `/history`. Scores are
  decision aids; Corvus never sanctions players. The page can be opened with `/scores?pseudonym=<64 hex>`.
- **CORS:** `CORVUS_API_CORS_ORIGINS` lists the browser origins that may call the API (credentials stay off); the
  same-origin proxy (`CORVUS_UI_API_UPSTREAM`) still avoids the need for it.

```

`docs/pilot.md`:

```md
# Corvus pilot runbook

The pilot answers, on a real proxy with real clients:

- real packet rates per player (connection state, direction, packet type, game context) and bytes/s,
- drop rates of the capture queue,
- whether frames are in the client's native protocol or the backend's (ViaVersion on Velocity),
- that no chat or command packets are captured,
- that chat signing still works with the plugin installed.

## Prerequisites

- Docker with Compose v2, a JDK for the Gradle build (the plugin build sets the toolchain), `uv`, `openssl`.
- A Minecraft Java account for every client you connect with (the proxy runs in online mode).
- Roughly 5.5 GB RAM and 4 CPUs free. Limits per container are set in `deploy/pilot/compose.yaml`
  (proxy 1 CPU / 1 GB, each Paper backend 1.5 CPU / 2 GB).

## Pinned versions

| Component | Version | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `itzg/mc-proxy` | `2026.10.0-java25` | Docker Hub tags (Velocity 4.x needs Java 25) |
| `itzg/minecraft-server` | `2026.10.0-java25` | Docker Hub tags |
| Velocity | 4.2.0, build 30 (stable) | PaperMC Fill API |
| Paper (lobby, pvp) | 26.2, build 134 (stable) | PaperMC Fill API |
| PacketEvents | 2.14.0 (`packetevents-velocity-2.14.0.jar`, sha256 `0772f64b...271b`) | GitHub release v2.14.0; identical to the Modrinth file |
| ViaVersion | 5.12.1 | Modrinth CDN, release |
| ViaBackwards | 5.12.1 | Modrinth CDN, release |

Plugins are downloaded by the proxy container from the URLs in `PLUGINS` in `compose.yaml`.
To bump a version, replace the URL and update this table. ViaVersion lets newer clients than the
backend join, ViaBackwards lets older clients join.

## Setup

```sh
cd deploy/pilot
cp .env.example .env
# fill in the secrets:
openssl rand -base64 24 | tr -d '\n=+/'   # VELOCITY_FORWARDING_SECRET
openssl rand -base64 32                   # CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY
# set EULA=TRUE after reading https://aka.ms/MinecraftEULA
```

Keep the pseudonym key outside the data you later share: it is what links a pseudonym to a player.

Build the plugin jar (done from the repository root; the `plugin/` module lives on its own branch):

```sh
./gradlew :plugin:shadowJar
```

The `stage-corvus` service copies exactly one `plugin/build/libs/corvus-velocity-*.jar` (never
`-sources`, `-plain`, `-javadoc`) into the proxy's `/plugins`. It fails with a clear message if there
are zero or several.

Pilot configuration of the plugin is `deploy/pilot/proxy/corvus-config.toml`, mounted read-only as
`plugins/corvus/config.toml` (Velocity's data directory for the plugin id `corvus`). Its keys are the
ones the plugin reads (`PilotConfigTest` fails if it contains a key the plugin ignores): game context
mapping `lobby -> lobby`, `pvp -> pvp` (a backend named `<Task>-<n>`, as CloudNet services are, falls back to
its task name: `Lobby-2` maps via `lobby`; exact names win, only one trailing `-<digits>` is removed, and
`game_context.strip_instance_suffix = false` turns this off), pseudonym key id `pilot-1`, and the payload policy below. The
HMAC key itself is read from the environment variable `CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY` (base64, at least 16
bytes). The plugin writes `plugins/corvus/captures/<yyyy-MM-dd>/<session-id>.cvc`, which is bind
mounted from `deploy/pilot/data/captures`; the one-shot `stage-corvus` service makes that directory
writable for the proxy user (uid 1000).

### Sink (`sink.type`)

`sink.type = "file"` (the pilot default) writes the `.cvc` files described above. `sink.type = "nats"`
publishes every envelope to NATS JetStream instead, following the transport contract in
[`docs/reference/data-lake.md`](reference/data-lake.md) section 1: subject `<nats.subject_prefix>.<proxy_id>.<partition>` (`nats.partitions`, default 16, two-digit decimal),
body = one serialized `Envelope`, headers `Nats-Msg-Id` (`<session-id-hex>-<n>`) and `Corvus-Schema`, each
envelope below 512 KiB. The keys are `nats.url` (one URL or a list), `nats.creds_file` (optional),
`nats.subject_prefix` (default `corvus.capture.v1`), `nats.max_in_flight_bytes` (default 32 MiB) and
`nats.publish_timeout_seconds`; the commented example in `deploy/pilot/proxy/corvus-config.toml` shows them.

Behaviour to know when operating the NATS sink:

- The plugin connects in the background and reconnects forever; an unreachable NATS never delays the proxy
  start. Until the first connection exists, batches are dropped.
- The plugin never creates the stream. If `CORVUS_CAPTURE` does not exist, publishes fail and the log warns
  (at most once a minute) with a hint to check the stream.
- Publishing is asynchronous. When the in-flight byte budget is exhausted or a publish fails or times out, the
  batch is dropped; its frames are counted as `dropped_transport`, reported in the next `CaptureBatch` or
  `SessionEnd` counters, and shown as `dropped_transport=` in `/corvus stats` and the 60 s log line.
- On shutdown the plugin flushes with a bounded 3 s timeout and then closes the connection.

### Private CA for NATS and the control plane (`[tls]`)

If NATS (`tls://`, `wss://`) or the control-plane API (`https://`) are served with certificates from a private CA
(for example a step-ca behind an internal gateway), set `tls.ca_file` to a PEM bundle with that CA. The path is
relative to `plugins/corvus` or absolute; empty (the default) means the JVM default CAs only.

- The bundle is trusted **in addition to** the JVM default CAs, and only by the plugin's NATS connections (sink and
  scores) and the blocklist sync client. The JVM-wide truststore is not changed, so other TLS clients of the proxy
  (Mojang, ...) are unaffected.
- A chain is accepted if either the JVM default trust or the bundle accepts it. Hostname checks still apply.
- If `tls.ca_file` is set but unreadable or contains no certificate, the plugin logs an `ERROR` and does not start
  the NATS sink (nothing is captured when `sink.type = "nats"`), the scores subscription and the blocklist sync. It
  never falls back silently to the JVM default trust. The proxy itself keeps running; fix the file and restart.

### Online scores (`[scores]`)

With `sink.type = "nats"` (or `scores.enabled = true`) the plugin also subscribes to `corvus.score.v1.>` and serves
the scores of online players to other plugins through `corvus-api`, and through `/corvus score <player>`
(permission `corvus.admin`). Details and the decision-aid rules: [`docs/reference/plugin-api.md`](reference/plugin-api.md).

### Blocklist sync (`[blocklist_sync]`)

Optional and off by default. With `blocklist_sync.enabled = true` the plugin fetches
`GET <blocklist_sync.url>/api/v1/plugin/blocklist` (see
[`docs/reference/control-plane-api.md`](reference/control-plane-api.md)) every `interval_seconds` (default 300,
request timeout `timeout_seconds`, default 10) and never captures a player whose pseudonym is in `blocked`, in
addition to the UUID lists of `[players]`. The request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the token is one of
`CORVUS_API_PLUGIN_TOKENS` of the API and is read from the environment variable `CORVUS_PLUGIN_API_TOKEN` or from
`blocklist_sync.token_file` (relative to `plugins/corvus`). It needs the pseudonym key.

- The fetch runs on its own daemon thread, never on Netty or Velocity event threads.
- A player who becomes blocked while online gets a `SessionEnd` and their further frames are ignored.
- A failed sync (network, HTTP status, bad body) keeps the last good list and logs at most once a minute. Until the
  first success only the config lists apply.
- `/corvus stats` shows `blocklist_size`, `blocklist_last_sync` and `blocklist_last_result`.

### Raw payload policy (`capture.raw_payloads`)

Clientbound packets such as scoreboard, teams, titles, spawn player, boss bars contain names and UUIDs
of other players, so payload bytes are restricted. The setting is `none`, `serverbound` (default) or
`all`; the old booleans still parse (`true` = `serverbound`, `false` = `none`).

| Packet group | `none` | `serverbound` | `all` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chat, commands, signing, tab completion, player info (see `PrivacyFilter`) | frame dropped | frame dropped | frame dropped |
| Serverbound text-bearing play types (sign, book, anvil name, plugin message, command blocks, structure and jigsaw blocks, cookie response, test blocks, game rule, custom click action, spectate, inventory clicks) | no payload | no payload | no payload |
| Other serverbound play types in the vocabulary | no payload | payload | payload |
| Serverbound play types outside the vocabulary | no payload | no payload | payload |
| Clientbound entity relative move (and rotation), rotation, head look, teleport, velocity, position sync, player position and look | no payload | payload | payload |
| All other clientbound play types and all configuration packets | no payload | no payload | payload |

Frames are always recorded with their packet type; only the payload bytes differ. `all` logs a WARN
at startup and is for local debugging only: never feed such captures into the data lake.
`Frame.payload_original_size` holds the size before truncation to `max_payload_bytes`; the analyzer
reports the share of truncated payloads.

## Start

```sh
cd deploy/pilot
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f proxy
```

The proxy waits for both backends to become healthy (first start downloads Paper, a few minutes).
Connect to `127.0.0.1:25565` (change `PROXY_BIND`/`PROXY_PORT` in `.env` to expose it).
Captures appear in `deploy/pilot/data/captures/<yyyy-MM-dd>/<session-id>.cvc`.
Stop with `docker compose down` (add `-v` to also drop world data and the plugin volume).

## Clients

Connect with at least:

1. the current vanilla release (matches the backend, native frames expected),
2. an older vanilla version (for example 1.21.x or 1.20.x) to exercise ViaBackwards,
3. optionally a Fabric client (brand check in `SegmentStart.client_brand`).

## Checks on the proxy

1. Plugin load order. the plugin load order decides whether ViaVersion's `via-decoder` sits
   before PacketEvents' `pe-decoder-<id>` in the Netty pipeline. The Corvus plugin logs the pipeline handler names
   once per session together with a `via_before_pe` flag:

   ```sh
   docker compose logs proxy | grep -i via_before_pe
   ```

   Record the value per session. `via_before_pe=true` is a finding to report, because captured frames
   may then be in the translated rather than the client's native protocol (compare with the version
   table in the analyzer output). PacketEvents on Velocity only sees the client to proxy
   connection; there is no backend channel, which is expected.
2. `docker compose logs proxy | grep -i -E "error|exception|corvus"` shows no Corvus errors.

## Manual checklist

For each client:

- [ ] Join; you land on `lobby`.
- [ ] `/server pvp`, then `/server lobby` several times (each switch must start a new segment).
- [ ] Send normal chat messages (signed) on both servers, and run a few commands. Nobody is
      disconnected with "chat validation failed", "out of order chat" or similar.
- [ ] `/corvus stats` shows frames, queue state and drop counters that grow while you play.
- [ ] On `pvp`: a PvP session of N minutes (N >= 10; use two clients fighting each other, moving,
      swinging, placing and breaking blocks).
- [ ] Disconnect cleanly (a `SessionEnd` is written) for most sessions, and kill one client
      abruptly to check truncation handling.
- [ ] No kicks or disconnects caused by Corvus, no stack traces from Corvus in the proxy log.

## Analyze

Stop the stack first (or analyze only closed files; an open file may end in a truncated message,
which the analyzer counts and tolerates).

```sh
cd ml
uv sync
uv run corvus-pilot analyze ../deploy/pilot/data/captures --json /tmp/pilot-report.json
```

The pool size defaults to the cgroup CPU limit (`/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max`), else the usable CPU
count; override with `--workers N`. Exit code: 0 ok, 1 privacy check failed, 2 usage error.

The report contains, per session and per game context: duration, frames/s and bytes/s per direction
and connection state (bytes are payload bytes), top packet types by rate, decoded event rates
(movement, swing, interact_entity, dig, place, held_item, entity_motion), sequence gaps, drop
counters (queue full, privacy, listener errors), a client vs observed protocol version table
(`translated` is true when they differ), and the privacy check. Rates for a context are per
player-second; `per_player_frames_per_s` gives min/median/p95/max over player-segments.

### Privacy check

The analyzer loads `proto/corvus/capture/v1/vocabulary.json` (exported from the plugin, kept in sync
by `VocabularyJsonTest`) and fails when

- a frame has a privacy-dropped packet type (chat, commands, signing, player lists),
- a frame of a payload-stripped type (sign, book, ...) carries a payload,
- under the default policy a frame carries a payload outside the policy: any clientbound payload
  other than the motion allowlist, or a serverbound payload of a type that is not in the vocabulary,
- any string field looks like a UUID or an IP address (the finding reports only the field).

`--payload-policy none|serverbound|all` states which `capture.raw_payloads` the captures were
recorded with (default `serverbound`); only the `stripped` rule applies to `all`. `--vocabulary FILE`
overrides the file. `--denylist FILE` adds packet types or wire ids to the vocabulary's private
ids, for example version dependent wire ids:

```json
{"packet_types": [], "wire_ids": [{"id": 6, "direction": "serverbound", "state": "play"}]}
```

Payload bytes are not scanned for identifiers; the payload policy is what keeps them clean.

## Acceptance thresholds

| Criterion | Pass when |
| --- | --- |
| Corvus-caused kicks and errors | 0 |
| Chat signing | signed chat and commands work on both servers, all clients, across server switches |
| Drop rate (`queue_full / (captured + queue_full)`) | < 0.1 % under normal load, per context and overall |
| Privacy check | analyzer exits 0 (vocabulary denylist and payload policy are always active) |
| Native protocol | `via_before_pe` and the version table understood; any translated frames reported as a finding |

Also report: observed rates per player and context (these size the real pipeline), sequence gaps
(any gap with zero queue drops is a bug), and truncated or corrupt files.

```

`docs/reference/control-plane-api.md`:

```md
# Reference: control-plane API (v1)

HTTP API behind the management UI. It manages training pools, dataset snapshots, labels, players and erasure, the
blocklist, the model registry and training jobs. Corvus never sanctions players itself: the API only produces data
and models. The catalog it reads is described in [data-lake.md](data-lake.md); its own tables are created by
`services/migrations/0002_control_plane.sql`.

- Service: `corvus-api` (FastAPI, uvicorn), default port 8080.
- OpenAPI: `/openapi.json`, interactive docs at `/docs`.
- All business endpoints are under `/api/v1`. `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` are unversioned and unauthenticated.
- Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) with `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`,
  `instance` and, where useful, extension members (`errors` on validation errors, `reasons` on a rejected model
  transition). Validation errors list the location of a problem but never echo the submitted value.
- Lists use keyset pagination: `?limit=` (server maximum applies) and `?cursor=`; the response is
  `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..." | null}`, newest first.

## Authentication and roles

Bearer tokens (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`), validated against an OIDC issuer:

| Check | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Signature | Keys from `CORVUS_API_OIDC_JWKS_URL`, cached for `CORVUS_API_JWKS_CACHE_TTL_S` (600 s). An unknown `kid` triggers one refetch per `CORVUS_API_JWKS_MIN_REFRESH_S` (30 s). Cached keys keep working during an IdP outage. |
| Algorithms | Allowlist `RS256`, `ES256` only (`CORVUS_API_OIDC_ALGORITHMS`). `none` and HMAC algorithms are rejected, the key type must match the algorithm. |
| Claims | `iss` equals `CORVUS_API_OIDC_ISSUER`, `aud` contains `CORVUS_API_OIDC_AUDIENCE`, `exp` and `sub` are required, `nbf` is honoured, leeway `CORVUS_API_OIDC_LEEWAY_S` (30 s). |
| Roles | Read from the claim `CORVUS_API_ROLES_CLAIM` (default `roles`; dotted paths such as `realm_access.roles` work; a list or a space-separated string). `CORVUS_API_ROLE_MAPPING` (JSON) maps external names to Corvus roles; unknown values are ignored. |

Roles: `admin`, `data_scientist`, `staff`, `viewer`. Each endpoint declares the roles it needs; `admin` may call every
endpoint, the other roles are not hierarchical. A missing or invalid token is `401` (with `WWW-Authenticate`), a valid
token without the role is `403`.

**Development token.** Setting `CORVUS_API_DEV_TOKEN` accepts that static value as a bearer token with the roles in
`CORVUS_API_DEV_TOKEN_ROLES` (default `["admin"]`) and logs a warning at startup. It is off unless set. Never set it
outside local development. The service refuses to start if neither OIDC nor a dev token is configured.

**Proxy API tokens.** `GET /api/v1/plugin/blocklist` is a machine endpoint: it accepts only the tokens in
`CORVUS_API_PLUGIN_TOKENS` (comma separated) and nothing else; OIDC tokens and the dev token do not work there, and
proxy tokens open nothing else. With no tokens configured the endpoint rejects every request.

**Job tokens.** ML jobs authenticate with a machine token instead of a person's OIDC token. The API is configured with
`CORVUS_API_JOB_TOKENS`, a comma separated list of `<sha256 hex of the token>:<job name>` entries; only the hash is
stored, never the token. The presented bearer is hashed with SHA-256 and compared in constant time against every
configured hash. A match yields a principal with role `data_scientist` and subject `job:<name>`. Generate a token and
its entry with:

```sh
token=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
echo "$(printf %s "$token" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1):train"   # goes into CORVUS_API_JOB_TOKENS
```

A job token is accepted only where a job needs it: `GET /snapshots`, `GET /snapshots/{id}`, `GET /snapshots/{id}/sessions`, `GET /snapshots/{id}/files`, `POST /models`,
`GET /models`, `GET /models/{id}`, `GET /models/{name}/{version}`, `GET /jobs/{id}` and `PATCH /jobs/{id}`. It cannot
submit jobs, promote models or reach pools, labels, players, erasure, blocklist, scores, `/me` or `/summary` (`403`).
On `GET` and `PATCH /jobs/{id}` a job token additionally needs the header `X-Corvus-Job-Id` to equal the id in the
path (the job's `CORVUS_JOB_ID`), so a job can only act on its own job. The ML job runner reads `CORVUS_API_URL` and
`CORVUS_API_TOKEN` from its environment (for Kubernetes jobs put both into the Secret named by
`CORVUS_API_JOB_K8S_ENV_SECRET`; the local runner passes these two variables through and strips every other
`CORVUS_API_*`) and uses them to register models (`POST /models`) and report progress (`PATCH /jobs/{id}`).

**CORS.** Browsers may call the API from the origins in `CORVUS_API_CORS_ORIGINS` (comma separated, `*` for any;
default none, which disables CORS). Credentials are off (the bearer token travels in the `Authorization` header, not in
cookies), the allowed request headers are `Authorization` and `Content-Type`, and no response headers are exposed
because pagination is part of the JSON body.

## Endpoints

`DS` = `data_scientist`. "read" = `viewer`, `staff`, `data_scientist` (and `admin`).

### Identity and dashboard

| Method and path | Role | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /me` | any valid token | `{"subject", "display_name", "roles"}`; `roles` are the Corvus roles after `CORVUS_API_ROLE_MAPPING`; `display_name` comes from the claim `CORVUS_API_DISPLAY_NAME_CLAIM` (default `name`, fallback `preferred_username`) and is `null` when the token has none. |
| `GET /summary` | read | Counts and recent activity for the dashboard, see below. |
| `GET /erasure-requests` | admin | Erasure requests, newest first, paginated; filter `status` (`completed`). |

`GET /summary` returns `pools`, `snapshots`, `jobs_by_status` (`queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`),
`models_by_stage`, `labels_by_label` (`legit`, `cheat`; absent buckets are `0`), `pending_erasures` (requests with
`compaction_pending`), `recent_jobs` (the 10 newest; id, type, status, snapshot, timestamps, no parameters) and
`recent_erasures` (the 10 newest; id, `pseudonym_prefix` with the first 12 hex characters only, time, status,
`compaction_pending`).

### Pools and snapshots

| Method and path | Role | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /pools`, `GET /pools`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /pools/{id}` | DS | Pool definitions. Names are unique (`409`). Deleting a pool keeps its snapshots. |
| `POST /pools/{id}/preview` | DS | Counts for the current filter. |
| `POST /pools/preview` | DS | Live preview without saving: the body is a pool filter (the `filter` object of a pool), validated exactly like on create; nothing is stored. |
| `POST /pools/{id}/snapshots` | DS | Materialise an immutable snapshot. |
| `GET /pools/{id}/snapshots`, `GET /snapshots`, `GET /snapshots/{id}` | DS | List and detail (the detail view includes the manifest). |
| `GET /snapshots/{id}/sessions` | DS | Sessions of the manifest, ascending by id. Items: `session_id` (32 hex), `pseudonym` (64 hex or `null`), `started_at`, `client_protocol` (integer or `null`), `segments` (`segment`, `game_context`), `labels` (`label`, `source`, `confidence`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`; those applicable at the session start) and `erased`. `exclude_erased=true` leaves out sessions of erased players; `limit` (server maximum applies), `cursor` (the previous page's `next_cursor`, the last session id). |
| `GET /snapshots/{id}/files` | DS | `{"items": [...], "raw": [...]}`, entries `{"manifest_file_id", "id", "key"}`: `items` are the live `events` files for the manifest's files; a file replaced by compaction is followed to its successor, a file that vanished entirely is omitted. `raw` are the live `raw` files that list a session of the manifest (the manifest lists no raw files; `manifest_file_id` equals `id`), so jobs do not scan partitions. |
| `POST /snapshots/{id}/artifacts`, `POST /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts` | DS or job token | Register a prefix a job wrote (derived artefacts, see below). `201` new, `200` repeated. |
| `GET /snapshots/{id}/artifacts` | DS or job token | The snapshot's live registered artefacts. |

A pool also has `raw_retention_days` (integer 1 to `CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_MAX_DAYS`, default 365, `null` = the
deployment default `CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS`, 21; a larger value is `422`). The response adds
`effective_raw_retention_days` (the value that applies, capped at the maximum). Snapshots show `needs_rebuild`
(erasure deleted their raw-derived artefacts).

**Derived artefacts.** Body of both registration endpoints: `{"kind": "raw_features", "s3_prefix":
"features/<snapshot_id>/raw/", "contains_raw": true, "job_id": "<uuid, optional>"}`. `kind` is `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}`;
`s3_prefix` ends with `/` and lies below `features/<snapshot_id>/` or `tokenizers/<snapshot_id>/` (no `.`/`..`/empty
segments); `contains_raw` marks tokenised payload content. A job token sends `X-Corvus-Job-Id` (its own job, which must
belong to the snapshot, otherwise `403`); `POST /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts` takes the snapshot from the job. Registration
is idempotent per (snapshot, prefix): repeating it updates the row (also reviving one that erasure removed) and answers
`200`. `409` means an erasure invalidated the snapshot's raw-derived artefacts after the job started. Response:
`{"id", "snapshot_id", "job_id", "kind", "s3_prefix", "contains_raw", "created_at"}`.

Pool filter (`filter` in the body; all parts optional, combined with AND):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `game_contexts`, `backend_servers` | Session has a segment in one of these. |
| `client_brand.include` / `.exclude` | Session has a segment with (or without) one of these brands. Segment conditions are evaluated on the same segment. |
| `client_protocol.min` / `.max` | Client protocol range of the session. |
| `date_range.start` / `.end` | Inclusive UTC dates of the session start. |
| `label.value` (`legit`, `cheat`, `labeled`, `unlabeled`), `label.min_confidence` | Labels that apply to the session (directly or via its pseudonym) and are valid at its start. |
| `min_session_duration_s` | Ended sessions at least this long. |
| `max_drop_rate` | Dropped frames (queue, privacy, transport) divided by dropped plus estimated captured frames. The captured frames are estimated from `lake_files` row counts split evenly over the sessions of each file. |
| `exclude_orphans` (default `true`) | Skip sessions whose `SessionStart` never arrived. |
| `retention_days` | Stored with the pool for retention jobs; does not change the selection. |

Sessions of erased players are never selected. The filter is translated to SQL with named parameters only; values
never appear in the SQL text.

**Preview** returns `sessions`, `segments` (matching the segment filters), `distinct_players`, `events_files`,
`total_frames_estimate` (each `events` file's `row_count` times the share of its sessions that are selected) and
`label_distribution` (`legit`, `cheat`, `unlabeled`; per session the applicable label with the highest confidence,
then the newest).

**Snapshot** manifest (canonical JSON, keys sorted, no whitespace):

```json
{"version": 1, "pool": {"id": "...", "name": "..."}, "filter": {...},
 "sessions": ["<hex session id, sorted>"], "files": {"events": [{"id": 12, "key": "lake/events/..."}]},
 "created_at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00+00:00"}
```

`sha256` is the SHA-256 of that canonical form, so the same inputs and timestamp give the same hash. Selection and
file list are read in one repeatable-read transaction. Snapshots are append-only: there is no update or delete
endpoint and a database trigger rejects `UPDATE` and `DELETE`.

### Labels

| Method and path | Role | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /labels` | `staff` | One label. |
| `GET /labels` | read | List; filter with `subject_type` (`pseudonym`, `session`) and `subject` (hex). |
| `POST /labels/import` | DS | Bulk import, body `text/csv`, all rows or none. |

A label has `subject_type` and `subject` (pseudonym: 64 hex characters, session id: 32), `label` (`legit`, `cheat`),
`source` (`honeypot`, `staff_verdict`, `ban_import`, `weak_rule`), `confidence` 0 to 1, optional timezone-aware
`valid_from` and `valid_to` (`valid_from` before `valid_to`), `note` (at most 2000 characters; keep personal data out)
and `created_by`, which is always the token subject. CSV columns: `subject_type,subject,label,source,confidence`
(required) and `valid_from,valid_to,note` (optional). An invalid file is answered with `422` and the failing line
numbers in `errors`; limits `CORVUS_API_LABEL_IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` (50 000) and `..._MAX_BYTES` (8 MiB, `413`).

### Players, erasure and blocklist (admin)

| Method and path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /players/lookup` | `{"uuid": ...}` to the pseudonym and its catalog state. `POST` keeps the UUID out of URLs and access logs. |
| `POST /players/erasure` | `{"uuid": ...}` or `{"pseudonym": ...}` (exactly one). Returns `202` with the request. |
| `GET /players/erasure/{id}` | The audit row of a request. |
| `GET /blocklist`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /blocklist/{pseudonym}` | Blocklist and allowlist (`kind`: `block`, `allow`). |
| `GET /plugin/blocklist` | Proxy feed (proxy API token): `{"version", "blocked": [...], "allowed": [...]}`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. `version` is a hash of both lists. |

The UUID to pseudonym step is `HMAC-SHA-256(key, 16 UUID bytes)` with `CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY` (base64) and
`CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY_ID`, identical to the plugin; see [pseudonym-test-vector.md](pseudonym-test-vector.md). Without
the key, UUID endpoints answer `503`; erasure by pseudonym still works. The API never stores or logs a clear UUID; it
logs only the first 12 hex characters of the pseudonym.

**Erasure semantics.** In one transaction: (1) delete the `player_keys` row, which crypto-shreds the player's `raw`
payloads; (2) set `players.erased_at` (ingest stops storing data for that pseudonym); (3) put the pseudonym on the
blocklist with `source = erasure`; (4) delete the player's rows in `scores_latest` and `score_history`; (5) insert an `erasure_requests` row (who, when,
pseudonym, `status = completed`, `player_known`, `key_deleted`, `compaction_pending = true`). If any step fails nothing is changed. A pseudonym that was
never captured is still blocklisted and audited. Erasure can be repeated. `events` files are not rewritten here:
`compaction_pending` stays `true` until `corvus-compact` clears it and sets `compacted_at` (see [data-lake.md](data-lake.md) section 7). Blocklist entries created by an erasure
are permanent: changing or deleting them is `409`. Snapshots keep the (random) session ids they were built from; a
training job reads them through `GET /snapshots/{id}/sessions?exclude_erased=true` and `GET /snapshots/{id}/files`.

### Models

| Method and path | Role | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /models` | DS | Register (`stage = registered`). `name` plus `version` is unique; the snapshot must exist. |
| `GET /models`, `GET /models/{id}`, `GET /models/{id}/transitions` | read | List, detail, audit trail. The list filters on `name`, `version`, `game_context`, `domain` and `stage` (exact match, combined with AND). |
| `GET /models/{name}/{version}` | read | One model by its unique name and version (`404` if unknown). |
| `POST /models/{id}/stage` | DS | `{"stage": ..., "reason": ...}`. |

Fields: `name`, `version`, `candidate_type`, `game_context`, `domain`, `snapshot_id`, `metrics` (JSON), `onnx_key`.
Stages: `registered`, `shadow`, `canary`, `enforce`, `archived`.

Allowed transitions: `registered` to `shadow` to `canary` to `enforce`, and any stage to `archived`; `archived` is
final. Anything else is `409`.

**Quality gate for `enforce`.** The candidate's metrics must satisfy:

1. `p99_latency_ms` is present and below `CORVUS_API_GATE_MAX_P99_LATENCY_MS` (default 10, strictly).
2. If a model is currently in `enforce` for the same snapshot and game context, `recall_at_fpr_0_1pct` is present and
   at least that model's. If the incumbent has no such metric the gate fails closed. Without an incumbent only the
   latency applies.

A failing gate (or a not-allowed transition) answers `409` with every failed condition in `reasons`; nothing is
changed or audited. A passing promotion archives the replaced incumbent in the same transaction. Every applied
transition (including the automatic archive) is stored in `model_transitions` with actor, reason, time and, for
`enforce`, the gate result.

### Jobs (DS)

`POST /jobs` (`202`), `GET /jobs` (filter `status`), `GET /jobs/{id}`, `PATCH /jobs/{id}`. A job has `type` (`build_features`, `evaluate`,
`train`), a `snapshot_id` that must exist, and free-form `params` (at most 16 KiB; no secrets). Status values:
`queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`. `GET /jobs/{id}` refreshes a non-final job from the runner; runner errors
leave the stored status unchanged.

`PATCH /jobs/{id}` is how the job process reports back (DS or a job token, see above): body
`{"status": "running" | "succeeded" | "failed", "message": "...", "result": {...}}` (`message` at most 2000
characters, `result` at most 16 KiB and free of secrets; unknown members are `422`). `succeeded` and `failed` are
final: a different status afterwards is `409`, repeating the identical report is accepted. `result` is returned on the
job. A message the job reported is not overwritten by the runner's own status refresh.

The runner is selected with `CORVUS_API_JOB_RUNNER`:

| Runner | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `local` | Starts `CORVUS_API_JOB_LOCAL_COMMAND` (JSON list, default `["corvus-job"]`) plus the job type as a subprocess without a shell. The child does not inherit `CORVUS_API_*`, `CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY*` or `CORVUS_KEK`. Process handles are in memory: after an API restart a running job is reported `failed` ("process handle lost"). |
| `kubernetes` | Creates a `batch/v1` Job through the official Python client (in-cluster config, else kubeconfig) in `CORVUS_API_JOB_K8S_NAMESPACE`: image, command, `CPU`/`memory` requests and limits (`CORVUS_API_JOB_K8S_*`), labels `app.kubernetes.io/name=corvus-job` and `corvus.onelitefeather.net/job-id`/`job-type`, `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`, `activeDeadlineSeconds`, `backoffLimit` 0, a sized `emptyDir` at `/scratch` (`CORVUS_API_JOB_K8S_SCRATCH_SIZE_LIMIT`, default `20Gi`; `CORVUS_JOB_SCRATCH_DIR` and `TMPDIR` point there), `restartPolicy: Never`, non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped. `CORVUS_API_JOB_K8S_ENV_SECRET` names a Secret exposed as environment. Status comes from the Job's `Complete` and `Failed` conditions. The API's service account needs `create` and `get` on `jobs` in that namespace. |

Contract with the job process, identical for both runners: arguments are the command followed by the job type; the
environment carries `CORVUS_JOB_ID`, `CORVUS_JOB_TYPE`, `CORVUS_JOB_SNAPSHOT_ID` and `CORVUS_JOB_PARAMS` (JSON).

### Scores (staff, data scientist)

Read-only view of what `corvus-score` persisted (see [data-lake.md](data-lake.md) section 6). Roles `staff`,
`data_scientist` and `admin`. The pseudonym is the 64-hex form (`POST /players/lookup` resolves a UUID); a malformed
one is `422`. Scores of `shadow` models are not validated and must not influence decisions about players: they are
returned to `data_scientist` and `admin` only (also in the history, filtered before `limit` applies); `staff` sees
`canary` and `enforce` scores. A player without scores yields an empty list, not `404`. Scores are informational, Corvus never sanctions players.

| Method and path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /scores/players/{pseudonym}` | `{"items": [...]}`: the latest score per (`game_context`, `domain`, `model_name`) with `model_version`, `stage`, `score`, `smoothed`, `windows`, `updated_at`. |
| `GET /scores/players/{pseudonym}/history?game_context=&limit=` | `{"items": [...]}` newest first: the same fields per window plus `session_id`, `segment`, `window_start_offset_nanos`, `window_end_offset_nanos`, `scored_at`. `game_context` is optional, `limit` defaults to 100 (1 to 1000). |

The history keeps `CORVUS_SCORE_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 14) days; `corvus-housekeeping` prunes it.

### Operations

`GET /healthz` (liveness, no dependencies), `GET /readyz` (`503` when PostgreSQL does not answer within 3 s),
`GET /metrics` (Prometheus: `corvus_api_requests_total`, `corvus_api_request_seconds` by route template and method,
`corvus_api_erasures_total`, `corvus_api_model_transitions_total`, `corvus_api_jobs_total`). `/metrics` is
unauthenticated; keep it on the cluster network.
