`docs/reference/data-lake.md`:

```md
# Reference: capture transport, data lake and catalog (v1)

This is the contract between the capture plugin, the ingest service and the ML side.
Changing it requires a schema version bump or an append-only change.

## 1. Transport (NATS JetStream)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Stream | `CORVUS_CAPTURE` |
| Subjects | `corvus.capture.v1.>` |
| Publish subject | `corvus.capture.v1.<proxy_id>.<partition>`; `partition` = first 4 bytes of `session_id` as big-endian unsigned int mod `partitions` (default 16), formatted as two-digit decimal (`00`..`15`) |
| Message body | one serialized `corvus.capture.v1.Envelope` (no length prefix) |
| Header `Nats-Msg-Id` | `<session-id-hex>-<n>`, `n` = per-session envelope counter starting at 0 (JetStream de-duplication) |
| Header `Corvus-Schema` | `capture.v1` |
| Max message size | 1 MiB; the plugin splits `CaptureBatch`es so that each serialized envelope stays below 512 KiB |
| Stream limits | file storage, `max_age` 24 h, `max_bytes` configurable (default 10 GiB), discard old, duplicate window 2 min |
| Consumer (ingest) | durable pull consumer `corvus-ingest` on `corvus.capture.v1.>`, explicit ack, `ack_wait` 120 s, `max_ack_pending` 1000; all ingest replicas share it |

All envelopes of one session use the same partition, so a consumer that filters on a partition sees a
session completely. The partition count is part of the deployment config and must be identical on all
proxies; changing it requires draining the scorers.

Envelope kinds: `SessionStart`, `SegmentStart`, `CaptureBatch`, `SessionEnd`. Every `CaptureBatch` carries
`session_id` and `segment`, so ingest never depends on message order.

The plugin publishes asynchronously and never blocks a Netty thread. If the in-flight limit is reached or a publish
fails, the frames of that batch are dropped and counted in `CaptureCounters.dropped_transport`.

## 2. Object storage layout (S3 / MinIO)

Bucket configurable (default `corvus-lake`). All files are Parquet, zstd-compressed, written by ingest.

```
lake/events/date=YYYY-MM-DD/part-<ulid>.parquet   long retention (per pool)
lake/raw/date=YYYY-MM-DD/part-<ulid>.parquet      short retention (default 21 days)
_staging/<table>/<ulid>.parquet                   upload target before promotion
```

`date` is the UTC date of the session start. Partitioning by player is forbidden (tiny files).

### Table `events` (one row per captured frame, also frames without a decoded event)

| Column | Arrow type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | fixed_size_binary(16) | |
| `segment` | uint32 | |
| `seq` | uint64 | dedup key together with `session_id` |
| `offset_nanos` | uint64 | since session start |
| `direction` | uint8 | proto `Direction` value |
| `state` | uint8 | proto `ConnectionState` value |
| `packet_type` | uint32 | Corvus vocabulary id (`proto/corvus/capture/v1/vocabulary.json`) |
| `wire_packet_id` | int32 | |
| `payload_original_size` | uint32 | 0 if no payload |
| `event_kind` | uint8 | 0 none, 1 movement, 2 interact_entity, 3 swing, 4 dig, 5 place, 6 held_item, 7 entity_motion |
| `has_position`, `has_rotation`, `on_ground` | bool (nullable) | movement |
| `x`, `y`, `z` | float64 (nullable) | movement position, entity_motion vector |
| `yaw`, `pitch` | float32 (nullable) | movement |
| `entity_id` | int32 (nullable) | interact_entity, entity_motion |
| `action` | uint8 (nullable) | interact action / entity_motion kind (1 relative, 2 teleport, 3 velocity, 4 spawn) |
| `sneaking`, `off_hand` | bool (nullable) | interact, swing, place |
| `block_x`, `block_y`, `block_z`, `face`, `status` | int32 (nullable) | dig, place |
| `slot` | int32 (nullable) | held_item |

Rows are sorted by (`session_id`, `seq`) within a file.

### Table `raw` (short retention, crypto-shredded)

| Column | Arrow type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | fixed_size_binary(16) | |
| `segment` | uint32 | |
| `seq` | uint64 | |
| `payload_original_size` | uint32 | |
| `nonce` | fixed_size_binary(12) | |
| `ciphertext` | binary | AES-256-GCM of the payload with the player's DEK, AAD = `session_id || seq (8 bytes big-endian)` |

Only frames that carry a payload get a `raw` row.

Retention is per pool (NFR-018): `pools.raw_retention_days` (default `CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS`, 21; at most
`CORVUS_RAW_RETENTION_MAX_DAYS`, 365). `corvus-housekeeping` deletes a `raw` file only when its date is older than the
**longest** retention of any pool whose snapshot lists a session of the file (found through `lake_file_sessions` and
the snapshot manifests). Sessions in no snapshot, and pools that were deleted, count with the default. So a pool can
shorten the life of data nobody else uses, and keep a file longer than the default.

## 3. Keys and erasure

- Every pseudonymised player gets a random 256-bit data encryption key (DEK) on first sight.
- The DEK is stored wrapped (AES-256-GCM) with a key encryption key (KEK) from `CORVUS_KEK` (base64, 32 bytes),
  identified by `CORVUS_KEK_ID`. The KEK never touches the database or the lake.
- Erasure of a player: delete the `player_keys` row (crypto-shredding of `raw`), mark `players.erased_at`, add the
  pseudonym to the blocklist; `corvus-compact` later rewrites `events` and still-existing `raw` files without the player's sessions (section 7).

## 4. Catalog (PostgreSQL, schema `corvus`)

| Table | Key | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `players` | `pseudonym bytea` | `key_id`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `erased_at` |
| `player_keys` | `pseudonym bytea` → players | `dek_wrapped bytea`, `kek_id text`, `created_at` |
| `sessions` | `session_id bytea` | `pseudonym`, `proxy_id`, `client_protocol`, `observed_protocol`, `plugin_version`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, counters (`dropped_queue_full`, `dropped_privacy`, `listener_errors`, `dropped_transport`, summed over batches) |
| `segments` | (`session_id`, `segment`) | `backend_server`, `game_context`, `client_brand`, `started_at` |
| `lake_files` | `id bigserial`, unique `s3_key` | `table_name`, `date`, `row_count`, `size_bytes`, `schema_version`, `created_at`, `deleted_at` |
| `lake_file_sessions` | (`file_id`, `session_id`) | which sessions a file contains (pool selection, erasure, compaction) |

Migration `0005_compaction.sql` adds `lake_files.replaced_by` (successor of a compacted file), `lake_files.purge_pending`
(row marked deleted, object not yet removed), `erasure_requests.compacted_at` and the view `corvus.erased_sessions`
(`session_id`, `pseudonym`, `erased_at` for sessions of erased players).

Migrations are plain, numbered SQL files applied in order under a PostgreSQL advisory lock; they are never edited
after release.

## 5. Ingest delivery semantics

1. Fetch a batch of messages, decode envelopes, upsert `players`/`sessions`/`segments` immediately.
2. Buffer frames in Arrow builders per (table, date); flush when a buffer exceeds the row or byte limit or its age
   limit (defaults 200 000 rows, 64 MiB, 60 s).
3. Flush: write Parquet to `_staging/`, copy to the final key, insert `lake_files` + `lake_file_sessions` in one
   transaction, then ack all messages whose frames are in the file, then delete the staging object.
4. Redelivery can produce duplicate rows; readers de-duplicate on (`session_id`, `seq`). Final objects without a
   catalog row older than 1 h are orphans and are removed by housekeeping.

## 6. Online scoring

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Consumer (scoring) | one durable pull consumer per scorer replica, `corvus-score-<ordinal>`, `filter_subjects` = the replica's partitions (`corvus.capture.v1.*.<pp>`, `<pp>` formatted like the plugin: two digits, wider above 100 partitions, e.g. `005` of 128), deliver policy `new` (scoring never replays history), explicit ack right after the frames are fed into the featurizer. An existing consumer with different filters is updated, an unchanged one is left alone |
| Partition assignment | replica `i` of `n` owns partitions `p` with `p mod n == i` (`CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICA_INDEX`, else the StatefulSet ordinal; `CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICAS`, `CORVUS_CAPTURE_PARTITIONS`) |
| Session state | `SessionStart` gives the pseudonym, `SegmentStart` the game context. Because of deliver policy `new` a batch can arrive for a session the scorer never saw start: it is then looked up in the catalog (`sessions`, `segments`, written by ingest). If the catalog does not know it either (or ingest has not written it yet) the batch is skipped and counted (`corvus_score_unknown_session_skips_total`); the failed lookup is remembered for `CORVUS_SCORE_LOOKUP_RETRY_S` (5 s) |
| Featurizer | the same `corvus_ml.features` code as offline feature building (no training/serving skew); frames are mapped by `codec.event_row` (the `events` table mapping) plus the offline null conventions. State per session in a bounded LRU with idle eviction, freed on `SessionEnd`; the tail windows of an ended or evicted session are still scored. `tick_end` hint: sessions below protocol 768 are known not to send `CLIENT_TICK_END` (hint `false`), otherwise it is inferred |
| Models | loaded from the model registry (`corvus.models`) in the stages `shadow`, `canary`, `enforce`; every such model scores the windows of its `game_context` (several domains and several models per context are possible). Polled every `CORVUS_SCORE_REGISTRY_POLL_S` (30 s); ONNX and the `feature_spec.json` next to it are downloaded from S3, validated with `FeatureSpec.load` (a mismatch keeps only that model out) and swapped in atomically. The input layout (aggregates or token sequence) follows from the ONNX input rank. ONNX Runtime on CPU, sequential, inter-op 1, intra-op threads = CPU budget / concurrently running models |
| Inference | completed windows of all sessions are micro-batched (`CORVUS_SCORE_BATCH_MAX` 64, `CORVUS_SCORE_BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS` 50) and run per model in a bounded thread pool. Scores are clipped to [0, 1]. Smoothing is an EMA (`CORVUS_SCORE_EMA_ALPHA`) per (pseudonym, segment, model) |
| Score subject | `corvus.score.v1.<game_context>` (characters outside `A-Za-z0-9_-` in the context are replaced by `_`); body = serialized `corvus.score.v1.Score` (`proto/corvus/score/v1/score.proto`) |
| Score stream | `CORVUS_SCORE`, subjects `corvus.score.v1.>`, `max_age` 7 d (`CORVUS_SCORE_STREAM_MAX_AGE_S`), created by the scorer if missing |
| Persistence | `scores_latest` (primary key pseudonym, game_context, domain, model_name; newer `updated_at` wins) and the append-only `score_history` (migration `0003_scores.sql`), written in batches off the consumer path. When the bounded write queue (`CORVUS_SCORE_WRITE_QUEUE`) is full, history rows are dropped and counted, the latest row is still upserted. `corvus-housekeeping` prunes the history after `CORVUS_SCORE_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` (14) |
| Shutdown | on SIGTERM: stop fetching, score the pending windows, flush the writes, drain NATS. Featurizer state is not persisted; after a restart sessions continue from the next batch |

Scores of `shadow` models are persisted but never published. Consumers must treat `canary` scores as
informational; only `enforce` scores may drive automated actions in other systems, and Corvus itself
never sanctions players.

## 7. Compaction after erasure

`corvus-compact` is a one-shot process (Helm: CronJob, hourly) that makes erasure physical. It takes the
`erasure_requests` with `compaction_pending = true` that are older than `CORVUS_COMPACT_GRACE_S` (600 s, so frames still
buffered or cached by ingest at erasure time have landed), finds the live `events` and `raw` files that list sessions of
the erased pseudonyms in `lake_file_sessions`, and per file, under `pg_try_advisory_lock` (a file that another run holds
is skipped and the request stays pending):

1. downloads the file to local disk and rewrites it as zstd Parquet batch by batch (`CORVUS_COMPACT_BATCH_ROWS`, 65 536
   rows), dropping the rows of erased sessions; row order and schema are unchanged;
2. uploads the result to `_staging/<table>/<ulid>.parquet` and copies it to a new final key
   `lake/<table>/date=<day>/part-<ulid>.parquet`, like ingest does;
3. in one transaction inserts the new `lake_files` and `lake_file_sessions` rows (the old file's sessions minus the
   erased ones), sets the old file's `deleted_at`, `replaced_by` and `purge_pending`; a file with no rows left has no
   successor;
4. deletes the old object and clears `purge_pending`.

A file that lists an erased session without holding rows of it (typical for `raw`) is not rewritten; only the
`lake_file_sessions` entry is removed. When every file of the requests is done, the requests get
`compaction_pending = false` and `compacted_at`. The job exits non-zero if any file failed.

Crash safety: until step 3 commits the old file stays the live one (an object copied but never registered is an orphan
that housekeeping removes after one hour); after it only `purge_pending` work remains, which every run retries first.
Repeating a run, or a repeated erasure of the same pseudonym, changes nothing.

Snapshots are immutable and keep naming erased sessions and the file ids that compaction replaced. Jobs read a snapshot
through `GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/sessions?exclude_erased=true` (paged) and `GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/files`
(follows `replaced_by` to the live files; `raw` lists the live raw files, so a job does not scan partitions) instead of
trusting the manifest alone; see [control-plane-api.md](control-plane-api.md).

### Derived artefacts

Tokenised raw-byte features (`features/<snapshot_id>/raw/`, the packet table) contain payload content: they are personal
data derived from `raw`. A job registers every prefix it writes in `corvus.derived_artifacts` (`snapshot_id`, `job_id`,
`kind`, `s3_prefix`, `contains_raw`, `created_at`, `deleted_at`, `deleted_reason`) with
`POST /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/artifacts` (see [ml-jobs.md](ml-jobs.md)). Only registered prefixes are reached by erasure
and retention; the API accepts only prefixes below `features/<snapshot_id>/` and `tokenizers/<snapshot_id>/`, and the
deleting side refuses anything else.

- **Erasure.** Before it rewrites files, `corvus-compact` finds the live `contains_raw` artefacts of the snapshots that
  list a session of an erased player and deletes their whole prefix (not a rewrite: the packet table is a derived,
  window-agnostic table that is cheaper to rebuild than to rewrite, and a rebuild skips erased players because their DEK
  is gone). The artefact row gets `deleted_at` / `deleted_reason = 'erasure'` and the snapshot is marked
  `needs_rebuild` in `corvus.snapshot_state` (a table of its own, because `dataset_snapshots` is immutable;
  `GET /snapshots/{id}` shows `needs_rebuild`). Artefacts of jobs that started after the erasure request are kept: those
  jobs already excluded the player. The requests complete only after this step succeeded; a failed delete is retried.
- **Rebuild.** Registering a `contains_raw` artefact from a job that started after the erasure clears `needs_rebuild`;
  a job that started before it is refused with `409` (its output may contain the erased player, delete its prefix).
- **Retention.** `corvus-housekeeping` deletes a `contains_raw` artefact once its snapshot's pool retention has passed
  since the start of the newest session of the snapshot, so derived data never outlives the raw data it comes from.
  Expiry does not set `needs_rebuild`: the raw source is gone, a rebuild would fail.
- Prefixes nobody registered (a job that crashed before registering) are not tracked. Register right after writing,
  and before the long-running parts of the job where possible.

```

`docs/reference/feature-spec.md`:

```md
# Reference: feature spec (`feature_spec.json`)

A feature spec pins everything a model depends on besides its weights: how the windows were cut,
which aggregates and token columns exist, and exactly how they are turned into model input
tensors. It is written next to the artifacts and checked on load, so a model is never silently
scored with features that differ from the ones it was trained on.

Code: `ml/src/corvus_ml/features/spec.py` (format and validation) and `model_input.py` (the
adapter that builds the tensors). Both import without Arrow, torch, scikit-learn or ONNX Runtime.

## 1. Where it is written and read

| Artifact | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `<build out>/feature_spec.json` next to `windows/` and `window_tokens/` | `corvus-features build` | `corvus-eval` (window parameters of the data; validated) |
| `<eval out>/onnx/<game_context>/feature_spec.json` next to the exported `*.onnx` | `corvus-eval run` | the scoring service, before it loads a model |
| `models/<name>/<version>/feature_spec.json` next to `model.onnx` | the `train` job (copied from the export) | the scoring service |

The `train` job also writes `model_card.json` and `calibration.json` there; the feature spec stays
unchanged. What the model outputs is described in `model_card.json` (`output_semantics`), see
[ml-jobs.md](ml-jobs.md).

The file next to a model describes both input kinds (`agg`, `seq`); a model uses the one matching
its input. Normalisation (mean and std) is inside the ONNX graph and is not part of the spec.

## 2. Format (version 1)

```json
{
  "name": "corvus-features",
  "version": 1,
  "window": {
    "window": 256, "overlap": 0.5, "max_duration_s": 30.0, "min_frames": 16,
    "dt_edges_ms": [0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 35.0, 50.0, 75.0, 100.0, 200.0, 500.0, 1000.0, 5000.0],
    "entity_cache": 256
  },
  "aggregate_names": ["cps", "attacks_per_s", "packets_per_s", "movement_per_s", "rot_var",
                      "rot_speed_mean", "rot_speed_max", "on_ground_frac", "tick_end_rate"],
  "token_columns": ["packet_type", "direction", "event_kind", "domain", "action", "dt_bucket",
                    "log_dt", "has_pos_delta", "dx", "dy", "dz", "has_rot_delta", "dyaw", "dpitch",
                    "rot_speed", "rot_accel", "on_ground", "t_since_swing", "t_since_move",
                    "target_dist", "target_angle"],
  "model_inputs": {
    "agg": {"columns": ["cps", "attacks_per_s", "packets_per_s", "movement_per_s", "rot_var",
                        "rot_speed_mean", "rot_speed_max", "n_frames", "on_ground_frac",
                        "tick_end_rate", "has_on_ground_frac", "has_tick_end_rate"]},
    "seq": {
      "length": 256,
      "columns": [{"name": "event_kind", "transform": "scale8"}, "... 19 columns in total"],
      "mask": "last"
    }
  }
}
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name`, `version` | Always `corvus-features`; `version` is bumped whenever the meaning of a feature or the input layout changes (a new token column, another transform, a changed formula). |
| `window` | The `FeaturizerConfig` the windows were produced with. |
| `aggregate_names` | Order of `CompletedWindow.aggregates` (float64, NaN = null). |
| `token_columns` | Column order of `CompletedWindow.tokens` (float32 matrix, one row per serverbound frame). |
| `model_inputs.agg.columns` | Column order of the aggregate input `(n, len(columns))`, float32. Nullable aggregates are 0 when null and followed by a `has_<name>` indicator (1 = present). `n_frames` is the window's frame count. |
| `model_inputs.seq` | Token input `(n, length, len(columns) + 1)`, float32, input name `x`. The transformed token columns are placed from position 0, zero padding follows, frames beyond `length` are cut, and the last channel is the mask (1 = real frame). Transforms: `id`, `slog` = `sign(x) * ln(1 + abs(x))`, `scale8` = `x / 8`. |

### Kind `raw_bytes` (version 2)

A model on tokenised raw packet bytes ([raw-byte-tokenizer.md](raw-byte-tokenizer.md)) has
`"version": 2` and a `raw_bytes` object inside `model_inputs`: the hash and size of `tokenizer.json`
(which must sit next to the spec), the token layout, the packet row width and the window configuration.
The aggregate and sequence sections are still written but unused. Because of the version, a runtime
that only knows version 1 refuses such a model (`FeatureSpecMismatch`, version) instead of feeding it
the wrong tensor. `FeatureSpec.load(path, require_tokenizer=True)` additionally compares the SHA-256 of
`tokenizer.json` with the recorded one.

## 3. Validation

`FeatureSpec.load(path)` parses the file and compares it with the spec of the running code:
`name`, `version`, `aggregate_names`, `token_columns` and both `model_inputs` layouts must be
equal. `window` and `length` of the file are authoritative; a service builds its
`SessionFeaturizer` from `spec.window`. `FeatureSpec.load(path, expected=...)` additionally
compares the window parameters and `seq_len` (for a service configured with explicit values).

Any difference raises `FeatureSpecMismatch` listing every difference, for example:

```
feature spec of the model does not match the runtime:
  - version: model has 1, runtime expects 2
  - token_columns: model has (...), runtime expects (...)
```

A missing, unparsable or structurally invalid file raises `FeatureSpecError`.

## 4. Using it

```python
from corvus_ml.features.featurizer import SessionFeaturizer
from corvus_ml.features.model_input import model_inputs
from corvus_ml.features.spec import FeatureSpec

spec = FeatureSpec.load(model_dir)               # raises on mismatch
featurizer = SessionFeaturizer(session_id, spec.window)
windows = [w for frame in frames for w in featurizer.feed(frame)]
x = model_inputs(windows, "seq", spec)           # feed to the ONNX graph as input "x"
```

Evaluation reads the offline Parquet tables and builds the same tensors with the same functions
(`aggregate_inputs`, `encode_tokens`, `scatter_frames`), and `tests/test_model_input.py` asserts that both
paths produce identical arrays for every candidate.

```

`docs/reference/features.md`:

```md
# Reference: feature and window stage (v1)

Input is the lake table `events` plus a `segments(session_id, segment, game_context)` table
(see [data-lake.md](data-lake.md)). Output is two Parquet tables written by `corvus-features build`
(`ml/src/corvus_ml/features/`). The feature logic is an incremental core
([section 6](#6-incremental-featurizer-offline-and-online)) that the online scoring service runs
unchanged; `build` also writes [`feature_spec.json`](feature-spec.md) next to the tables.

```
uv run corvus-features build --events <dir|s3://...> --segments <parquet|csv|arrow> --out <dir>
    [--context pvp] [--session <hex>]... [--window 256] [--overlap 0.5] [--max-duration 30]
    [--min-frames 16] [--dt-edges-ms ...] [--workers N] [--group-size 4]
    [--s3-endpoint URL --s3-region R --s3-scheme http|https]
```

S3 credentials come from the standard AWS environment. A CSV `session_id` is the 32-char hex string.

## 1. Pipeline

1. Sessions are selected from the segments table (`--context`, `--session`), sorted, and split into
   groups of `--group-size` sessions (default 4).
2. A worker reads one group: the dataset scan is filtered by `session_id IN (...)` and projects only
   the needed columns, in batches of at most 65 536 rows. Per session the rows are ordered by `seq`
   and de-duplicated on (`session_id`, `seq`); the first row of a duplicate wins.
3. The session is cut into runs of equal `segment`. Runs whose segment is absent from the segments
   table are skipped. **All per-run state is reset at a segment boundary** (previous frame, position,
   rotation, entity positions), and windows never cross it.
4. The frames of a run are fed one by one into a `SessionFeaturizer`: tokens are computed for the
   serverbound frames, clientbound `entity_motion` frames only feed the entity position state.
5. Windows are cut and aggregated by the featurizer as soon as their extent is known, then written. One file per group: `windows/part-<group>.parquet` and
   `window_tokens/part-<group>.parquet`. The output does not depend on the worker count.

Worker count defaults to the cgroup CPU limit (`corvus_ml.cgroup.default_workers`). Memory is
bounded by the group (sessions per task) times the largest session, not by the dataset: a
synthetic 4 x 300 000 frame run with `--group-size 1` peaked at about 650 MiB including the generation of
the test data in the same process. Lower `--group-size` for very long sessions.

## 2. Token features (table `window_tokens`)

One row per serverbound frame. Unknown values are never NaN: they are 0 with the matching `has_*`
flag, or an explicit sentinel (documented per feature).

| Feature | Type | Unit | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packet_type` | uint32 | id | Corvus vocabulary id (`vocabulary.json`), version stable |
| `direction` | uint8 | enum | proto `Direction` (always 1 here) |
| `event_kind` | uint8 | enum | as in `events` |
| `domain` | uint8 | enum | 1 movement (`event_kind` 1), 2 combat (2, 3), 3 interaction (4, 5, 6), 0 other |
| `action` | uint8 | enum | `events.action` (2 = attack for interact_entity), 0 if null |
| `dt_bucket` | int16 | index | index of the first edge greater than the gap to the previous serverbound frame (`searchsorted(edges, dt, side="right")`); edges default to 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 35, 50, 75, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 5000 ms, so values are `0..len(edges)`; first frame of a segment: `len(edges)+1` |
| `log_dt` | float32 | ln(1+ms) | `ln(1 + dt_ms)`, 0 for the first frame |
| `has_pos_delta` | uint8 | flag | movement frame with position and a known previous position |
| `dx`, `dy`, `dz` | float32 | blocks | position minus the last known position (any earlier movement frame with position); 0 if `has_pos_delta` = 0 |
| `has_rot_delta` | uint8 | flag | movement frame with rotation and a known previous rotation |
| `dyaw` | float32 | degrees | `((yaw - prev_yaw + 180) mod 360) - 180`, in [-180, 180); 179 to -179 gives +2 |
| `dpitch` | float32 | degrees | `pitch - prev_pitch` (no wrap) |
| `rot_speed` | float32 | deg/s | `hypot(dyaw, dpitch) / dt_rot`, `dt_rot` = seconds since the previous rotation sample; 0 if `dt_rot` <= 0 |
| `rot_accel` | float32 | deg/s^2 | `(rot_speed - prev_rot_speed) / dt_rot`; 0 if there is no previous speed |
| `on_ground` | int8 | flag | movement frames: 0 or 1; -1 for everything else or null |
| `t_since_swing` | float32 | s | attack frames only: time since the last swing frame, capped at 10; 10 if none; 0 on other frames |
| `t_since_move` | float32 | s | attack frames only: time since the last movement frame, same cap |
| `target_dist` | float32 | blocks | attack frames only: distance eye to the target aim point; -1 if the target entity or the player pose is unknown |
| `target_angle` | float32 | degrees | attack frames only: angle between the look vector and the eye to aim point direction; -1 if unknown |

Attack frame: `event_kind` = 2 and `action` = 2 (`ACTION_ATTACK`).

Geometry for `target_*`:

- Eye = last known player position + (0, 1.62, 0).
- Aim point = last known entity position + (0, 0.9, 0) (mid body of a 1.8 block entity).
- Look vector from the last known rotation, Minecraft convention:
  `(-sin(yaw) cos(pitch), -sin(pitch), cos(yaw) cos(pitch))`, angles in radians.
- `target_angle = acos(clamp(look . v / |v|))` in degrees, `v` = aim point minus eye.

Entity positions come from clientbound `entity_motion` frames (`events.action` = kind): kind 2
(teleport) and kind 4 (spawn) store the absolute position, kind 1 (relative) adds the delta to a known position and is
ignored for unknown entities, kind 3 (velocity) is ignored. The state is a bounded LRU (256 entities,
`FeatureConfig.entity_cache`), reset per segment.

## 3. Windows (table `windows`)

A window is up to N serverbound frames (`--window`, default 256) that start within `--max-duration`
(default 30 s) of its first frame. The next window starts `n - floor(n * overlap)` frames after the
start of the current one (n = frames of that window; 128 for a full 256 frame window at 50 % overlap).
The window that contains the last frame of the run is the last one. Windows with fewer than
`--min-frames` (default 16) frames are dropped.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `session_id`, `segment` | binary(16), uint32 | |
| `game_context` | string | from the segments table |
| `window_index` | uint32 | counter per (session, segment), from 0 |
| `start_offset_nanos`, `end_offset_nanos` | uint64 | `offset_nanos` of the first and last frame |
| `first_seq`, `last_seq` | uint64 | join keys back to `events` (and to labels later) |
| `n_frames` | uint32 | |
| `cut` | string | `full` (N frames), `duration` (max duration hit), `end` (run ended) |
| `cps` | float64 | swings per second: `count(event_kind = 3) / span` |
| `attacks_per_s` | float64 | `count(attack frames) / span` |
| `packets_per_s` | float64 | `n_frames / span` (serverbound) |
| `movement_per_s` | float64 | `count(event_kind = 1) / span` |
| `rot_var` | float64 | population variance of `dyaw` plus population variance of `dpitch` over frames with `has_rot_delta`; 0 with fewer than 2 samples |
| `rot_speed_mean`, `rot_speed_max` | float64 | over frames with `has_rot_delta`; 0 if none |
| `on_ground_frac` | float64, null | share of `on_ground` = 1 among frames with `on_ground` >= 0; null if none |
| `tick_end_rate` | float64, null | `count(CLIENT_TICK_END) / span`; null if the segment never sends it |

`span` is `(end_offset_nanos - start_offset_nanos) / 1e9`; all rates are 0 when `span` is 0.

## 4. Why a separate `window_tokens` table

Tokens are stored long (`session_id`, `segment`, `window_index`, `pos`, features) instead of
fixed-size list columns in `windows` because:

- the schema does not depend on `--window`, so runs with different N stay comparable and a model can
  change N without a schema migration;
- duration-cut and tail windows are shorter than N and need no padding or mask column;
- columnar compression works per feature column, and a consumer can read aggregates without touching
  the 10 to 20 times larger token data;
- the cost is a regroup by (`session_id`, `segment`, `window_index`) when training, ordered by `pos`.

With 50 % overlap every frame is stored about twice. Per-domain views are a filter on `domain`.

## 5. Determinism

Same input produces byte-identical files: groups are sorted, one file per group index, fixed Parquet
settings (zstd level 3), no timestamps, and `seq` order with first-wins de-duplication.

## 6. Incremental featurizer (offline and online)

The code that computes tokens, cuts windows and aggregates them is one pure, numpy-only component
(`ml/src/corvus_ml/features/featurizer.py`, no Arrow import). The offline build and the scoring
service both use it, so there is no training/serving skew by construction; `tests/
test_features_golden.py` pins the offline output to a fixture generated before the extraction.

```python
fz = SessionFeaturizer(session_id, FeaturizerConfig(window=256, overlap=0.5, ...))
fz.begin_segment(segment, tick_end=None)     # optional; feed() starts runs by itself
for frame in frames:                          # corvus_ml.features.frames.Frame, one events row
    for window in fz.feed(frame):             # CompletedWindow
        ...
for window in fz.flush():                     # tail of the current run
    ...
```

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| `Frame` | NamedTuple mirroring the `events` columns the featurizer reads: `segment`, `seq`, `offset_nanos`, `direction`, `packet_type`, `event_kind`, `has_position`, `has_rotation`, `on_ground` (None or -1 = unknown), `x`, `y`, `z`, `yaw`, `pitch` (NaN = null), `entity_id`, `action` |
| `FeaturizerConfig` | frozen: `window`, `overlap`, `max_duration_s`, `min_frames`, `dt_edges_ms`, `entity_cache`; the offline `FeatureConfig` adds only I/O knobs |
| `CompletedWindow` | `session_id`, `segment`, `window_index`, `start_offset_nanos`, `end_offset_nanos`, `first_seq`, `last_seq`, `n_frames`, `cut`; `aggregates` float64 vector in the order of the aggregate columns of section 3 (NaN = null); `tokens` float32 matrix `(n_frames, 21)` in the column order of section 2 (all token features, `packet_type` first); `token_seq`, `token_offset_nanos` uint64 per row |
| Emission | A window is returned from `feed` once its extent is certain: its `window`-th frame arrived, or a frame beyond `max_duration_s` arrived. `flush` emits the tail (`cut = end`) subject to `min_frames`, and resets the run. A window that already reached the last frame is not emitted twice. |
| Segment boundary | `feed` of a frame with another `segment` first flushes the run; previous frame, position, rotation, entity positions and buffered tokens are reset. `window_index` continues per segment if a segment is entered again. |
| Redelivery | A frame with `seq` not greater than the last one is ignored, so at-least-once delivery is harmless. Frames must otherwise arrive in `seq` order. |
| `tick_end_rate` | Null when the run never sends `CLIENT_TICK_END`. The offline build knows this for the whole run and passes it to `begin_segment(tick_end=...)`. Online (`tick_end=None`) it is inferred from the frames seen so far, so a window that completes before the first tick end reports null where the offline build would report 0.0 if the run sends tick ends later. |
| Memory | Consumed frames are released; the buffer holds about one window of tokens per run. |

The streaming result equals the batch definition of sections 2 and 3 for any chunking of the same
frames (`tests/test_featurizer.py` checks this against an independent whole-run reference).
Token values are stored as float32; every integer feature is far below 2^24, so the conversion back
to the Arrow types of section 2 is lossless.

The model inputs derived from windows (aggregate vector order, token tensor layout and padding) are
defined once, in `model_input.py`, and described by the [feature spec](feature-spec.md).

```

`docs/reference/ml-jobs.md`:

```md
# Reference: ML jobs (`corvus-job`)

The feature, evaluation and training pipelines run as jobs started by the control plane
([control-plane-api.md](control-plane-api.md), section Jobs). The image `corvus-ml` (`ml/Dockerfile`)
has the entry point `corvus-job <build_features|evaluate|train>`. Code: `ml/src/corvus_ml/jobs/`.
Jobs on raw packet bytes (ADR-CORV-0008) are described in [raw-byte-tokenizer.md](raw-byte-tokenizer.md);
this page lists their parameters and extra requirements.

## 1. Contract with the runner

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Argument | the job type (`build_features`, `evaluate`, `train`); must equal `CORVUS_JOB_TYPE` if that is set |
| `CORVUS_JOB_ID`, `CORVUS_JOB_SNAPSHOT_ID` | UUIDs |
| `CORVUS_JOB_PARAMS` | JSON object, see section 3; unknown keys fail the job |
| `CORVUS_API_URL`, `CORVUS_API_TOKEN` | API base URL and bearer token; every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `X-Corvus-Job-Id` |
| `CORVUS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL`, `CORVUS_S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `CORVUS_S3_SECRET_KEY`, `CORVUS_S3_BUCKET` (default `corvus-lake`), `CORVUS_S3_REGION` (default `us-east-1`) | the lake bucket, path-style addressing, same names as the services |
| `CORVUS_JOB_SCRATCH_DIR` | optional directory for temporary files (default: the system temp dir; features can be large, mount an `emptyDir`) |
| `CORVUS_PG_DSN`, `PGPASSWORD`, `CORVUS_KEK` | **raw-byte jobs only** (`build_features` with `kind = "raw_bytes"` or `"train_tokenizer"`): read-only access to `corvus.player_keys` and the KEK that unwraps the DEKs. The role needs `SELECT` on `corvus.player_keys`; the values are scrubbed from job messages |
| `CORVUS_OPTUNA_STORAGE` | optional Optuna storage URL for `params.tune` (default: a SQLite file in the job's scratch dir) |

Exit code 0: succeeded. 1: the job failed (reported as `failed`). 2: the contract was violated or the
API could not be told about the state.

Status updates: `PATCH /api/v1/jobs/{id}` with `running` at the start, then `succeeded` (message and
`result`) or `failed` (message). A message is at most 500 characters and is scrubbed: the API token,
the S3 keys and anything shaped like `Bearer ...` are replaced by `***`. SIGTERM (for example the
Kubernetes deadline) is reported as `failed`. Non-finite numbers are dropped from `result`.

API calls beyond `PATCH /jobs/{id}`:

| Call | Used for |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id}` | the manifest: `files.events[].key` (object keys of the `events` files), `sessions`; `needs_rebuild` |
| `GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/files` | `raw[].key`: the live `raw` files that list a session of the snapshot (raw-byte jobs) |
| `GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/sessions?exclude_erased=true` | sessions of the snapshot, paged (`limit`, `cursor`, `next_cursor`) |
| `POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/artifacts` | registering every prefix a job wrote, right after writing it (section 2) |
| `POST /api/v1/models` | registering a trained model (not retried) |

**Shape assumed for the sessions endpoint.** Each item has `session_id` (hex, 16 bytes), `pseudonym`
(hex, 32 bytes), `started_at` (ISO 8601), `segments` (`[{"segment": 0, "game_context": "pvp"}]`),
`client_protocol` (integer or `null`, `sessions.client_protocol`; the raw-byte build takes the protocol
token from it, a missing value gives `[PROTO_OTHER]` and is counted) and optionally `labels` (`[{"label": "cheat", "source": "honeypot", "confidence": 1.0, "valid_from": null,
"valid_to": null}]`) and `erased`. Sessions flagged `erased` are skipped by the job even if the API
returned them, and sessions that are not in the manifest's `sessions` list are ignored. A missing
pseudonym keeps the session out of evaluation (windows without a pseudonym are dropped there).

## 2. Artefact layout (below the bucket root)

```
features/<snapshot_id>/windows/part-*.parquet
features/<snapshot_id>/window_tokens/part-*.parquet
features/<snapshot_id>/feature_spec.json
features/<snapshot_id>/sessions.parquet      session_id, pseudonym (hex), started_at
features/<snapshot_id>/labels.parquet        session_id, label, source, confidence, valid_from, valid_to
features/<snapshot_id>/build.json            written last: marks a complete build
reports/<snapshot_id>/<job_id>/report.json, report.md
models/<name>/<version>/model.onnx           calibrated, single output "score"
models/<name>/<version>/feature_spec.json
models/<name>/<version>/calibration.json
models/<name>/<version>/model_card.json
models/<name>/<version>/evaluation.json     the candidate's entry of report.json
```

A raw-byte build writes `features/<snapshot_id>/raw/` instead (tokenizer, feature spec, packet table,
sessions, labels, `build.json`; section 4 of [raw-byte-tokenizer.md](raw-byte-tokenizer.md)); a
`train_tokenizer` job writes `tokenizers/<snapshot_id>/<job_id>/{tokenizer.json,feature_spec.json}`.
Raw-byte models additionally upload `models/<name>/<version>/tokenizer.json`.

**Register what you write.** `features/<snapshot_id>/raw/` holds tokenised payloads, which are personal data derived from
`raw`. Right after writing a prefix (and, for the feature builds, after its `build.json` marker) a job calls
`POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/artifacts` with `{"kind", "s3_prefix", "contains_raw"}` (`s3_prefix` ends with `/`):

| Job | `kind` | `s3_prefix` | `contains_raw` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build_features`, `raw_bytes` | `raw_features` | `features/<snapshot_id>/raw/` | `true` |
| `build_features`, aggregate | `window_features`, `window_tokens` | `features/<snapshot_id>/windows/`, `features/<snapshot_id>/window_tokens/` | `false` |
| `build_features`, `train_tokenizer` | `tokenizer` | `tokenizers/<snapshot_id>/<job_id>/` | `false` |

Erasure and the raw retention then delete the prefix; see [data-lake.md](data-lake.md) section 7 and
[control-plane-api.md](control-plane-api.md). `201` is a new registration, `200` a repeat (a repeated call is safe and
is retried like a read). **`409`** means an erasure invalidated the snapshot's raw-derived artefacts after the job
started: the job deletes the prefix it just wrote and fails with "an erasure invalidated the raw-derived artefacts of
this snapshot while the job ran; <prefix> was deleted. Start a new job to rebuild". Other errors fail the job as well.

A new `build_features` job replaces `features/<snapshot_id>/` completely (the raw-byte build only its `raw/` prefix). The windows and tokens
tables are those of [features.md](features.md); the same code builds them offline and online.

## 3. Jobs and parameters

**`build_features`** reads the `events` files of the snapshot's manifest (explicit file list, no
directory scan) and the sessions from the API. It reads a few sessions per task and Arrow batches,
so memory stays bounded; the number of worker processes is at most the CPU limit of the cgroup.

| Param | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `game_context` / `game_contexts` | all | only segments in these contexts |
| `window`, `overlap`, `max_duration_s`, `min_frames`, `dt_edges_ms` | as `corvus-features` | windowing, recorded in `feature_spec.json` |
| `group_size` | 4 | sessions per task (memory knob) |
| `workers` | cgroup limit | upper bound; never above the cgroup limit |
| `strict` | `false` | refuse a snapshot with `needs_rebuild`, see below |

**`needs_rebuild`.** `GET /snapshots/{id}` flags a snapshot whose raw-derived artefacts an erasure deleted. A feature
build is the way to recreate them, so by default (`strict` false, for all `build_features` kinds) the job only logs a
warning and builds. With `"strict": true` it fails before reading any data and writes nothing.

**`build_features` with `kind = "raw_bytes"`** reads the `events` and `raw` files of the snapshot, decrypts
the payloads, trains the tokenizer (unless `tokenizer_prefix` points at a trained one) and tokenizes all
sessions. Sessions whose player has no DEK (erased) are skipped; the result counts them
(`sessions_crypto_shredded`). `raw` files come from the `raw` list of `GET /snapshots/{id}/files`, so no partition is scanned; an empty
list means the snapshot has no raw files (the job fails). Only if the API does not send the field (an older
version) the job logs a warning and falls back to `manifest.files.raw`, else to the `lake/raw/date=...`
partitions of the sessions' start dates. Parameters (all optional): `kind` (`aggregate` default, `raw_bytes`,
`train_tokenizer`), `strict` (see below), `game_context(s)`, `group_size` (4), `vocab_size` (4096), `min_frequency` (2),
`train_bytes_per_payload` (256), `max_train_payloads`, `max_train_bytes`, `tokenizer_sessions` (2000),
`tokenizer_prefix`, `dt_buckets`, `dt_min_ms`, `dt_max_ms`, `protocols`, `packet_type_max`,
`max_tokens_per_packet` (48), `proto_mode` and the window defaults recorded in the spec (`window_seconds`,
`stride_seconds`, `max_packets`, `overflow`, `min_packets`, `macro_window_seconds`). The build runs in one
process (decryption and tokenization are not parallelised).

**`evaluate`** needs a complete feature build and runs `corvus-eval` on it ([evaluate-models.md](../how-to/evaluate-models.md));
it uploads the reports and registers nothing. **`train`** does the same, then for each game context
takes the best usable candidate (highest `select_by` on the test split, ties by lower p99 latency;
the ONNX parity check must pass), uploads its artefacts and registers the model.

| Param | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates` | `["isolation_forest", "gradient_boosting"]` | list of names or `{name: {hyperparameters}}`; `raw_hier_classifier` / `raw_hier_anomaly` need the raw build and cannot be mixed with the others |
| `game_context` / `game_contexts` | all | contexts to evaluate |
| `unlabelled` | `exclude` | or `assume_legit` |
| `label_sources`, `min_confidence` | all, 0 | which labels count (for example `["honeypot", "staff_verdict"]`) |
| `seed`, `threads`, `seq_len`, `split`, `fpr_targets`, `learning_curve`, `benchmark` | as `eval.toml` | `threads` at most 8 |
| `calibration` | `auto` | `isotonic`, `platt`, `ecdf`; `none` is refused |
| `select_by` | `recall@fpr0.1pct` | metric that picks the candidate |
| `tune` | off | `true` or an object (`trials`, `timeout_s`, `storage`, `study_name`, `tune_windows`, `space`): an Optuna study per tunable candidate before the evaluation, see section 8 of [raw-byte-tokenizer.md](raw-byte-tokenizer.md). The API has no `tune` job type, so a search is an `evaluate` or `train` job with this parameter; the result lists `best_params` per candidate |
| `window_seconds`, `stride_seconds`, `max_packets`, `overflow`, `min_packets`, `macro_window_seconds`, `max_windows` | from the build | raw-byte candidates only: override the window configuration of the raw build (`max_windows` 200 000 caps the dataset); refused for other candidates |
| `model_name`, `version`, `domain` (`train`) | candidate name, `<snapshot8>-<job8>`, `general` | registry fields; the registered name is `<model_name>-<game_context>` |

## 4. Output semantics and calibration

Every exported model outputs a calibrated, probability-like score in [0, 1] in the single output
`score` (float32, shape `[batch]`); the calibration is part of the graph, nothing else has to be
applied. Supervised candidates: isotonic regression or Platt scaling on the validation split
(estimate of P(cheating)). Unsupervised candidates: the empirical CDF of the validation windows
that are legit (or assumed legit), so 0.99 means "higher than 99 % of legit windows". Details and
limits: [evaluate-models.md](../how-to/evaluate-models.md#calibration). `model_card.json` records the
candidate, the calibration (`method`, `n_fit`, `fit_on`), snapshot and job, `created_at`, the
metrics and `output_semantics` (`onnx_output`, `range`, `meaning`, `post_processing`).

## 5. Model registration

`POST /models` with `name`, `version`, `candidate_type`, `game_context`, `domain`, `snapshot_id`,
`metrics` and `onnx_key` (`models/<name>/<version>/model.onnx`); the stage is `registered`.
`candidate_type` is `<candidate>_calibrated` (for example `isolation_forest_calibrated`), because
the graph differs from the raw scikit-learn graphs: see section 6.

Metrics (the test split of the chosen candidate): `roc_auc`, `pr_auc`, `recall_at_fpr_1pct`,
`recall_at_fpr_0_1pct` (the quality gate's name for `recall@fpr0.1pct`), their `_player_max` /
`_player_mean` variants, `resolved_at_fpr_*` (1 = the split resolves the operating point), `ece`
(supervised), `p50_latency_ms`, `p99_latency_ms`, `mean_latency_ms`, `batch_throughput_wps`,
`peak_rss_mb`, `model_size_kb`, `n_params`, `fit_seconds`, `test_windows`, `test_cheat_windows`.
Without latency (`benchmark.enabled = false`) the promotion to `enforce` fails closed.

## 6. What the scorer relies on

`corvus_services.scoring.models.scores_from_outputs` chooses how to read a graph by `candidate_type`:
`isolation_forest` and `gradient_boosting` use output 1 of the raw scikit-learn graph, anything else
the first output, clipped to [0, 1]. Calibrated graphs have one output, so they are registered with
the type `<candidate>_calibrated`, which takes the generic branch and works without a change.
Recommended follow-up in the services: decide by `output_semantics` in `model_card.json` (or by the
output name `score`) instead of by candidate type, and drop the clip once all models are calibrated.

```

`docs/reference/plugin-api.md`:

```md
# Reference: Corvus plugin API (v1)

The Corvus Velocity plugin exposes the latest model scores of online players to other Velocity plugins through the
`corvus-api` module (package `net.onelitefeather.corvus.api`, plain Java 21+, no dependencies).

## Decision aids, not verdicts

- A score is a probability-like model output in [0, 1]; higher means more likely cheating.
- **Only `ENFORCE` scores are meant to drive automated actions** in other plugins. `CANARY` scores are
  informational. `SHADOW` scores are never exposed: the scoring service does not publish them and the plugin
  drops them if they arrive anyway.
- Corvus itself **never sanctions players**. What happens with a score is the decision of the plugin that reads
  it. Prefer the smoothed score and a minimum `windows()` over a single window score, and keep a human in the loop
  for anything irreversible.

## Depending on `corvus-api`

The API classes are packaged unrelocated inside the Corvus plugin jar, so other plugins compile against the API
and use the classes of the running Corvus plugin at runtime. Do not shade `corvus-api` into your plugin.

```kotlin
dependencies {
    compileOnly("net.onelitefeather.corvus:corvus-api:<version>")
}
```

Publishing the artifact is not set up yet (open point); until then use `./gradlew :api:jar` and depend on
`api/build/libs/corvus-api-<version>.jar` as a file, or on the Corvus plugin jar with `compileOnly(files(...))`.

Declare the dependency so Velocity loads Corvus first. The plugin id is `corvus`:

```java
@Plugin(id = "my-plugin", name = "My Plugin", version = "1.0.0",
        dependencies = {@Dependency(id = "corvus")})
public final class MyPlugin { ... }
```

Use `optional = true` if your plugin also works without Corvus and guard every access with
`CorvusProvider.find()`.

## Lookup

Velocity has no service registry, so the API is looked up through a static holder:

```java
CorvusApi api = CorvusProvider.get();            // throws IllegalStateException if Corvus is not started
Optional<CorvusApi> maybe = CorvusProvider.find(); // empty instead of throwing
```

The provider is filled when Corvus handles `ProxyInitializeEvent` (so read it in your own
`ProxyInitializeEvent` handler or later, with the `@Dependency` above) and cleared on shutdown. The API object is
available even when scoring is disabled; it simply never has scores.

## Reading scores

```java
Optional<PlayerScore> latest = api.latestScore(player.getUniqueId(), "pvp");
Collection<PlayerScore> all = api.latestScores(player.getUniqueId());

latest.filter(s -> s.stage() == ScoreStage.ENFORCE)
      .filter(s -> s.windows() >= 5 && s.smoothedScore() > 0.9f)
      .ifPresent(s -> notifyStaff(player, s));   // a decision aid for staff, not an automatic ban
```

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| `latestScore(UUID, String gameContext)` | the most recent score of the player in that game context (any domain) |
| `latestScores(UUID)` | snapshot with the latest score per (game context, domain); empty if none |
| `registerScoreListener(ScoreListener)` | `Registration`; call `unregister()` when your plugin shuts down |

`PlayerScore` is an immutable record: `player`, `gameContext`, `domain`, `score`, `smoothedScore`, `windows`
(number of windows behind the smoothed score), `modelName`, `modelVersion`, `stage` (`CANARY` or `ENFORCE`),
`scoredAt`.

Scores only exist for players that are online on this proxy and are forgotten when they disconnect. The latest
score per (player, game context, domain) is decided by `scoredAt`; a late older score never replaces a newer one.

### Listeners

```java
CorvusApi.Registration reg = api.registerScoreListener(score -> { /* light work */ });
```

- Listeners run asynchronously on Corvus worker threads (`scores.listener_threads`, default 2), never on Netty
  threads, Velocity event threads or the NATS dispatcher.
- A bounded queue (`scores.listener_queue`, default 1024) sits in front of the workers. When it is full, updates
  are dropped (the latest value is still readable through `latestScore`).
- An exception in one listener is caught and logged (at most once a minute) and does not affect other listeners.
  Do not block in a listener; hand long work to your own executor.

## How scores reach the plugin

When `sink.type = "nats"` (or `scores.enabled = true`) the plugin subscribes (core NATS) to `corvus.score.v1.>`
(`scores.subject`), decodes `corvus.score.v1.Score` and maps its `player_pseudonym` to an online player. For that
it computes the HMAC pseudonym (same key as capture) of every player on login and caches it until they
disconnect. Scores for players that are not online on this proxy and scores of stage `SHADOW` are ignored. Without
the pseudonym key, scoring is disabled with a warning. See `docs/reference/data-lake.md` section 6 for the
producer side and `deploy/pilot/proxy/corvus-config.toml` for the config keys.

The command `/corvus score <player>` (permission `corvus.admin`) prints the latest scores of an online player.

## Partitioned capture subjects

Capture envelopes are published to `<nats.subject_prefix>.<proxy_id>.<partition>`. `partition` is the first four
bytes of the session id as a big-endian unsigned integer modulo `nats.partitions` (default 16), written as decimal
with at least two digits (`00`..`15`). With more than 100 partitions the width grows to the number of digits of
the highest partition (128 partitions give `000`..`127`). The count must be identical on all proxies and match the
scorers' filter subjects.

## Compatibility

The API follows the plugin version. Additions are made append-only (new methods have defaults); a breaking change
bumps the major version.

```

`docs/reference/pseudonym-test-vector.md`:

```md
# Reference: pseudonym test vector

The player pseudonym is computed twice: by the capture plugin (`Pseudonymizer.java`) and by the control-plane API
(`corvus_services/api/pseudonym.py`, used for UUID lookup and erasure). Both must produce identical bytes, otherwise an
erasure by UUID would silently miss the player.

## Algorithm

```
pseudonym = HMAC-SHA-256(key, uuid_bytes)
uuid_bytes = most significant 8 bytes || least significant 8 bytes, big-endian (16 bytes, RFC 4122 byte order)
key        = base64-decoded value of CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY (at least 16 bytes)
```

The UUID is hashed as its 16 raw bytes, not as text. The result is 32 bytes; the API shows it as 64 lowercase hex
characters. The key identifier (`CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY_ID`) is not part of the computation; it is stored next to the
pseudonym so that a key rotation can be detected.

## Vectors

| # | Key (hex of the raw bytes) | UUID | Pseudonym (hex) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `30313233343536373839616263646566` (`0123456789abcdef`, the key of `PseudonymizerTest`) | `11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555` (`PLAYER` in `PseudonymizerTest`) | `40642e55746eeaffde2e9de80d506b79cd3dbbc299a84da87a3812759417da84` |
| 2 | `000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f` (bytes 0 to 31) | `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` | `ff921230177d146ee8401eb82173128410002ba6f997e8e837e804407c8cdd38` |

For `CORVUS_PSEUDONYM_KEY` the keys are the base64 of the raw bytes: vector 1 is `MDEyMzQ1Njc4OWFiY2RlZg==`, vector 2 is
`AAECAwQFBgcICQoLDA0ODxAREhMUFRYXGBkaGxwdHh8=`.

Independent check with OpenSSL:

```sh
printf '11111111222233334444555555555555' | xxd -r -p | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac '0123456789abcdef' -hex
printf '00000000000000000000000000000000' | xxd -r -p \
  | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt hexkey:000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f -hex
```

## Where it is tested

- API: `services/tests/api/test_api_players.py` (`test_pseudonym_matches_the_documented_vector` and the second vector).
- Plugin: `plugin/src/test/java/net/onelitefeather/corvus/plugin/privacy/PseudonymTestVectorTest.java` loads each
  base64 key through `KeyLoader` (environment value injected) and asserts both pseudonyms above via `Pseudonymizer`.
  `PseudonymizerTest` additionally checks properties (determinism, length, no raw UUID bytes).

`docs/reference/raw-byte-tokenizer.md`:

```md
# Reference: raw-byte tokenizer and hierarchical model

ADR-CORV-0008 decides that the model input is the tokenised raw packet bytes. This page is the
contract of that path: how the bytes are read, how they become token ids, how windows are cut, what
the model is, what the exported artefacts contain and what a scorer has to do to feed the model.
Code: `ml/src/corvus_ml/raw/` (reader, tokenizer, windows, model), `ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/` (candidates,
tuning) and `ml/src/corvus_ml/jobs/raw_job.py`.

Everything here is additive: the aggregate and token-sequence models of [features.md](features.md)
and [feature-spec.md](feature-spec.md) are unchanged.

## 1. Pipeline

```
lake events + raw ──decrypt──> frames of a session ──BPE──> packet table (Parquet, in S3)
                                                              │ windows (seconds, stride, caps)
                                                              v
        ONNX (score) <──export── model <──pretrain/finetune── token tensor (batch, [macro,] P, T+1)
```

1. **Read.** `raw` rows are decrypted and joined with `events` on (`session_id`, `seq`).
2. **Train the tokenizer** on payload prefixes of a session sample (step `train_tokenizer`).
3. **Tokenize** every frame once into the packet table. It does not depend on the window settings.
4. **Cut windows** from the packet table when a model is evaluated or trained, so `window_seconds`,
   `stride_seconds` and `max_packets` can be tuned without reading the encrypted data again.
5. **Pretrain / train / tune / export** (sections 6 to 9).

## 2. Reading raw bytes

Payloads are AES-256-GCM encrypted with the player's DEK; the AAD is `session_id || seq` (8 bytes
big-endian); see [data-lake.md](data-lake.md). `corvus_ml.raw.crypto` repeats the services' algorithm
(the ML package must not depend on `corvus_services`); `tests/test_raw_crypto.py` checks it against
vectors computed with `corvus_services.crypto`.

The wrapped DEKs are not available through the control-plane API, so the port
`corvus_ml.raw.keys.DekProvider` has an adapter that reads them directly:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Table | `corvus.player_keys` (`pseudonym`, `dek_wrapped`), read-only `SELECT ... WHERE pseudonym = ANY(...)` |
| `CORVUS_PG_DSN`, `PGPASSWORD` | the connection (same names as the services) |
| `CORVUS_KEK` | base64 KEK (32 bytes); unwraps `nonce(12) \|\| AES-GCM(dek)` with the pseudonym as AAD |
| Permission | the job's database role needs `SELECT` on `corvus.player_keys` and nothing else |

All three values are scrubbed from job messages. A pseudonym without a `player_keys` row is an
**erased** player: its sessions are skipped without a message and counted
(`sessions_crypto_shredded`). A frame that does not decrypt (wrong key, tampered ciphertext) is
treated as a frame without payload and counted (`decrypt_failures`). Sessions without a pseudonym
cannot be decrypted (`sessions_without_pseudonym`). Frames without a `raw` row (privacy-stripped
types, clientbound frames outside the allowlist, empty payloads) keep their header tokens.

Sessions come from `GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/sessions`. The raw-byte build additionally reads
`client_protocol` (integer, optional) of each item for the protocol token; see
[ml-jobs.md](ml-jobs.md). The live `raw` files come from `raw` of `GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/files`
(found through `lake_file_sessions`, compaction replacements followed); only without that field does
the job fall back to the `lake/raw/date=...` partitions of the days the snapshot's sessions started on.

## 3. Token layout

Ids below `n_special` are reserved; byte-level BPE tokens follow. The layout is determined by five
parameters stored in the feature spec (`dt_buckets` 16, `dt_min_ms` 0.5, `dt_max_ms` 5000,
`protocols`, `packet_type_max` 255).

| Ids (in order) | Tokens |
|---|---|
| 0 to 4 | `[PAD]` `[MASK]` `[CLS]` `[SEP]` `[UNK]` |
| 5 to 7 | `[DIR_SB]` `[DIR_CB]` `[DIR_OTHER]` (serverbound, clientbound, other) |
| 8, 9 | `[TRUNC]` `[NOPAYLOAD]` |
| 10 to 12 | `[PROTO_OTHER]` `[DT_NONE]` `[PKT_OTHER]` |
| next `dt_buckets` | `[DT_0]` ... `[DT_<n-1>]`: log-spaced buckets of the gap to the previous frame of the segment |
| next `len(protocols)` | `[PROTO_<v>]` for the known protocol versions (default 47, 340, 754, 758, 762 to 771); anything else, or none: `[PROTO_OTHER]` |
| next `packet_type_max` | `[PKT_1]` ... `[PKT_<max>]`: one token per Corvus packet type id (`vocabulary.json`, ids 1 to 228 today); ids above the maximum or 0: `[PKT_OTHER]` |

The vocabulary is append-only, so existing ids keep their token. `packet_type_max` defaults to 255 so
the tokenizer does not have to be retrained when types are added; the image does not need
`vocabulary.json`.

**Packet row** (one frame, at most `max_tokens_per_packet`, default 48, ids; the rest is `[PAD]`):

```
[DIR_*] [PKT_<id>] [DT_<bucket>] [PROTO_<v>]? <payload BPE tokens...> [TRUNC]? [SEP]
[DIR_*] [PKT_<id>] [DT_<bucket>] [PROTO_<v>]? [NOPAYLOAD] [SEP]
```

- `[DT_*]` is `[DT_NONE]` for the first frame of a segment, otherwise the bucket of the gap in ms.
- `[PROTO_*]` position is `proto_mode`: `first` (first packet of every window, default), `every`, `none`.
- `[NOPAYLOAD]`: the frame has no payload row (stripped, dropped or empty). The header still counts.
- `[TRUNC]`: `payload_original_size` is larger than the recorded bytes (the plugin cut the payload at
  2048), **or** the payload has more BPE tokens than fit into the row. The model cannot tell the two
  apart; both mean "there is more than you see".
- At most `max_tokens_per_packet - 3 - 2` payload tokens fit (`- 3` header, `- 2` flag and `[SEP]`);
  with a protocol token one less, and a payload that no longer fits is cut and flagged `[TRUNC]`.

### Byte tokens

Payload byte `b` is mapped to the character `chr(0x100 + b)` and fed to a Hugging Face `tokenizers`
BPE model without normalizer or pre-tokenizer, so merges may span any bytes and decoding is exact
(`RawTokenizer.decode(encode(x)) == x` for all byte strings, tested). The characters never collide with
the ASCII spelling of the reserved tokens, so a payload that contains the text `[PAD]` cannot forge
one. The 256 single-byte tokens come right after the reserved ids; merges follow.

Training (`TokenizerConfig`): `vocab_size` 4096 (at most 32767; ids are stored as `int16`),
`min_frequency` 2, only the first `train_bytes_per_payload` (256) bytes of each payload, at most
`max_train_payloads` (2 000 000) payloads and `max_train_bytes` (256 MiB), whichever comes first. The
iterator is streamed, so memory is bounded by the number of distinct payload prefixes. Training is
deterministic for the same payloads in the same order (the job samples sessions evenly from the
sorted session ids). `tokenizer.json` is written compactly and hashed (SHA-256) into the spec.

## 4. Artefacts

Written by `build_features` with `kind = "raw_bytes"` below `features/<snapshot_id>/raw/`
(the aggregate build in `features/<snapshot_id>/` is not touched):

```
raw/tokenizer.json            the trained tokenizer (hash in feature_spec.json)
raw/feature_spec.json         kind raw_bytes, see section 9
raw/packets/part-*.parquet    packet table
raw/sessions.parquet          session_id, pseudonym (hex), started_at, client_protocol
raw/labels.parquet            as for the aggregate build
raw/build.json                written last: marks a complete build
```

Packet table (one row per frame in a segment with a game context): `session_id` fixed_size_binary(16),
`segment` uint32, `seq` uint64, `offset_nanos` uint64, `direction` uint8, `packet_type` uint32,
`dt_id` int16 (token id), `trunc` bool, `nopayload` bool, `tokens` list&lt;int16&gt; (payload BPE ids),
`game_context` string. `kind = "train_tokenizer"` writes only `tokenizer.json` and
`feature_spec.json` to `tokenizers/<snapshot_id>/<job_id>/`; a later build reuses them with
`tokenizer_prefix` (a tokenizer trained once can serve several snapshots).

## 5. Windows

Per (session, segment), never across segments:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `window_seconds` | 10 | length of a window |
| `stride_seconds` | 5 | distance between window starts (the grid is anchored at the first packet of the segment) |
| `max_packets` | 1024 | packets per window; on overflow `overflow = "recent"` keeps the newest, `"uniform"` an evenly spaced subsample |
| `min_packets` | 8 | windows with fewer packets are dropped |
| `macro_window_seconds` | none | hierarchy over minutes: this many seconds of consecutive windows form one macro window; needs `stride_seconds == window_seconds` |

A partial window at the end of a segment is kept only if it contains packets that no earlier window
contained. A segment shorter than one window gives one window. In a macro window a missing window
(too few packets) stays padding; the second-level model ignores it.

**Model input**: one float32 array `(batch, [macro,] packets, max_tokens_per_packet + 1)`. Channels
`0 .. T-1` are token ids (exact in float32; `0` = `[PAD]`, a packet whose first token is `[PAD]`
is padding), the last channel is the packet time in seconds since the window start.
`corvus_ml.raw.windows.to_input` builds it. Windows are padded to the largest packet count in the
data; the exported graph accepts any packet count.

## 6. Model

`corvus_ml.raw.model` (PyTorch, CPU, ONNX opset 17), MEGABYTE-style:

1. **Local encoder** per packet: token embedding plus learned position, `local_layers` (1) small
   transformer blocks (`local_type = "cnn"` uses two 1D convolutions instead) over the packet's tokens,
   masked mean pooling. The embeddings of the three header tokens are concatenated and fused with the
   pooled vector into the **packet embedding** (`d_model`).
2. **Global transformer** (`layers` 2, `d_model` 64, `heads` 4) over `[CLS]` and the packet embeddings.
   The position of a packet is a sinusoidal encoding of its time in seconds (`time_freqs` 16 log-spaced
   periods from 10 ms to 600 s), not its index. Padding packets are masked.
3. **Head**: `[CLS]` to one logit.
4. **Second level** (`macro_window_seconds` set): the `[CLS]` vectors of the windows of a macro window
   get a learned window position, pass `macro_layers` (1) transformer blocks and are pooled (`macro_pool`
   `"attention"` or `"mean"`, missing windows masked) before the head. The packet axis and the batch axis
   are dynamic in ONNX; the macro axis is fixed.

Attention is written with matmul and softmax with an additive mask, so padded packets cannot produce
NaN and the graph uses plain operators. Extra padding packets do not change the output (tested).

| Candidate | Supervised | Output before calibration | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raw_hier_classifier` | yes | probability of cheating | BCE with the class ratio as `pos_weight`; supports macro windows |
| `raw_hier_anomaly` | no | mean masked-prediction loss of the window (higher = less predictable) | trained on legit windows with random masks; single windows only |

The anomaly score measures how unpredictable a window is for a model of legit traffic. It is not a
cheat detector by construction: a cheat that is more regular than human input (a constant cadence)
scores low. Treat it as a feature for review and compare it against labels before trusting it.

Parameters of both candidates (all optional; unknown keys are errors): `epochs` 10, `batch_size` 16,
`lr` (number or `"auto"` for the LR range test), `weight_decay` 0.01, `patience` 3, `d_model`, `layers`,
`heads`, `ffn_mult` 2, `dropout` 0.1, `local_dim` 32, `local_layers` 1, `local_type`, `local_heads` 2,
`macro_layers`, `macro_pool`, `pretrain_epochs` 0, `pretrain_lr` 1e-3, `init_from`, `checkpoint_out`,
`p_token` 0.15, `p_packet` 0.1, `first_tokens` 2, `max_masked` 2048, `score_period` 8,
`score_passes` 2. Training is AdamW with linear warmup and cosine decay, gradient clipping and early
stopping on the validation loss.

## 7. Pretraining

Objectives on unlabelled windows (all windows of the training players, labelled or not):

- **Masked byte tokens**: `p_token` of the payload tokens become `[MASK]`; they are predicted from the
  local state plus the global state of their packet (`max_masked` caps the masked tokens per batch to
  bound the logits).
- **Masked packets**: `p_packet` of the packets get `[PKT_*]` and the first `first_tokens` payload tokens
  masked; the packet type and those tokens are predicted from the global state.

`pretrain_epochs > 0` pretrains inside the classifier's `fit`; `checkpoint_out` saves the weights;
`init_from` starts a classifier from a checkpoint (the architecture keys must match, otherwise the load
fails with the list of differences). `corvus-eval pretrain` pretrains on its own and writes
`<out>/pretrain/<game_context>.pt`. A checkpoint made on single windows also initialises a macro
classifier. `raw_hier_anomaly` is itself the pretraining objective.

## 8. Hyper-parameter search

`corvus-eval tune` (or `params.tune` in an `evaluate` / `train` job) runs one Optuna study per game
context and tunable candidate (raw-byte candidates, `gru_autoencoder`, `cnn1d`): TPE sampler and median
pruner (2 startup trials, 1 warm-up epoch), fixed seed (`run.seed`), objective = best validation loss
(the loss early stopping uses; the pruner sees it per epoch). The split is by player and fixed before the
search; the test split is never touched. After the search the candidate is evaluated with the best
parameters, and the exported spec carries the best window.

| Parameter | Space |
|---|---|
| `lr` | log 3e-4 to 1e-2 |
| `weight_decay` | log 1e-4 to 1e-1 |
| `d_model` | 32, 64, 96, 128 |
| `layers` | 1 to 4 |
| `dropout` | 0 to 0.3 |
| `window_seconds` | 5, 10, 20 (stride and macro window scale with it) |
| `max_packets` | 256, 512, 1024 |
| `hidden`, `latent` (`gru_autoencoder`), `channels` (`cnn1d`) | categorical |

`[tune]` keys: `trials` 20, `timeout_s`, `storage`, `study_name`, `tune_windows` true, `space` (per
parameter `[low, high]` or a list of choices). Storage: `"memory"`, a URL, or by default
`CORVUS_OPTUNA_STORAGE`, else `sqlite:///<out>/optuna.db`. With a persistent storage an existing study is
resumed up to `trials` trials in total. The report lists the sampler, pruner, search space, every trial and
the best parameters (`report.json` and `report.md`).

## 9. Export, feature spec and model card

The exported graph is calibrated as for every other candidate: input `x`, **single output `score`**
(float32, `[batch]`, in [0, 1], nothing to apply afterwards), see [ml-jobs.md](ml-jobs.md). The calibration
is fitted on the validation split and baked into the graph; parity of the graph against PyTorch is
checked on a sample of the test windows (`parity_ok`).

`feature_spec.json` next to the model has `"version": 2` and a `raw_bytes` section inside
`model_inputs`:

```json
"raw_bytes": {
  "tokenizer": {"file": "tokenizer.json", "sha256": "…", "vocab_size": 4096, "byte_mapping": "chr(0x100 + byte)"},
  "layout": {"dt_buckets": 16, "dt_min_ms": 0.5, "dt_max_ms": 5000.0, "protocols": [47, 340, …], "packet_type_max": 255},
  "packet": {"max_tokens_per_packet": 48, "proto_mode": "first"},
  "window": {"window_seconds": 10.0, "stride_seconds": 5.0, "max_packets": 1024, "overflow": "recent",
             "min_packets": 8, "macro_window_seconds": null},
  "input": {"dtype": "float32", "shape": "(batch, [macro,] packets, max_tokens_per_packet + 1)", "channels": "…"}
}
```

`FeatureSpec.load(path, require_tokenizer=True)` checks that `tokenizer.json` next to the spec hashes to
`tokenizer.sha256` (`FeatureSpecMismatch` otherwise) and `RawTokenizer.load` that the file follows the
layout (every reserved token has its id, no extra reserved token). Version 2 makes a runtime that only
knows aggregate / token-sequence models refuse the spec instead of feeding the tensor to the wrong graph.

`model_card.json` of a raw-byte model: `input_kind: "raw_bytes"`, `tokenizer` (`file`, `sha256`), `window`,
`packet`, plus the usual fields (`candidate_type` is `<candidate>_calibrated`). `models/<name>/<version>/`
also holds `tokenizer.json`.

## 10. What the scorer has to do

`corvus-score` (`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/`) implements this; the steps below are the contract and
name where each one lives. A scorer that serves a raw-byte model must:

1. Dispatch on `model_card.input_kind == "raw_bytes"` (or `feature_spec.json` having `raw_bytes`), **not**
   on the ONNX input rank: a token-sequence model has the same rank 3.
2. Validate with `FeatureSpec.load(dir, require_tokenizer=True)` and load `tokenizer.json` with
   `corvus_ml.raw.tokenizer.RawTokenizer.load(dir, spec.raw_bytes)`. The `serve` extra contains
   `tokenizers` (a Rust wheel of a few MB).
3. Receive the **payloads**, not only the decoded events. Online, the `CaptureBatch` frames carry them;
   decode them like ingest does (`payload` and `payload_original_size` per frame) and map the frame to
   direction, packet type and time as `codec.event_row` does.
4. Keep per (session, segment) the packets of the last `window_seconds` (bounded by `max_packets` with
   the configured `overflow`), tokenize each frame once with `session_packet_table` semantics
   (`[DT_*]` from the gap to the previous frame of the segment, `[NOPAYLOAD]` / `[TRUNC]` as in section
   3), and cut windows on the same grid (`window_bounds`: anchored at the first packet of the segment,
   every `stride_seconds`).
5. Assemble the rows with `corvus_ml.raw.windows.assemble_rows` / `stream_input` (the single code path
   used by training and evaluation) and the session's `client_protocol` for `[PROTO_*]`, pad packets to the
   longest window of the micro-batch, and run the graph. The packet count may vary per call.
6. For a macro model keep the last `macro_windows` windows of the segment (gaps stay padding).
7. Use the same code, not a re-implementation: the token ids are part of the model.

How `corvus-score` does it:

| Step | Implementation |
|---|---|
| 1, 2 | `ModelManager` reads `model_card.json` first. `input_kind` `raw_bytes` (or a `raw_bytes` section in the spec) selects the raw path; a card that contradicts the spec (`agg`/`seq` with a raw spec, `raw_bytes` without one, an unknown kind) rejects the model. `FeatureSpec.load(..., require_tokenizer=True)` and `RawTokenizer.load` check the hash and the layout; a mismatch keeps the model out (reason `rejected`, not retried), all other models keep running. The ONNX input rank (3, or 4 with macro windows) and the channel count `max_tokens_per_packet + 1` are checked against the spec. |
| 3 | `scoring/raw.py: raw_frame` maps the capture `Frame` (plaintext `payload`, `payload_original_size`, direction, packet type, offset). |
| 4, 6 | `corvus_ml.raw.streaming.SegmentWindower`, one per (session, segment, distinct `RawBytesSpec`). It shares `tokenize_payloads` and `cut_window` with the offline path; `tests/test_raw_streaming.py` proves stream = batch for chunked feeds, segments, caps, protocol modes and macro windows. A window is emitted as soon as a frame at or after its end arrived; the windows that are only complete at the end of the segment follow on a new segment, the end of the session or an idle eviction. A macro window is emitted when the first window of the next group is complete (like training: disjoint groups). |
| 5 | The `[PROTO_*]` token comes from `sessions.client_protocol` (`SessionStart.client_protocol_version`, or the catalog on a lookup). The micro-batch is padded to its longest window (`scoring/raw.py: stack_inputs`). |

Memory and privacy: the windower tokenizes a frame when it arrives and keeps token ids only (int16), from the start of
the next undecided window on, so about `window_seconds + stride_seconds` of traffic; a cap
(`CORVUS_SCORE_RAW_MAX_BUFFERED_FRAMES`) bounds it. Plaintext payload bytes live for the duration of one call and are
never stored, persisted or logged. A model that appears while a segment runs starts its window grid at its first frame
(the featurizers behave the same); a frame whose `seq` does not exceed the last one (redelivery) is ignored.

Metrics: `corvus_score_model_window_max_packets{model}`, `corvus_score_model_window_seconds{model}`,
`corvus_score_model_estimated_p99_ms{model}`, `corvus_score_raw_window_packets` (packets per window handed to the
models) and `corvus_score_raw_frames_dropped_total`.

Cost: the table below was measured with default-size models (`d_model` 64, 2 global layers; random
weights, latency does not depend on them) on a 32-core development machine, ONNX Runtime CPU, one window
per call. The anomaly graph is slower because it runs the prediction heads for the masked positions.

| Packets per window | `raw_hier_classifier` 1 thread | 2 threads | `raw_hier_anomaly` 1 thread | 2 threads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 3.8 ms | 2.3 ms | 10.0 ms | 5.9 ms |
| 512 | 17.0 ms | 10.0 ms | 44.7 ms | 25.8 ms |
| 1024 | 41.9 ms (p99 47.6) | 25.6 ms | 108.7 ms | 66.9 ms |

A larger model (`d_model` 128, 4 layers) needs 68.9 ms (1 thread) for 1024 packets.

**Budget guard.** At load time the scorer estimates the p99 of a full window from `max_packets` (piecewise linear
through the 1-thread classifier points above, times 0.6 for two or more threads, times 2.6 for `raw_hier_anomaly`, times
1.15 from mean to p99; a larger model needs about 1.6 times more) and logs a warning if it exceeds
`CORVUS_SCORE_P99_BUDGET_MS` (default 10, the registry gate `CORVUS_GATE_MAX_P99_LATENCY_MS`). The model is still
served; the estimate is exported as `corvus_score_model_estimated_p99_ms`. With the default budget a classifier on one
thread stays quiet up to about 270 packets and warns at 512 (about 20 ms) and 1024. Re-measure on the
target hardware (`[benchmark] raw_packets = [128, 512, 1024]` adds this table to every report). With a
stride of 5 s one window per session every 5 s is one call; the budget is the number of concurrent
sessions times the cost of the window, so cap `max_packets` rather than the window length when CPU is
the limit.

## 11. Limits

- Memory: a window of 1024 packets by 48 tokens is 98 KiB as `int16`; the evaluation holds the whole
  dataset in memory (`max_windows` caps it, default 200 000 in jobs). Use `window_seconds` / `max_packets`
  to size it.
- The tokenizer sees what the lake keeps: serverbound play payloads and the clientbound motion allowlist,
  truncated at 2048 bytes. Chat, signs and other private types never reach it.
- `raw` has a short retention (21 days by default). A raw-byte build of an old snapshot fails with "no raw
  files"; the packet table in `features/` survives, the encrypted source does not.
- Erasure: the packet table contains tokenized payload content. It is derived data of the `raw` table and
  is deleted with it: the job registers the prefix (`POST /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/artifacts`,
  `contains_raw: true`), `corvus-compact` deletes the registered prefix when a player of the snapshot is
  erased and marks the snapshot `needs_rebuild`, and `corvus-housekeeping` deletes it with the pool's raw
  retention. A rebuild drops erased players, whose DEK is gone. The tokenizer itself is trained on a payload
  sample and contains no player identifier.
- An unregistered prefix is invisible to erasure and retention, so register every build.

```

#
# Copyright © 2015 the original authors.

# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");

# limitations under the License.
