```
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#

##############################################################################
#
#   gradlew start up script for POSIX generated by Gradle.
#
#   Important for running:
#
#   (1) You need a POSIX-compliant shell to run this script. If your /bin/sh is
#       noncompliant, but you have some other compliant shell such as ksh or
#       bash, then to run this script, type that shell name before the whole
#       command line, like:
#
#           ksh gradlew
#
#       Busybox and similar reduced shells will NOT work, because this script
#       requires all of these POSIX shell features:
#         * functions;
#         * expansions «$var», «${var}», «${var:-default}», «${var+SET}»,
#           «${var#prefix}», «${var%suffix}», and «$( cmd )»;
#         * compound commands having a testable exit status, especially «case»;
#         * various built-in commands including «command», «set», and «ulimit».
#
#   Important for patching:
#
#   (2) This script targets any POSIX shell, so it avoids extensions provided
#       by Bash, Ksh, etc; in particular arrays are avoided.
#
#       The "traditional" practice of packing multiple parameters into a
#       space-separated string is a well documented source of bugs and security
#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.
#
#       Where the inherited environment variables (DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS,
#       and GRADLE_OPTS) rely on word-splitting, this is performed explicitly;
#       see the in-line comments for details.
#
#       There are tweaks for specific operating systems such as AIX, CygWin,
#       Darwin, MinGW, and NonStop.
#
#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/3d91ce3b8caaf77ad09f381f43615b715b53f72c/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac



# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi
        # Roll the args list around exactly as many times as the number of
        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.
        #
        # NB: a `for` loop captures its iteration list before it begins, so
        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -jar "$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar" \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"
```

`ml/Dockerfile`:

```
# Image of the ML jobs the control plane starts (build_features, evaluate, train).
# Build context is the repository root (the proto sources live in ./proto):
#   docker build -f ml/Dockerfile -t corvus-ml .
# Run (the control plane's runner sets the environment, see docs/reference/ml-jobs.md):
#   docker run --rm -e CORVUS_JOB_ID=... corvus-ml train
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.24 AS uv

FROM python:3.13-slim AS build
COPY --from=uv /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
# The venv is created where it runs: console scripts carry the interpreter path of the build.
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv
WORKDIR /build/ml
COPY ml/pyproject.toml ml/uv.lock ml/README.md ./
# Dependencies first, for layer caching: the eval extra (CPU-only torch from the pytorch-cpu index
# pinned in uv.lock, scikit-learn, ONNX, ONNX Runtime) plus protoc (proto group, build time only).
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra eval --group proto --no-install-project
COPY proto /build/proto
COPY ml/scripts scripts
COPY ml/src src
# Generate the protobuf bindings, then install the project without the proto group: uv removes
# grpcio-tools again, so the runtime has no protoc.
RUN PYTHON=/opt/venv/bin/python scripts/gen_proto.sh \
 && uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra eval --no-editable

FROM python:3.13-slim
RUN groupadd --system --gid 10001 corvus \
 && useradd --system --uid 10001 --gid corvus --no-create-home corvus
COPY --from=build /opt/venv /opt/venv
# HOME must be writable for the non-root user (ONNX Runtime writes a telemetry id there).
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    HOME=/tmp
USER 10001:10001
# Temporary files (feature builds, exports) go to the system temp dir; point
# CORVUS_JOB_SCRATCH_DIR at a mounted volume for large snapshots.
ENTRYPOINT ["corvus-job"]

```

`ml/README.md`:

```md
# corvus-ml

Python tooling for Corvus: the pilot capture analyzer, the feature stage and the model evaluation
harness.

The core install needs only numpy, pyarrow and protobuf; grpcio-tools (protoc) is a build-time
tool in the dependency group `proto` and not installed at runtime.
torch, scikit-learn, onnx and skl2onnx (plus tokenizers, optuna, cryptography and psycopg for the
raw-byte models) live in the optional extra `eval`; ONNX Runtime is in `eval` and in `serve`
(`serve` also has `tokenizers`). In this checkout `uv sync` installs the `eval` extra through the `dev` group, so
tests and CI (`uv sync --locked`) cover everything. Outside the repo:

```
pip install corvus-ml                # features, pilot analyzer, FeatureSpec, model-input adapter
pip install 'corvus-ml[eval]'        # + corvus-eval (training, ONNX export, benchmark)
pip install 'corvus-ml[serve]'       # + onnxruntime for the scoring service
uv sync --no-default-groups          # in this checkout: core install only
```

```
uv sync
uv run corvus-pilot analyze <captures-dir> [--json out.json] [--vocabulary vocabulary.json]
    [--payload-policy none|serverbound|all] [--denylist extra.json] [--workers N]
uv run corvus-features build --events <lake/events> --segments <segments.parquet|csv> --out <dir>
    [--context pvp] [--window 256] [--overlap 0.5] [--workers N]
uv run corvus-job <build_features|evaluate|train>   # what the control plane starts, see below
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
```

Models on tokenised raw packet bytes (`raw_hier_classifier`, `raw_hier_anomaly`, `corvus-eval tune`):
`../docs/reference/raw-byte-tokenizer.md`.

`corvus-job` reads the job contract from the environment (`CORVUS_JOB_*`, `CORVUS_API_*`,
`CORVUS_S3_*`) and reports its status to the control plane; see
`../docs/reference/ml-jobs.md`. The container image is built from `ml/Dockerfile` with the
repository root as context:

```
docker build -f ml/Dockerfile -t corvus-ml .
```

The privacy check uses `../proto/corvus/capture/v1/vocabulary.json` (exported by the plugin) as its
denylist and payload policy by default; see `../docs/pilot.md`.

Protobuf bindings are generated from `../proto` into `src/corvus_ml/_gen/` (gitignored). In a
checkout (the `dev` group includes `proto`) that happens automatically on first import; images and
wheels get them at build time with `scripts/gen_proto.sh`, so the runtime install needs no
`grpcio-tools`. See `../docs/pilot.md` for the pilot runbook.
```

`ml/scripts/gen_proto.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generates the Python protobuf bindings for the capture schema into
# src/corvus_ml/_gen/ (gitignored). Run from anywhere: ml/scripts/gen_proto.sh
#
# Build-time step: needs protoc from the `proto` dependency group (grpcio-tools), which is not part
# of the runtime install. In a checkout corvus_ml.proto also generates the bindings on first
# import when they are missing or older than the .proto; images run this script instead.
# PYTHON selects the interpreter that has grpcio-tools (default: `uv run python`).
set -euo pipefail

ml_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
proto_dir="${CORVUS_PROTO_DIR:-${ml_dir}/../proto}"
out_dir="${ml_dir}/src/corvus_ml/_gen"

rm -rf "${out_dir}"
mkdir -p "${out_dir}"
cd "${ml_dir}"
${PYTHON:-uv run python} -m grpc_tools.protoc \
  --proto_path="${proto_dir}" \
  --python_out="${out_dir}" \
  "${proto_dir}/corvus/capture/v1/capture.proto"
echo "generated into ${out_dir}"

```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/aggregate.py`:

```py
"""Per-file aggregation of capture envelopes into a mergeable FileResult."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from google.protobuf.descriptor import Descriptor, FieldDescriptor

from corvus_ml.model import (
    UNASSIGNED,
    Agg,
    ContextAgg,
    Counters,
    FileResult,
    SegmentSummary,
    SessionSummary,
)
from corvus_ml.privacy import (
    Denylist,
    PayloadCheck,
    PrivacyFindings,
    identifier_kind,
    iter_string_fields,
)
from corvus_ml.proto import pb
from corvus_ml.reader import ReadStats, iter_envelopes, read_file


def _enum_names(enum_descriptor, prefix: str) -> dict[int, str]:
    return {v.number: v.name.removeprefix(prefix).lower() for v in enum_descriptor.values}


_DIRECTIONS = _enum_names(pb.Direction.DESCRIPTOR, "DIRECTION_")
_STATES = _enum_names(pb.ConnectionState.DESCRIPTOR, "CONNECTION_STATE_")


def _name(table: dict[int, str], number: int) -> str:
    return table.get(number) or f"unknown({number})"


def _has_strings(descriptor: Descriptor, seen: frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> bool:
    if descriptor.full_name in seen:
        return False
    seen = seen | {descriptor.full_name}
    for f in descriptor.fields:
        if f.type == FieldDescriptor.TYPE_STRING:
            return True
        if f.type == FieldDescriptor.TYPE_MESSAGE and _has_strings(f.message_type, seen):
            return True
    return False


_FRAME_HAS_STRINGS = _has_strings(pb.Frame.DESCRIPTOR)


@dataclass
class _Segment:
    context: str = UNASSIGNED
    brand: str = ""
    started_ms: int = 0
    agg: Agg = field(default_factory=Agg)
    min_offset: int | None = None
    max_offset: int | None = None
    batch_counters: Counters = field(default_factory=Counters)


@dataclass
class _Session:
    file: str
    session_id: str
    client_protocol: int = 0
    observed_protocol: int = 0
    plugin_version: str = ""
    started_ms: int = 0
    ended_ms: int = 0
    has_start: bool = False
    has_end: bool = False
    end_counters: Counters | None = None
    last_seq: int | None = None
    max_offset: int = 0
    segments: dict[int, _Segment] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def segment(self, number: int) -> _Segment:
        return self.segments.setdefault(number, _Segment())


def _counters(message) -> Counters:
    return Counters(message.dropped_queue_full, message.dropped_privacy, message.listener_errors)


def _scan_strings(message, where: str, findings: PrivacyFindings) -> None:
    for name, value in iter_string_fields(message):
        kind = identifier_kind(value)
        if kind:
            findings.add(f"{kind}_in_string_field", f"{where}.{name}")


def _record_frames(
    session: _Session,
    batch,
    denylist: Denylist,
    findings: PrivacyFindings,
    file_name: str,
    payload_check: PayloadCheck | None = None,
) -> None:
    seg = session.segment(batch.segment)
    agg = seg.agg
    agg.counters.add(_counters(batch.counters))
    seg.batch_counters.add(_counters(batch.counters))
    for frame in batch.frames:
        direction = _name(_DIRECTIONS, frame.direction)
        state = _name(_STATES, frame.state)
        size = len(frame.payload)

        agg.frames_ds[direction, state] += 1
        agg.bytes_ds[direction, state] += size
        key = (
            direction,
            state,
            frame.packet_type,
            frame.wire_packet_id if not frame.packet_type else -1,
        )
        agg.packets[key] += 1
        agg.packet_bytes[key] += size
        if size or frame.payload_original_size:
            agg.payload_frames += 1
            if frame.payload_original_size > size:
                agg.payload_truncated += 1
        event = frame.WhichOneof("event")
        if event:
            agg.events[event] += 1

        # Sequence gaps: seq must increase by exactly one within a session.
        if session.last_seq is None:
            session.last_seq = frame.seq
        else:
            expected = session.last_seq + 1
            if frame.seq > expected:
                agg.gaps.events += 1
                agg.gaps.missing_frames += frame.seq - expected
            if frame.seq >= expected:
                session.last_seq = frame.seq
            else:
                agg.gaps.out_of_order += 1

        if seg.min_offset is None or frame.offset_nanos < seg.min_offset:
            seg.min_offset = frame.offset_nanos
        if seg.max_offset is None or frame.offset_nanos > seg.max_offset:
            seg.max_offset = frame.offset_nanos
        session.max_offset = max(session.max_offset, frame.offset_nanos)

        reason = denylist.hit(direction, state, frame.packet_type, frame.wire_packet_id)
        if reason:
            findings.add(reason, f"{file_name} seq={frame.seq} {direction}/{state}")
        if payload_check:
            reason = payload_check.violation(direction, frame.packet_type, size)
            if reason:
                findings.add(
                    reason,
                    f"{file_name} seq={frame.seq} {direction}/{state} type={frame.packet_type}",
                )
        if _FRAME_HAS_STRINGS:
            _scan_strings(frame, f"{file_name}.frame", findings)


def _segment_durations(session: _Session) -> dict[int, float]:
    """Seconds spent per segment: wall-clock boundaries, falling back to frame offsets."""
    ordered = sorted(session.segments)
    session_end_s = (
        (session.ended_ms - session.started_ms) / 1000
        if session.has_end and session.started_ms and session.ended_ms
        else session.max_offset / 1e9
    )
    out: dict[int, float] = {}
    for i, number in enumerate(ordered):
        seg = session.segments[number]
        duration = 0.0
        if seg.started_ms and session.started_ms:
            start_s = (seg.started_ms - session.started_ms) / 1000
            if i + 1 < len(ordered):
                nxt = session.segments[ordered[i + 1]]
                end_s = (
                    (nxt.started_ms - session.started_ms) / 1000
                    if nxt.started_ms
                    else session_end_s
                )
            else:
                end_s = session_end_s
            duration = max(0.0, end_s - start_s)
        if duration <= 0 and seg.min_offset is not None and seg.max_offset is not None:
            duration = (seg.max_offset - seg.min_offset) / 1e9
        out[number] = duration
    return out


def _finalize(session: _Session, result: FileResult) -> None:
    durations = _segment_durations(session)
    session_agg = Agg()
    contexts: list[str] = []
    brands: list[str] = []

    batch_total = Counters()
    for seg in session.segments.values():
        batch_total.add(seg.batch_counters)
    effective = batch_total.maxed(session.end_counters) if session.end_counters else batch_total
    remainder = effective.minus(batch_total)

    ordered = sorted(session.segments)
    for i, number in enumerate(ordered):
        seg = session.segments[number]
        if i == len(ordered) - 1:
            seg.agg.counters.add(remainder)  # unattributed end-of-session counters
        duration = durations[number]
        ctx = result.contexts.setdefault(seg.context, ContextAgg())
        ctx.agg.merge(seg.agg)
        ctx.player_seconds += duration
        ctx.segments.append(
            SegmentSummary(
                session.session_id,
                number,
                seg.context,
                duration,
                seg.agg.frames,
                seg.agg.bytes,
            )
        )
        session_agg.merge(seg.agg)
        if seg.context not in contexts:
            contexts.append(seg.context)
        if seg.brand and seg.brand not in brands:
            brands.append(seg.brand)

    if session.has_start and session.started_ms and session.has_end and session.ended_ms:
        duration_s = (session.ended_ms - session.started_ms) / 1000
    else:
        duration_s = 0.0
    duration_s = max(duration_s, session.max_offset / 1e9)

    result.sessions.append(
        SessionSummary(
            session_id=session.session_id,
            file=session.file,
            client_protocol=session.client_protocol,
            observed_protocol=session.observed_protocol,
            plugin_version=session.plugin_version,
            contexts=contexts,
            brands=brands,
            duration_s=duration_s,
            complete=session.has_end,
            agg=session_agg,
            end_counters=session.end_counters,
        )
    )
    if session.has_start:
        result.versions[session.client_protocol, session.observed_protocol] += 1


def aggregate_stream(
    envelopes, name: str, denylist: Denylist, payload_check: PayloadCheck | None = None
) -> FileResult:
    """Aggregate an iterable of envelopes (one logical capture file)."""
    result = FileResult(files=1, denylist_active=denylist.active)
    sessions: dict[bytes, _Session] = {}

    def get(session_id: bytes) -> _Session:
        if session_id not in sessions:
            sessions[session_id] = _Session(file=name, session_id=session_id.hex())
        return sessions[session_id]

    for env in envelopes:
        kind = env.WhichOneof("body")
        if kind == "session_start":
            m = env.session_start
            s = get(m.session_id)
            s.has_start = True
            s.client_protocol = m.client_protocol_version
            s.observed_protocol = m.observed_protocol_version
            s.plugin_version = m.plugin_version
            s.started_ms = m.started_at_unix_millis
            _scan_strings(m, f"{name}.session_start", result.privacy)
        elif kind == "segment_start":
            m = env.segment_start
            seg = get(m.session_id).segment(m.segment)
            seg.context = m.game_context or UNASSIGNED
            seg.brand = m.client_brand
            seg.started_ms = m.started_at_unix_millis
            _scan_strings(m, f"{name}.segment_start", result.privacy)
        elif kind == "batch":
            m = env.batch
            _record_frames(get(m.session_id), m, denylist, result.privacy, name, payload_check)
        elif kind == "session_end":
            m = env.session_end
            s = get(m.session_id)
            s.has_end = True
            s.ended_ms = m.ended_at_unix_millis
            s.end_counters = _counters(m.counters)
    for session in sessions.values():
        _finalize(session, result)
    return result


def analyze_file(
    path: Path, denylist: Denylist, payload_check: PayloadCheck | None = None
) -> FileResult:
    """Aggregate one capture file (top-level so it can run in a worker process)."""
    stats = ReadStats()
    result = aggregate_stream(read_file(path, stats), path.name, denylist, payload_check)
    result.envelopes = stats.envelopes
    result.truncated_files = int(stats.truncated)
    result.corrupt_files = int(stats.corrupt)
    return result


__all__ = ["aggregate_stream", "analyze_file", "iter_envelopes"]

```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/calibration.py`:

```py
"""Score calibration: raw model output -> probability-like score in [0, 1].

Every exported model outputs a calibrated score:

* supervised candidates: isotonic regression (enough validation data) or Platt scaling on the
  validation split, so the score approximates P(cheat | window);
* unsupervised candidates: the empirical CDF of the raw scores of legit (or assumed-legit)
  validation windows, so 0.99 means "scores higher than 99 % of legit windows".

A :class:`Calibration` is either piecewise linear (isotonic, empirical CDF, identity) or a sigmoid
(Platt). Both are monotone non-decreasing, so the ranking of the raw score is preserved (isotonic
and the CDF can merge neighbouring values into ties). The same object is applied in Python
(:meth:`Calibration.apply`) and embedded into the ONNX graph
(:mod:`corvus_ml.calibration_onnx`); a test pins the two to each other.

Importing this module needs only numpy; the fit helpers import scikit-learn lazily.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

METHODS = ("auto", "isotonic", "platt", "ecdf", "none")
# Knots kept for a piecewise-linear calibration: bounds the size of the embedded ONNX constants.
MAX_KNOTS = 256
# Isotonic regression needs enough points of both classes; below this Platt scaling is used.
MIN_ISOTONIC_PER_CLASS = 20
MIN_ISOTONIC_TOTAL = 200
# Quantile levels of the empirical CDF knots: uniform plus a dense upper tail.
_ECDF_LEVELS = np.unique(
    np.concatenate(
        [
            np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 193),
            [0.9, 0.95, 0.97, 0.98, 0.99, 0.995, 0.997, 0.999, 0.9995, 0.9999],
        ]
    )
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Calibration:
    """Monotone map from a raw score to [0, 1].

    ``kind`` is ``"piecewise_linear"`` (``xs`` strictly increasing, ``ys`` non-decreasing in
    [0, 1]; constant outside ``[xs[0], xs[-1]]``) or ``"sigmoid"`` (``sigmoid(a * s + b)`` with
    ``a >= 0``). ``method`` names how it was fitted, ``fit_on`` which data it was fitted on.
    """

    method: str
    kind: str
    xs: tuple[float, ...] = ()
    ys: tuple[float, ...] = ()
    a: float = 0.0
    b: float = 0.0
    n_fit: int = 0
    fit_on: str = "validation"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.kind == "piecewise_linear":
            if len(self.xs) < 1 or len(self.xs) != len(self.ys):
                raise ValueError("piecewise_linear needs matching, non-empty xs and ys")
            if np.any(np.diff(self.xs) <= 0):
                raise ValueError("xs must be strictly increasing")
            if np.any(np.diff(self.ys) < 0) or min(self.ys) < 0.0 or max(self.ys) > 1.0:
                raise ValueError("ys must be non-decreasing and within [0, 1]")
        elif self.kind == "sigmoid":
            if self.a < 0:
                raise ValueError("a sigmoid calibration must not be decreasing (a >= 0)")
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown calibration kind {self.kind!r}")

    def apply(self, raw: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Float64 calibrated scores, same shape as ``raw``."""
        s = np.asarray(raw, dtype=np.float64)
        if self.kind == "sigmoid":
            z = np.clip(self.a * s + self.b, -60.0, 60.0)
            return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-z))
        return np.interp(s, self.xs, self.ys)

    # --- serialisation -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        out: dict[str, Any] = {
            "method": self.method,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "n_fit": self.n_fit,
            "fit_on": self.fit_on,
        }
        if self.kind == "sigmoid":
            out.update(a=self.a, b=self.b)
        else:
            out.update(xs=list(self.xs), ys=list(self.ys))
        return out

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Calibration:
        return cls(
            method=str(raw["method"]),
            kind=str(raw["kind"]),
            xs=tuple(float(v) for v in raw.get("xs", ())),
            ys=tuple(float(v) for v in raw.get("ys", ())),
            a=float(raw.get("a", 0.0)),
            b=float(raw.get("b", 0.0)),
            n_fit=int(raw.get("n_fit", 0)),
            fit_on=str(raw.get("fit_on", "validation")),
        )


def identity(n_fit: int = 0, fit_on: str = "none") -> Calibration:
    """Clip a score that already lives in [0, 1] (probability outputs without usable data)."""
    return Calibration(
        "identity", "piecewise_linear", (0.0, 1.0), (0.0, 1.0), n_fit=n_fit, fit_on=fit_on
    )


def _thin(xs: np.ndarray, ys: np.ndarray, limit: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """At most ``limit`` knots, evenly spread over the knot index; ends are kept."""
    if len(xs) <= limit:
        return xs, ys
    keep = np.unique(np.linspace(0, len(xs) - 1, limit).round().astype(int))
    return xs[keep], ys[keep]


def _strictly_increasing(xs: np.ndarray, ys: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Collapse equal ``xs`` (keeping the highest ``ys``) and drop non-finite knots."""
    ok = np.isfinite(xs) & np.isfinite(ys)
    xs, ys = xs[ok], ys[ok]
    order = np.argsort(xs, kind="stable")
    xs, ys = xs[order], ys[order]
    last = np.concatenate((xs[1:] != xs[:-1], [True]))
    return xs[last], np.maximum.accumulate(ys)[last]


def _piecewise(method: str, xs: np.ndarray, ys: np.ndarray, n_fit: int, fit_on: str) -> Calibration:
    xs, ys = _strictly_increasing(xs, np.clip(ys, 0.0, 1.0))
    xs, ys = _thin(xs, ys, MAX_KNOTS)
    return Calibration(
        method,
        "piecewise_linear",
        tuple(xs.tolist()),
        tuple(ys.tolist()),
        n_fit=n_fit,
        fit_on=fit_on,
    )


def fit_isotonic(raw: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, fit_on: str = "validation") -> Calibration:
    """Isotonic regression of the cheat label on the raw score (linear between its thresholds)."""
    from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression

    s = np.asarray(raw, dtype=np.float64)
    iso = IsotonicRegression(y_min=0.0, y_max=1.0, out_of_bounds="clip").fit(s, y)
    return _piecewise(
        "isotonic",
        np.asarray(iso.X_thresholds_, dtype=np.float64),
        np.asarray(iso.y_thresholds_, dtype=np.float64),
        len(s),
        fit_on,
    )


def fit_platt(raw: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, fit_on: str = "validation") -> Calibration | None:
    """Platt scaling ``sigmoid(a * s + b)``; None if the fit is decreasing (not a calibration)."""
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

    s = np.asarray(raw, dtype=np.float64)
    mean, std = float(s.mean()), float(s.std())
    if not np.isfinite(std) or std < 1e-12:
        std = 1.0
    z = ((s - mean) / std).reshape(-1, 1)
    lr = LogisticRegression(C=1e4, max_iter=1000).fit(z, y)
    slope = float(lr.coef_[0, 0]) / std
    if slope < 0:
        return None
    intercept = float(lr.intercept_[0]) - float(lr.coef_[0, 0]) * mean / std
    return Calibration("platt", "sigmoid", a=slope, b=intercept, n_fit=len(s), fit_on=fit_on)


def fit_ecdf(legit_raw: np.ndarray, fit_on: str = "validation") -> Calibration:
    """Empirical CDF of the raw scores of legit windows: ``P(legit score <= s)``."""
    s = np.asarray(legit_raw, dtype=np.float64)
    s = s[np.isfinite(s)]
    if s.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("an empirical CDF needs at least one legit score")
    return _piecewise("ecdf", np.quantile(s, _ECDF_LEVELS), _ECDF_LEVELS.copy(), s.size, fit_on)


def fit_calibration(
    method: str,
    supervised: bool,
    val_raw: np.ndarray,
    val_cheat: np.ndarray | None,
    fallback_legit_raw: np.ndarray | None = None,
    bounded: bool = False,
) -> Calibration:
    """Fit the calibration for one candidate.

    ``val_raw`` are the raw scores of the validation windows the candidate may be calibrated on
    (labelled windows for supervised, legit windows for unsupervised candidates) and
    ``val_cheat`` their 0/1 cheat label (supervised only). ``fallback_legit_raw`` (unsupervised)
    is used when the validation split has no legit window. ``bounded`` says that the raw score
    is already a probability in [0, 1]: it is then passed through (clipped) when there is no
    usable calibration data. ``method`` is one of :data:`METHODS`; ``auto`` picks as described in
    the module docstring.
    """
    if method not in METHODS:
        raise ValueError(f"calibration must be one of {METHODS}, got {method!r}")
    if method == "none":
        raise ValueError("calibration 'none' means: do not call fit_calibration")
    if not supervised:
        if method not in ("auto", "ecdf"):
            raise ValueError(f"unsupervised candidates are calibrated with 'ecdf', not {method!r}")
        if len(val_raw):
            return fit_ecdf(val_raw)
        if fallback_legit_raw is not None and len(fallback_legit_raw):
            log.warning("no legit validation windows; calibrating on the training windows")
            return fit_ecdf(fallback_legit_raw, fit_on="train")
        raise ValueError("no legit windows to calibrate an unsupervised candidate on")
    if method == "ecdf":
        raise ValueError("supervised candidates are calibrated with 'isotonic' or 'platt'")
    y = np.asarray(val_cheat if val_cheat is not None else [], dtype=np.int64)
    pos, neg = int((y == 1).sum()), int((y == 0).sum())
    if pos == 0 or neg == 0:
        if bounded:
            log.warning("validation split has a single class; passing the probability through")
            return identity(len(y))
        raise ValueError("calibration needs validation windows of both classes")
    enough = pos >= MIN_ISOTONIC_PER_CLASS and neg >= MIN_ISOTONIC_PER_CLASS
    enough = enough and len(y) >= MIN_ISOTONIC_TOTAL
    if method == "isotonic" or (method == "auto" and enough):
        return fit_isotonic(val_raw, y)
    platt = fit_platt(val_raw, y)
    if platt is not None:
        return platt
    log.warning("Platt scaling was decreasing; falling back to isotonic regression")
    return fit_isotonic(val_raw, y)

```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/calibration_onnx.py`:

```py
"""Bake a :class:`~corvus_ml.calibration.Calibration` into an exported ONNX graph.

The result has one output named ``score`` (float32, shape ``[batch]``) in [0, 1], so a runtime
needs neither the candidate type nor a sidecar file to interpret it. Piecewise-linear maps are
evaluated with standard operators (a comparison against the inner knots finds the segment, then a
gathered slope and intercept give the value); a sigmoid map is ``Sigmoid(a * s + b)``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

import numpy as np
import onnx
from onnx import TensorProto, helper, numpy_helper

from corvus_ml.calibration import Calibration

# How the raw score is read from the original graph outputs:
#   first       output 0, flattened (torch models)
#   neg_second  minus output 1, flattened (IsolationForest: skl2onnx returns decision_function)
#   second_col1 column 1 of output 1 (probabilities of a scikit-learn classifier)
RawOutput = Literal["first", "neg_second", "second_col1"]

SCORE_OUTPUT = "score"
_MIN_OPSET = 13  # tensor-valued Clip/ReduceSum axes and Unsqueeze axes


def _const(name: str, values: np.ndarray) -> TensorProto:
    return numpy_helper.from_array(values, name)


def _default_opset(model: onnx.ModelProto) -> int:
    for entry in model.opset_import:
        if entry.domain in ("", "ai.onnx"):
            return int(entry.version)
    return 1


def _rename_outputs(graph: onnx.GraphProto, prefix: str) -> list[str]:
    """Prefix the names of the graph outputs (nodes and consumers) and return the new names."""
    old = [o.name for o in graph.output]
    mapping = {n: f"{prefix}{n}" for n in old}
    for node in graph.node:
        node.input[:] = [mapping.get(n, n) for n in node.input]
        node.output[:] = [mapping.get(n, n) for n in node.output]
    return [mapping[n] for n in old]


def _raw_score(raw_names: list[str], how: RawOutput, nodes: list, inits: list) -> str:
    inits.append(_const("cal_flat", np.array([-1], dtype=np.int64)))
    if how == "first":
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Reshape", [raw_names[0], "cal_flat"], ["cal_raw"]))
    elif how == "neg_second":
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Neg", [raw_names[1]], ["cal_neg"]))
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Reshape", ["cal_neg", "cal_flat"], ["cal_raw"]))
    elif how == "second_col1":
        inits.append(_const("cal_col", np.array(1, dtype=np.int64)))
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Gather", [raw_names[1], "cal_col"], ["cal_raw"], axis=1))
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown raw output kind {how!r}")
    return "cal_raw"


def _piecewise(cal: Calibration, raw: str, nodes: list, inits: list) -> str:
    xs = np.asarray(cal.xs, dtype=np.float64)
    ys = np.asarray(cal.ys, dtype=np.float64)
    f32 = np.float32
    if len(xs) == 1:
        inits += [_const("cal_zero", np.array(0.0, f32)), _const("cal_y0", np.array(ys[0], f32))]
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Mul", [raw, "cal_zero"], ["cal_z"]))
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Add", ["cal_z", "cal_y0"], ["cal_out"]))
        return "cal_out"
    inits += [
        _const("cal_lo", np.array(xs[0], f32)),
        _const("cal_hi", np.array(xs[-1], f32)),
    ]
    nodes.append(helper.make_node("Clip", [raw, "cal_lo", "cal_hi"], ["cal_sc"]))
    slopes = np.diff(ys) / np.diff(xs)
    if len(xs) == 2:
        inits += [
            _const("cal_x0", np.array(xs[0], f32)),
            _const("cal_y0", np.array(ys[0], f32)),
            _const("cal_slope", np.array(slopes[0], f32)),
        ]
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Sub", ["cal_sc", "cal_x0"], ["cal_d"]))
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Mul", ["cal_d", "cal_slope"], ["cal_s"]))
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Add", ["cal_y0", "cal_s"], ["cal_out"]))
        return "cal_out"
    inits += [
        _const("cal_inner", xs[1:-1].astype(f32)),
        _const("cal_xs", xs[:-1].astype(f32)),
        _const("cal_ys", ys[:-1].astype(f32)),
        _const("cal_slopes", slopes.astype(f32)),
        _const("cal_axis1", np.array([1], dtype=np.int64)),
    ]
    nodes += [
        helper.make_node("Unsqueeze", ["cal_sc", "cal_axis1"], ["cal_col2"]),
        helper.make_node("GreaterOrEqual", ["cal_col2", "cal_inner"], ["cal_ge"]),
        helper.make_node("Cast", ["cal_ge"], ["cal_ge_i"], to=TensorProto.INT64),
        helper.make_node("ReduceSum", ["cal_ge_i", "cal_axis1"], ["cal_idx"], keepdims=0),
        helper.make_node("Gather", ["cal_xs", "cal_idx"], ["cal_x0"]),
        helper.make_node("Gather", ["cal_ys", "cal_idx"], ["cal_y0"]),
        helper.make_node("Gather", ["cal_slopes", "cal_idx"], ["cal_slope"]),
        helper.make_node("Sub", ["cal_sc", "cal_x0"], ["cal_d"]),
        helper.make_node("Mul", ["cal_d", "cal_slope"], ["cal_s"]),
        helper.make_node("Add", ["cal_y0", "cal_s"], ["cal_out"]),
    ]
    return "cal_out"


def _sigmoid(cal: Calibration, raw: str, nodes: list, inits: list) -> str:
    inits += [
        _const("cal_a", np.array(cal.a, np.float32)),
        _const("cal_b", np.array(cal.b, np.float32)),
    ]
    nodes.append(helper.make_node("Mul", [raw, "cal_a"], ["cal_az"]))
    nodes.append(helper.make_node("Add", ["cal_az", "cal_b"], ["cal_z"]))
    nodes.append(helper.make_node("Sigmoid", ["cal_z"], ["cal_out"]))
    return "cal_out"


def embed_calibration(
    model: onnx.ModelProto, raw_output: RawOutput, calibration: Calibration
) -> onnx.ModelProto:
    """A copy of ``model`` whose only output ``score`` is the calibrated score in [0, 1]."""
    if _default_opset(model) < _MIN_OPSET:
        raise ValueError(f"the model uses opset {_default_opset(model)}, need >= {_MIN_OPSET}")
    out = onnx.ModelProto()
    out.CopyFrom(model)
    graph = out.graph
    raw_names = _rename_outputs(graph, "raw_")
    nodes: list[onnx.NodeProto] = []
    inits: list[TensorProto] = []
    raw = _raw_score(raw_names, raw_output, nodes, inits)
    if calibration.kind == "sigmoid":
        value = _sigmoid(calibration, raw, nodes, inits)
    else:
        value = _piecewise(calibration, raw, nodes, inits)
        inits += [_const("cal_one", np.array(1.0, np.float32))]
        inits += [_const("cal_nil", np.array(0.0, np.float32))]
        nodes.append(helper.make_node("Clip", [value, "cal_nil", "cal_one"], ["cal_clipped"]))
        value = "cal_clipped"
    nodes.append(helper.make_node("Identity", [value], [SCORE_OUTPUT]))
    graph.node.extend(nodes)
    graph.initializer.extend(inits)
    del graph.output[:]
    graph.output.append(helper.make_tensor_value_info(SCORE_OUTPUT, TensorProto.FLOAT, ["batch"]))
    onnx.checker.check_model(out)
    return out


def embed_calibration_file(
    src: str, dst: str, raw_output: RawOutput, calibration: Calibration
) -> str:
    """Load ``src``, embed the calibration and save the result to ``dst``."""
    model = embed_calibration(onnx.load(src), raw_output, calibration)
    onnx.save(model, dst)
    return dst

```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/cgroup.py`:

```py
"""Worker count derived from the cgroup CPU limit."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import os
from pathlib import Path

CPU_MAX_PATH = Path("/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max")


def parse_cpu_max(text: str) -> float | None:
    """Parse cgroup v2 ``cpu.max`` ("<quota|max> <period>") into a CPU count.

    Returns None when there is no limit or the content is not understood.
    """
    parts = text.split()
    if len(parts) < 1 or parts[0] == "max":
        return None
    try:
        quota = int(parts[0])
        period = int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 100_000
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if quota <= 0 or period <= 0:
        return None
    return quota / period


def cpu_limit(path: Path = CPU_MAX_PATH) -> float | None:
    """CPU limit from the cgroup file, None if absent, unreadable or unlimited."""
    try:
        return parse_cpu_max(path.read_text())
    except OSError:
        return None


def default_workers(path: Path = CPU_MAX_PATH, process_cpu_count: int | None = None) -> int:
    """Pool size: ceil(cgroup limit) if limited, else the usable CPU count; at least 1."""
    if process_cpu_count is None:
        process_cpu_count = os.process_cpu_count() or 1
    limit = cpu_limit(path)
    if limit is None:
        return max(1, process_cpu_count)
    return max(1, min(math.ceil(limit), process_cpu_count))

```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/candidates/base.py`:

```py
"""Candidate interface and registry.

Adding a candidate is one class: subclass :class:`Candidate`, set the class attributes, implement
``fit`` / ``score`` / ``export_onnx`` / ``n_params`` and decorate it with :func:`register`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import ClassVar, Literal

import numpy as np

from corvus_ml.calibration import Calibration
from corvus_ml.calibration_onnx import RawOutput
from corvus_ml.eval.data import EvalData
from corvus_ml.features.featurizer import CompletedWindow
from corvus_ml.features.model_input import model_inputs
from corvus_ml.features.spec import FeatureSpec

REGISTRY: dict[str, type[Candidate]] = {}


def register(cls: type[Candidate]) -> type[Candidate]:
    REGISTRY[cls.name] = cls
    return cls


class Candidate(ABC):
    name: ClassVar[str]
    supervised: ClassVar[bool]
    input_kind: ClassVar[Literal["agg", "seq", "raw_bytes"]]
    # True for torch models (they get the int8 dynamic-quantization variant).
    quantizable: ClassVar[bool] = False
    # How the raw score is read from the exported graph (see corvus_ml.calibration_onnx).
    onnx_raw: ClassVar[RawOutput] = "first"
    # True if the raw score is already a probability in [0, 1].
    bounded: ClassVar[bool] = False
    # Candidates that also learn from the (unlabelled) windows of the training players get them as
    # ``pool`` in ``fit`` (masked pretraining).
    pretrains: ClassVar[bool] = False
    # Optuna support: ``fit`` reports the validation loss per epoch to ``on_epoch``.
    tunable: ClassVar[bool] = False
    # Limit of test windows used for the ONNX parity check (huge inputs); None = all.
    parity_rows: ClassVar[int | None] = None

    def __init__(self, seed: int = 0, threads: int = 1, **params):
        self.seed = seed
        self.threads = threads
        self.params = params
        self.calibration: Calibration | None = None
        # Set by the tuner: called as ``on_epoch(epoch, val_loss)``; may raise to prune the run.
        self.on_epoch = None

    def calibrated_score(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        """The score a deployed model outputs: ``score`` mapped through the calibration."""
        raw = self.score(data)
        return raw if self.calibration is None else self.calibration.apply(raw)

    def export_calibrated_onnx(self, path: Path, example: np.ndarray) -> Path:
        """Export with the calibration baked in: one output ``score`` in [0, 1]."""
        import onnx

        from corvus_ml.calibration_onnx import embed_calibration

        if self.calibration is None:
            raise ValueError("fit a calibration before exporting a calibrated graph")
        raw_path = self.export_onnx(path.with_name(f"{path.stem}.raw.onnx"), example)
        model = embed_calibration(onnx.load(str(raw_path)), self.onnx_raw, self.calibration)
        onnx.save(model, str(path))
        return path

    def inputs(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        """The float32 array fed to both the native model and the ONNX graph."""
        arr = data.agg if self.input_kind == "agg" else data.seq
        if arr is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name} needs {self.input_kind} inputs")
        return np.ascontiguousarray(arr, dtype=np.float32)

    def inputs_for_windows(
        self, windows: Sequence[CompletedWindow], spec: FeatureSpec | None = None
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """The same array as :meth:`inputs`, built from freshly featurized windows (serving).

        Both paths use ``corvus_ml.features.model_input`` so they cannot drift apart.
        """
        return model_inputs(windows, self.input_kind, spec)

    @abstractmethod
    def fit(self, train: EvalData, val: EvalData | None = None) -> None:
        """Fit on ``train``. Supervised candidates get only labelled windows; unsupervised ones
        get windows that are legit (or assumed legit). ``val`` is used for early stopping."""

    @abstractmethod
    def score(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        """Float64 score per window, higher = more likely cheat."""

    @abstractmethod
    def export_onnx(self, path: Path, example: np.ndarray) -> Path:
        """Write the ONNX graph. Input name ``x`` (batch axis dynamic), output index 0 or the
        output named ``score`` is turned into the score by :meth:`onnx_to_score`."""

    def onnx_to_score(self, outputs: list[np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:
        return np.asarray(outputs[0], dtype=np.float64).reshape(len(outputs[0]), -1)[:, 0]

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def n_params(self) -> int:
        """Learnable parameters (trees: total node count)."""


def create(name: str, seed: int, threads: int, params: dict) -> Candidate:
    if name not in REGISTRY:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown candidate {name!r}; known: {sorted(REGISTRY)}")
    return REGISTRY[name](seed=seed, threads=threads, **params)

```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/candidates/raw_models.py`:

```py
"""Candidates on tokenized raw packet bytes (ADR-CORV-0008): ``raw_hier_classifier`` (supervised)
and ``raw_hier_anomaly`` (self-supervised, masked-reconstruction score).

Both take the float32 tensor ``(batch, [macro,] packets, tokens + 1)`` built by
:func:`corvus_ml.raw.windows.to_input`; the model, the pretraining objectives and the checkpoint
format are in :mod:`corvus_ml.raw`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from abc import abstractmethod
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn

from corvus_ml.eval.candidates.base import Candidate, register
from corvus_ml.eval.data import LABEL_CHEAT, EvalData
from corvus_ml.eval.training import fit, lr_range_test, seed_everything
from corvus_ml.raw.model import ModelConfig, RawAnomalyNet, RawHierNet
from corvus_ml.raw.pretrain import flatten_windows, load_encoder, pretrain, save_checkpoint
from corvus_ml.raw.spec import RawBytesSpec
from corvus_ml.raw.windows import to_input

_OPSET = 17
_MODEL_KEYS = (
    "d_model", "layers", "heads", "ffn_mult", "dropout", "local_dim", "local_layers", "local_type",
    "local_heads", "macro_layers", "macro_pool", "p_token", "p_packet", "first_tokens",
    "max_masked", "score_period", "score_passes", "time_freqs", "time_min_s", "time_max_s",
)  # fmt: skip
_TRAIN_KEYS = (
    "epochs", "batch_size", "lr", "weight_decay", "patience", "pretrain_epochs", "pretrain_lr",
    "init_from", "checkpoint_out", "score_batch",
)  # fmt: skip


class RawCandidate(Candidate):
    input_kind = "raw_bytes"
    quantizable = False
    pretrains = True
    tunable = True
    parity_rows = 64  # whole test sets are large; the parity check needs only a sample

    def __init__(self, seed: int = 0, threads: int = 1, **params):
        unknown = sorted(set(params) - set(_MODEL_KEYS) - set(_TRAIN_KEYS))
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown parameters for {self.name}: {unknown}")
        super().__init__(seed, threads, **params)

    # --- data ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def spec_of(data: EvalData) -> RawBytesSpec:
        spec = data.meta.get("raw_spec")
        if spec is None or data.raw_ids is None:
            raise ValueError("raw-byte candidates need raw windows (configure [raw])")
        return spec

    def inputs(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        spec = self.spec_of(data)
        assert data.raw_ids is not None
        assert data.raw_time is not None
        return to_input(data.raw_ids, data.raw_time, spec.window.macro_windows)

    def _tensors(self, data: EvalData) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        spec = self.spec_of(data)
        assert data.raw_ids is not None
        assert data.raw_time is not None
        ids, t = data.raw_ids, data.raw_time
        if spec.window.macro_windows == 1:
            ids, t = ids[:, 0], t[:, 0]
        return torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(ids)), torch.from_numpy(
            np.ascontiguousarray(t)
        )

    def model_config(self, data: EvalData) -> ModelConfig:
        spec = self.spec_of(data)
        kw = {k: self.params[k] for k in _MODEL_KEYS if k in self.params}
        return ModelConfig.for_layout(
            spec.layout,
            spec.vocab_size,
            spec.packet.max_tokens_per_packet,
            macro_windows=spec.window.macro_windows,
            **kw,
        )

    # --- training ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @abstractmethod
    def build(self, cfg: ModelConfig) -> nn.Module: ...

    def _pretrain(self, cfg: ModelConfig, pool: EvalData) -> RawAnomalyNet:
        """Masked pretraining on every window of ``pool`` (labels are not used)."""
        micro_cfg = ModelConfig(**{**cfg.to_dict(), "macro_windows": 1, "macro_layers": 1})
        net = RawAnomalyNet(micro_cfg)
        ids, t = flatten_windows(pool.raw_ids, pool.raw_time)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        if len(ids) == 0:
            return net
        epochs = int(self.params.get("pretrain_epochs", 0))
        lr = float(self.params.get("pretrain_lr", 1e-3))
        self.pretrain_history = pretrain(
            net, ids, t, epochs=epochs, batch_size=int(self.params.get("batch_size", 16)),
            lr=lr, weight_decay=float(self.params.get("weight_decay", 0.01)),
            patience=int(self.params.get("patience", 3)), seed=self.seed,
        )  # fmt: skip
        if "checkpoint_out" in self.params:
            save_checkpoint(Path(self.params["checkpoint_out"]), net)
        return net

    def _init_encoder(self, model: nn.Module, cfg: ModelConfig, pool: EvalData | None) -> None:
        if "init_from" in self.params:
            load_encoder(model, Path(self.params["init_from"]))
        elif int(self.params.get("pretrain_epochs", 0)) > 0 and pool is not None:
            net = self._pretrain(cfg, pool)
            model.micro.load_state_dict(net.micro.state_dict())  # type: ignore[union-attr]

    def _run_fit(self, tr, va, loss_fn) -> None:
        lr = self.params.get("lr", 2e-3)
        batch = int(self.params.get("batch_size", 16))
        wd = float(self.params.get("weight_decay", 0.01))
        self.lr_range = None
        if lr == "auto":
            self.lr_range = lr_range_test(
                self.model, loss_fn, tr, batch_size=batch, seed=self.seed, weight_decay=wd,
                steps=int(self.params.get("lr_steps", 60)),
            )  # fmt: skip
            lr = self.lr_range.suggested_lr
        self.lr_used = float(lr)
        self.history = fit(
            self.model, loss_fn, tr, va, epochs=int(self.params.get("epochs", 10)),
            batch_size=batch, lr=self.lr_used, weight_decay=wd,
            patience=int(self.params.get("patience", 3)), seed=self.seed, on_epoch=self.on_epoch,
        )  # fmt: skip

    # --- scoring and export ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    def score(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        ids, t = self._tensors(data)
        self.model.eval()
        step = int(self.params.get("score_batch", 16))
        out = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for i in range(0, ids.shape[0], step):
                out.append(self._score_batch(ids[i : i + step].long(), t[i : i + step]))
        return np.concatenate(out).astype(np.float64) if out else np.zeros(0)

    @abstractmethod
    def _score_batch(self, ids: torch.Tensor, t: torch.Tensor) -> np.ndarray: ...

    def export_onnx(self, path: Path, example: np.ndarray) -> Path:
        self.model.eval()
        packets_axis = example.ndim - 2
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            torch.onnx.export(
                self.model,
                (torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(example[:2], dtype=np.float32)),),
                str(path),
                input_names=["x"],
                output_names=["score"],
                dynamic_axes={"x": {0: "batch", packets_axis: "packets"}, "score": {0: "batch"}},
                opset_version=_OPSET,
                dynamo=False,
            )
        return path

    @property
    def n_params(self) -> int:
        return int(sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters()))


@register
class RawHierClassifier(RawCandidate):
    name = "raw_hier_classifier"
    supervised = True
    bounded = True

    def build(self, cfg: ModelConfig) -> nn.Module:
        return RawHierNet(cfg)

    def fit(
        self, train: EvalData, val: EvalData | None = None, pool: EvalData | None = None
    ) -> None:
        seed_everything(self.seed, self.threads)
        cfg = self.model_config(train)
        pos = max(1.0, float((train.label == LABEL_CHEAT).sum()))
        neg = max(1.0, float((train.label != LABEL_CHEAT).sum()))
        pos_weight = torch.tensor(neg / pos)
        self.model = self.build(cfg)
        self._init_encoder(self.model, cfg, pool if pool is not None else train)

        def tensors(d: EvalData):
            ids, t = self._tensors(d)
            return ids, t, torch.from_numpy((d.label == LABEL_CHEAT).astype(np.float32))

        def loss_fn(model, batch):
            logits = model.logits_ids(batch[0].long(), batch[1])
            return nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
                logits, batch[2], pos_weight=pos_weight
            )

        self._run_fit(
            tensors(train), tensors(val) if val is not None and len(val) else None, loss_fn
        )

    def _score_batch(self, ids, t):
        return self.model.logits_ids(ids, t).sigmoid().numpy()


@register
class RawHierAnomaly(RawCandidate):
    name = "raw_hier_anomaly"
    supervised = False

    def build(self, cfg: ModelConfig) -> nn.Module:
        return RawAnomalyNet(cfg)

    def model_config(self, data: EvalData) -> ModelConfig:
        cfg = super().model_config(data)
        if cfg.macro_windows != 1:
            raise ValueError("raw_hier_anomaly works on single windows: unset macro_window_seconds")
        return cfg

    def fit(
        self, train: EvalData, val: EvalData | None = None, pool: EvalData | None = None
    ) -> None:
        seed_everything(self.seed, self.threads)
        cfg = self.model_config(train)
        self.model = self.build(cfg)
        if "init_from" in self.params:
            load_encoder(self.model, Path(self.params["init_from"]))

        def tensors(d: EvalData):
            return self._tensors(d)

        def loss_fn(model, batch):
            return model.pretrain_loss(batch[0].long(), batch[1])

        self._run_fit(
            tensors(train), tensors(val) if val is not None and len(val) else None, loss_fn
        )
        if "checkpoint_out" in self.params:
            save_checkpoint(Path(self.params["checkpoint_out"]), self.model)

    def _score_batch(self, ids, t):
        return self.model.score_ids(ids, t).numpy()
```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/candidates/sklearn_models.py`:

```py
"""Candidates on window aggregates: IsolationForest and gradient boosting."""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import onnx.helper
from skl2onnx import to_onnx
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier, IsolationForest

from corvus_ml.eval.candidates.base import Candidate, register
from corvus_ml.eval.data import LABEL_CHEAT, EvalData

_OPSET = {"": 17, "ai.onnx.ml": 3}


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _int_attributes() -> Iterator[None]:
    """skl2onnx emits numpy bools in integer-list attributes (HistGradientBoosting); the
    current ``onnx`` rejects them. Convert them to ints while converting."""
    original = onnx.helper.make_attribute

    def patched(key, value, *args, **kwargs):
        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, np.ndarray)) and any(
            isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)) for v in value
        ):
            value = [int(v) for v in value]
        return original(key, value, *args, **kwargs)

    onnx.helper.make_attribute = patched
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        onnx.helper.make_attribute = original


@register
class IsolationForestCandidate(Candidate):
    name = "isolation_forest"
    supervised = False
    input_kind = "agg"
    onnx_raw = "neg_second"

    def fit(self, train: EvalData, val: EvalData | None = None) -> None:
        self.model = IsolationForest(
            n_estimators=int(self.params.get("n_estimators", 200)),
            max_samples=self.params.get("max_samples", "auto"),
            contamination="auto",
            random_state=self.seed,
            n_jobs=1,
        ).fit(self.inputs(train))

    def score(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        # -decision_function = offset-free anomaly score, the same quantity the ONNX graph yields.
        return -self.model.decision_function(self.inputs(data)).astype(np.float64)

    def export_onnx(self, path: Path, example: np.ndarray) -> Path:
        onx = to_onnx(self.model, example[:1], target_opset=_OPSET)
        path.write_bytes(onx.SerializeToString())
        return path

    def onnx_to_score(self, outputs: list[np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:
        # outputs: label, scores (= decision_function, higher = more normal)
        return -np.asarray(outputs[1], dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)

    @property
    def n_params(self) -> int:
        return int(sum(t.tree_.node_count for t in self.model.estimators_))


@register
class GradientBoostingCandidate(Candidate):
    name = "gradient_boosting"
    supervised = True
    input_kind = "agg"
    onnx_raw = "second_col1"
    bounded = True

    def fit(self, train: EvalData, val: EvalData | None = None) -> None:
        y = (train.label == LABEL_CHEAT).astype(int)
        self.model = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(
            max_iter=int(self.params.get("max_iter", 200)),
            learning_rate=float(self.params.get("learning_rate", 0.1)),
            max_depth=self.params.get("max_depth"),
            class_weight="balanced",
            early_stopping=bool(self.params.get("early_stopping", False)),
            random_state=self.seed,
        ).fit(self.inputs(train), y)

    def score(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        return self.model.predict_proba(self.inputs(data))[:, 1].astype(np.float64)

    def export_onnx(self, path: Path, example: np.ndarray) -> Path:
        with _int_attributes():
            onx = to_onnx(
                self.model,
                example[:1],
                target_opset=_OPSET,
                options={id(self.model): {"zipmap": False}},
            )
        path.write_bytes(onx.SerializeToString())
        return path

    def onnx_to_score(self, outputs: list[np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:
        return np.asarray(outputs[1], dtype=np.float64)[:, 1]

    @property
    def n_params(self) -> int:
        return int(sum(len(p.nodes) for stage in self.model._predictors for p in stage))
```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/candidates/torch_models.py`:

```py
"""Candidates on token sequences (PyTorch, CPU): GRU autoencoder and 1D-CNN classifier.

Both take a ``(batch, L, F + 1)`` tensor whose last channel is the padding mask. Per-feature
standardisation (statistics of the real training frames) lives inside the module as buffers, so
the exported ONNX graph is self-contained: raw transformed tokens in, one score per window out.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from abc import abstractmethod
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn

from corvus_ml.eval.candidates.base import Candidate, register
from corvus_ml.eval.data import LABEL_CHEAT, EvalData
from corvus_ml.eval.training import fit, lr_range_test, seed_everything

_OPSET = 17


def frame_stats(x: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Mean / std of the feature channels over real (unpadded) frames."""
    real = x[..., -1] > 0.5
    frames = x[..., :-1][real]
    if frames.shape[0] == 0:
        n = x.shape[-1] - 1
        return np.zeros(n, np.float32), np.ones(n, np.float32)
    return frames.mean(0).astype(np.float32), np.maximum(frames.std(0), 1e-3).astype(np.float32)


class _Normalised(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, mean: np.ndarray, std: np.ndarray):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("mean", torch.as_tensor(mean))
        self.register_buffer("std", torch.as_tensor(std))

    def normalise(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        mask = x[..., -1:]
        return (x[..., :-1] - self.mean) / self.std * mask, mask


class GruAutoencoder(_Normalised):
    """GRU encoder -> latent -> GRU decoder; forward returns the masked reconstruction MSE."""

    def __init__(self, mean, std, hidden: int = 64, latent: int = 32):
        super().__init__(mean, std)
        f = len(mean)
        self.enc = nn.GRU(f, hidden, batch_first=True)
        self.to_latent = nn.Linear(hidden, latent)
        self.from_latent = nn.Linear(latent, hidden)
        self.dec = nn.GRU(hidden, hidden, batch_first=True)
        self.out = nn.Linear(hidden, f)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        xn, mask = self.normalise(x)
        _, h = self.enc(xn)
        z = self.to_latent(h[-1])
        seed = self.from_latent(z).unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, xn.shape[1], -1)
        y, _ = self.dec(seed)
        err = ((self.out(y) - xn) ** 2).mean(-1)
        m = mask[..., 0]
        return (err * m).sum(1) / m.sum(1).clamp(min=1.0)


class Cnn1d(_Normalised):
    """Two dilated conv layers + masked mean/max pooling + linear head."""

    def __init__(self, mean, std, channels: int = 32):
        super().__init__(mean, std)
        f = len(mean)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv1d(f, channels, 5, padding=2)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv1d(channels, channels, 5, padding=4, dilation=2)
        self.head = nn.Linear(2 * channels, 1)

    def logits(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        xn, mask = self.normalise(x)
        h = torch.relu(self.c1(xn.transpose(1, 2)))
        h = torch.relu(self.c2(h)).transpose(1, 2) * mask
        mean = h.sum(1) / mask.sum(1).clamp(min=1.0)
        return self.head(torch.cat([mean, h.max(1).values], dim=1)).squeeze(-1)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return torch.sigmoid(self.logits(x))


class TorchCandidate(Candidate):
    quantizable = True
    tunable = True
    input_kind = "seq"

    @abstractmethod
    def build(self, mean: np.ndarray, std: np.ndarray) -> nn.Module: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def loss_fn(self, model: nn.Module, batch: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]) -> torch.Tensor: ...

    def tensors(self, data: EvalData) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
        return (torch.from_numpy(self.inputs(data)),)

    def fit(self, train: EvalData, val: EvalData | None = None) -> None:
        seed_everything(self.seed, self.threads)
        tr = self.tensors(train)
        va = self.tensors(val) if val is not None and len(val) else None
        self.model = self.build(*frame_stats(tr[0].numpy()))
        lr = self.params.get("lr", 2e-3)
        batch = int(self.params.get("batch_size", 64))
        self.lr_range = None
        if lr == "auto":
            self.lr_range = lr_range_test(
                self.model, self.loss_fn, tr, batch_size=batch, seed=self.seed
            )
            lr = self.lr_range.suggested_lr
        self.lr_used = float(lr)
        self.history = fit(
            self.model,
            self.loss_fn,
            tr,
            va,
            epochs=int(self.params.get("epochs", 30)),
            batch_size=batch,
            lr=self.lr_used,
            weight_decay=float(self.params.get("weight_decay", 0.01)),
            patience=int(self.params.get("patience", 5)),
            seed=self.seed,
            on_epoch=self.on_epoch,
        )

    def score(self, data: EvalData) -> np.ndarray:
        x = torch.from_numpy(self.inputs(data))
        self.model.eval()
        out = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for i in range(0, x.shape[0], 512):
                out.append(self.model(x[i : i + 512]).numpy())
        return np.concatenate(out).astype(np.float64) if out else np.zeros(0)

    def export_onnx(self, path: Path, example: np.ndarray) -> Path:
        self.model.eval()
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            torch.onnx.export(
                self.model,
                (torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(example[:2])),),
                str(path),
                input_names=["x"],
                output_names=["score"],
                dynamic_axes={"x": {0: "batch"}, "score": {0: "batch"}},
                opset_version=_OPSET,
                dynamo=False,
            )
        return path

    @property
    def n_params(self) -> int:
        return int(sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters()))


@register
class GruAutoencoderCandidate(TorchCandidate):
    name = "gru_autoencoder"
    supervised = False

    def build(self, mean, std) -> nn.Module:
        return GruAutoencoder(
            mean, std, int(self.params.get("hidden", 64)), int(self.params.get("latent", 32))
        )

    def loss_fn(self, model, batch):
        return model(batch[0]).mean()


@register
class CnnCandidate(TorchCandidate):
    name = "cnn1d"
    supervised = True
    bounded = True

    def tensors(self, data: EvalData):
        y = torch.from_numpy((data.label == LABEL_CHEAT).astype(np.float32))
        return (torch.from_numpy(self.inputs(data)), y)

    def build(self, mean, std) -> nn.Module:
        return Cnn1d(mean, std, int(self.params.get("channels", 32)))

    def fit(self, train: EvalData, val: EvalData | None = None) -> None:
        pos = max(1.0, float((train.label == LABEL_CHEAT).sum()))
        neg = max(1.0, float((train.label != LABEL_CHEAT).sum()))
        self._pos_weight = torch.tensor(neg / pos)
        super().fit(train, val)

    def loss_fn(self, model, batch):
        return nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
            model.logits(batch[0]), batch[1], pos_weight=self._pos_weight
        )
```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/cli.py`:

```py
"""``corvus-eval`` command line."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

from corvus_ml.eval.config import EvalConfig

MISSING_EXTRA = (
    "corvus-eval needs the optional 'eval' dependencies (torch, scikit-learn, onnx, ...): "
    "install them with `uv sync --extra eval` or `pip install 'corvus-ml[eval]'`"
)


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="corvus-eval")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="evaluate the configured candidates")
    r.add_argument("--config", required=True, type=Path, help="eval.toml")
    r.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path, help="report directory")
    t = sub.add_parser(
        "tune", help="Optuna search for the tunable candidates, then evaluate with the best"
    )
    t.add_argument("--config", required=True, type=Path, help="eval.toml (optional [tune] table)")
    t.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path, help="report directory")
    t.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=None, help="overrides tune.trials")
    q = sub.add_parser("pretrain", help="masked pretraining of a raw-byte model, saves checkpoints")
    q.add_argument("--config", required=True, type=Path, help="eval.toml with a [raw] table")
    q.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path, help="directory for pretrain/<context>.pt")
    return p


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
    try:
        from corvus_ml.eval import candidates as _candidates  # noqa: F401 - registers them
        from corvus_ml.eval.report import write_report
        from corvus_ml.eval.runner import run
    except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
        if exc.name and exc.name.split(".")[0] in {
            "torch",
            "sklearn",
            "skl2onnx",
            "onnx",
            "onnxruntime",
        }:
            print(f"{MISSING_EXTRA} (missing module: {exc.name})", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        raise
    cfg = EvalConfig.load(args.config)
    if args.command == "pretrain":
        from corvus_ml.eval.runner import pretrain_checkpoints

        print(json.dumps(pretrain_checkpoints(cfg, args.out), indent=2))
        return 0
    if args.command == "tune" and args.trials is not None:
        cfg.tune = replace(cfg.tune, trials=args.trials)
    report = run(cfg, args.out, tune=args.command == "tune")
    js, md = write_report(report, args.out)
    print(md.read_text())
    print(f"wrote {js} and {md}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`ml/src/corvus_ml/eval/config.py`:

```py
"""Run configuration (``eval.toml``); documented in docs/how-to/evaluate-models.md."""

from __future__ import annotations

import tomllib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from corvus_ml.calibration import METHODS as CALIBRATION_METHODS
from corvus_ml.eval.synthetic import SyntheticConfig
from corvus_ml.raw.layout import TokenLayout
from corvus_ml.raw.spec import PacketConfig, WindowConfig
from corvus_ml.raw.synthetic import SyntheticRawConfig
from corvus_ml.raw.tokenizer import TokenizerConfig

UNLABELLED_MODES = ("exclude", "assume_legit")


@dataclass
class BenchConfig:
    enabled: bool = True
    warmup: int = 20
    iters: int = 200
    batch: int = 64
    isolated: bool = True  # fresh process per model so peak RSS belongs to that model
    quantize: bool = True  # int8 dynamic quantisation variant of the torch models
    # Raw-byte models: extra single-window latencies at these packet counts (full-width rows).
    raw_packets: tuple[int, ...] = ()


@dataclass
class RawEvalConfig:
    """Raw-byte input (``[raw]``): a packet table below ``dir`` or a synthetic source."""

    dir: Path | None = None  # features/<snapshot>/raw: packets/, sessions, labels, spec, tokenizer
    window_overrides: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    synthetic: SyntheticRawConfig | None = None
    tokenizer: TokenizerConfig = field(default_factory=lambda: TokenizerConfig(vocab_size=1024))
    packet: PacketConfig = field(default_factory=PacketConfig)
    max_windows: int | None = None  # random subsample of the windows (memory bound)

    def window(self, base: WindowConfig | None = None) -> WindowConfig:
        merged = {**(base or WindowConfig()).__dict__, **self.window_overrides}
        return WindowConfig(**merged)


@dataclass
class TuneConfig:
    """Optuna study (``[tune]``); see docs/how-to/evaluate-models.md."""

    trials: int = 20
    timeout_s: float | None = None
    storage: str = ""  # "" = sqlite file in the output dir (or CORVUS_OPTUNA_STORAGE), "memory"
    study_name: str = "corvus"
    tune_windows: bool = True  # raw-byte models: window_seconds and max_packets are searched too
    space: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)  # per parameter [low, high] or a list


@dataclass
class EvalConfig:
    name: str = "eval"
    seed: int = 1337
    threads: int = 1
    seq_len: int = 256
    unlabelled: str = "exclude"
    calibration: str = "auto"  # auto | isotonic | platt | ecdf | none (see corvus_ml.calibration)
    contexts: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # empty = every context in the data
    split: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.6, 0.2, 0.2)
    fpr_targets: tuple[float, ...] = (0.01, 0.001)
    min_confidence: float = 0.0
    learning_curve: tuple[float, ...] = ()
    # Real data (all paths relative to the config file). tokens is only needed by sequence models.
    windows: Path | None = None
    tokens: Path | None = None
    sessions: Path | None = None
    labels: Path | None = None
    synthetic: SyntheticConfig | None = None
    candidates: dict[str, dict] = field(default_factory=dict)
    bench: BenchConfig = field(default_factory=BenchConfig)
    raw: RawEvalConfig | None = None
    tune: TuneConfig = field(default_factory=TuneConfig)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, raw: dict, base: Path = Path()) -> EvalConfig:
        run = dict(raw.get("run", {}))
        data = raw.get("data", {})
        cfg = cls(name=str(raw.get("name", "eval")))
        for key in (
            "seed",
            "threads",
            "seq_len",
            "unlabelled",
            "calibration",
            "contexts",
            "min_confidence",
        ):
            if key in run:
                setattr(cfg, key, run.pop(key))
        if "split" in run:
            cfg.split = tuple(float(v) for v in run.pop("split"))
        if "fpr_targets" in run:
            cfg.fpr_targets = tuple(float(v) for v in run.pop("fpr_targets"))
        if "learning_curve" in run:
            cfg.learning_curve = tuple(float(v) for v in run.pop("learning_curve"))
        if run:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown [run] keys: {sorted(run)}")
        if cfg.unlabelled not in UNLABELLED_MODES:
            raise ValueError(f"run.unlabelled must be one of {UNLABELLED_MODES}")
        if cfg.calibration not in CALIBRATION_METHODS:
            raise ValueError(f"run.calibration must be one of {CALIBRATION_METHODS}")
        for key in ("windows", "tokens", "sessions", "labels"):
            if key in data:
                setattr(cfg, key, (base / data[key]).resolve())
        if "synthetic" in raw:
            names = {f.name for f in fields(SyntheticConfig)}
            extra = set(raw["synthetic"]) - names
            if extra:
                raise ValueError(f"unknown [synthetic] keys: {sorted(extra)}")
            syn = dict(raw["synthetic"])
            if "contexts" in syn:
                syn["contexts"] = tuple(syn["contexts"])
            syn.setdefault("seed", cfg.seed)
            cfg.synthetic = SyntheticConfig(**syn)
        elif "raw" in raw:
            cfg.raw = _raw_config(dict(raw["raw"]), base)
        elif not (cfg.windows and cfg.sessions):
            raise ValueError(
                "config needs [data] windows + sessions, a [synthetic] table or a [raw] table"
            )
        cfg.candidates = {k: dict(v) for k, v in raw.get("candidates", {}).items()}
        if not cfg.candidates:
            raise ValueError("config needs at least one [candidates.<name>] table")
        bench = dict(raw.get("benchmark", {}))
        if "raw_packets" in bench:
            bench["raw_packets"] = tuple(int(v) for v in bench["raw_packets"])
        cfg.bench = BenchConfig(**bench)
        if "tune" in raw:
            tune = dict(raw["tune"])
            extra = set(tune) - {f.name for f in fields(TuneConfig)}
            if extra:
                raise ValueError(f"unknown [tune] keys: {sorted(extra)}")
            cfg.tune = TuneConfig(**tune)
        _check_candidate_kinds(cfg)
        return cfg

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> EvalConfig:
        path = Path(path)
        return cls.from_dict(tomllib.loads(path.read_text()), path.parent)


_WINDOW_KEYS = {f.name for f in fields(WindowConfig)}


def _raw_config(raw: dict, base: Path) -> RawEvalConfig:
    out = RawEvalConfig()
    if "dir" in raw:
        out.dir = (base / raw.pop("dir")).resolve()
    if "synthetic" in raw:
        syn = dict(raw.pop("synthetic"))
        for key in ("contexts", "protocols"):
            if key in syn:
                syn[key] = tuple(syn[key])
        out.synthetic = SyntheticRawConfig(**syn)
    if "tokenizer" in raw:
        tok = dict(raw.pop("tokenizer"))
        if "layout" in tok:
            lay = dict(tok.pop("layout"))
            if "protocols" in lay:
                lay["protocols"] = tuple(int(v) for v in lay["protocols"])
            tok["layout"] = TokenLayout(**lay)
        out.tokenizer = TokenizerConfig(**{"vocab_size": 1024, **tok})
    if "packet" in raw:
        out.packet = PacketConfig(**raw.pop("packet"))
    if "max_windows" in raw:
        out.max_windows = int(raw.pop("max_windows"))
    unknown = set(raw) - _WINDOW_KEYS
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown [raw] keys: {sorted(unknown)}")
    out.window_overrides = dict(raw)
    out.window()  # validates
    if (out.dir is None) == (out.synthetic is None):
        raise ValueError("[raw] needs exactly one of dir and [raw.synthetic]")
    return out


def _check_candidate_kinds(cfg: EvalConfig) -> None:
    """Raw-byte candidates run on their own windows: they cannot share a run with the others."""
    from corvus_ml.eval import candidates as cand_pkg

    kinds = {
```
