`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/models.py`:

```py
"""Model registry polling, download, validation and atomic hot-swap.

A :class:`ModelSet` is an immutable snapshot of the loaded models. :class:`ModelManager.sync`
builds the next snapshot from the registry and replaces ``current`` with a single assignment, so
the scoring path always sees either the old or the new set, never a mix. A model whose files fail
validation is not loaded (metric, error log); all other models keep running.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import posixpath
import shutil
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, cast

import numpy as np
from corvus_ml.features.config import FeaturizerConfig
from corvus_ml.features.spec import SPEC_FILE, FeatureSpec, FeatureSpecError
from corvus_ml.raw.spec import TOKENIZER_FILE, RawBytesSpec
from corvus_ml.raw.tokenizer import RawTokenizer

from .metrics import ScoreMetrics
from .ports import ModelEntry, ModelFiles, ModelSession, ScoreCatalog, SessionFactory
from .raw import budget_warning, estimate_p99_ms

log = logging.getLogger("corvus.score.models")

InputKind = Literal["agg", "seq", "raw_bytes"]
FEATURE_KINDS = ("agg", "seq")
RAW_KIND = "raw_bytes"
ONNX_FILE = "model.onnx"


class ModelRejectedError(Exception):
    """The model's files are not usable with this runtime; retrying will not help."""


def plan_threads(cpus: int, models: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Split the CPU budget across ``models``: ``(intra_op_threads_per_model, pool_workers)``.

    At most ``min(models, cpus)`` models run at the same time, each with ``cpus // that`` intra-op
    threads, so the compute threads never exceed ``cpus``. With one CPU everything runs
    sequentially on a single thread.
    """
    cpus = max(1, cpus)
    concurrent = max(1, min(models, cpus))
    return max(1, cpus // concurrent), concurrent


def input_kind_of(shape: tuple[int | str | None, ...], spec: FeatureSpec) -> InputKind:
    """Model input kind from the ONNX input rank (2: aggregates, 3: token sequences), checked
    against the feature spec; raises :class:`ModelRejectedError` on a mismatch."""
    if len(shape) == 2:
        width = shape[1]
        if isinstance(width, int) and width != spec.n_agg_inputs:
            raise ModelRejectedError(
                f"model takes {width} aggregates, spec has {spec.n_agg_inputs}"
            )
        return "agg"
    if len(shape) == 3:
        length, channels = shape[1], shape[2]
        if isinstance(length, int) and length != spec.seq_len:
            raise ModelRejectedError(f"model takes {length} frames, spec has {spec.seq_len}")
        if isinstance(channels, int) and channels != spec.n_seq_channels:
            raise ModelRejectedError(
                f"model takes {channels} channels, spec has {spec.n_seq_channels}"
            )
        return "seq"
    raise ModelRejectedError(f"unsupported model input shape {shape}")


def check_raw_shape(shape: tuple[int | str | None, ...], raw: RawBytesSpec) -> None:
    """The ONNX input of a raw-byte model: ``(batch, [macro,] packets, max_tokens + 1)``."""
    rank = 4 if raw.window.macro_windows > 1 else 3
    if len(shape) != rank:
        raise ModelRejectedError(
            f"raw-byte model input has rank {len(shape)}, the spec (macro windows "
            f"{raw.window.macro_windows}) needs rank {rank}"
        )
    channels = shape[-1]
    want = raw.packet.max_tokens_per_packet + 1
    if isinstance(channels, int) and channels != want:
        raise ModelRejectedError(f"model takes {channels} channels, the spec has {want}")
    if rank == 4 and isinstance(shape[1], int) and shape[1] != raw.window.macro_windows:
        raise ModelRejectedError(
            f"model takes {shape[1]} macro windows, the spec has {raw.window.macro_windows}"
        )


def declared_kind(card: dict[str, object] | None, spec: FeatureSpec) -> InputKind | None:
    """The input kind the model declares: ``model_card.json`` ``input_kind``, else ``raw_bytes``
    if the feature spec has a ``raw_bytes`` section, else None (legacy: decided by the ONNX rank).

    A raw-byte spec and a card that name different kinds are rejected: the ONNX rank alone cannot
    tell a token-sequence model from a raw-byte one (both feed a 3-D tensor).
    """
    declared = card.get("input_kind") if isinstance(card, dict) else None
    if declared is not None and declared not in (*FEATURE_KINDS, RAW_KIND):
        raise ModelRejectedError(f"model card declares unknown input_kind {declared!r}")
    if declared == RAW_KIND and spec.raw_bytes is None:
        raise ModelRejectedError("model card says raw_bytes but feature_spec.json has no raw_bytes")
    if declared in FEATURE_KINDS and spec.raw_bytes is not None:
        raise ModelRejectedError(
            f"model card says {declared} but feature_spec.json describes a raw-byte model"
        )
    if declared is not None:
        return cast(InputKind, declared)
    return "raw_bytes" if spec.raw_bytes is not None else None


CALIBRATED_SUFFIX = "_calibrated"
SCORE_OUTPUT = "score"
MODEL_CARD_FILE = "model_card.json"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OutputSemantics:
    """What the model declares about its output (``model_card.json`` / registered type)."""

    output_name: str | None = None
    calibrated: bool = False


def output_semantics(candidate_type: str, card: dict[str, object] | None) -> OutputSemantics:
    """Calibrated models are announced by the ``_calibrated`` candidate type suffix or by a
    ``model_card.json`` whose ``output_semantics.range`` is ``[0, 1]``; the card also names the
    ONNX output (``onnx_output``). Anything else is a legacy graph."""
    name: str | None = None
    calibrated = candidate_type.endswith(CALIBRATED_SUFFIX)
    sem = card.get("output_semantics") if isinstance(card, dict) else None
    if isinstance(sem, dict):
        out = sem.get("onnx_output")
        if isinstance(out, str) and out:
            name = out
        if sem.get("range") == [0, 1] or sem.get("range") == [0.0, 1.0]:
            calibrated = True
    if calibrated and name is None:
        name = SCORE_OUTPUT
    return OutputSemantics(name, calibrated)


def scores_from_outputs(
    candidate_type: str,
    outputs: list[np.ndarray],
    output_names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    semantics: OutputSemantics | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """One score per window, higher = more likely cheating.

    A model that declares a calibrated output (see :func:`output_semantics`) is read from the
    output of that name (``score``) and used as it is. Legacy graphs are clipped to [0, 1] and
    follow ``Candidate.onnx_to_score`` of ``corvus_ml.eval`` (which needs torch and so cannot be
    imported here): the scikit-learn candidates have two outputs (label, scores), every other
    graph exports a single ``score`` output.
    """
    sem = semantics or OutputSemantics(None, candidate_type.endswith(CALIBRATED_SUFFIX))
    if sem.calibrated:
        index = 0
        if output_names and (sem.output_name or SCORE_OUTPUT) in output_names:
            index = output_names.index(sem.output_name or SCORE_OUTPUT)
        out = np.asarray(outputs[index], dtype=np.float64)
        return out.reshape(len(out), -1)[:, 0]
    if candidate_type == "isolation_forest":
        raw = -np.asarray(outputs[1], dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
    elif candidate_type == "gradient_boosting":
        raw = np.asarray(outputs[1], dtype=np.float64)[:, 1]
    else:
        first = np.asarray(outputs[0], dtype=np.float64)
        raw = first.reshape(len(first), -1)[:, 0]
    return np.clip(raw, 0.0, 1.0)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LoadedModel:
    entry: ModelEntry
    spec: FeatureSpec
    session: ModelSession
    input_kind: InputKind
    intra_op_threads: int
    semantics: OutputSemantics = field(default_factory=OutputSemantics)
    tokenizer: RawTokenizer | None = None  # raw-byte models only

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        return self.entry.id

    @property
    def raw_spec(self) -> RawBytesSpec | None:
        """The tokenization and windowing contract of a raw-byte model, else None."""
        return self.spec.raw_bytes if self.input_kind == RAW_KIND else None

    @property
    def window(self) -> FeaturizerConfig:
        return self.spec.window


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelSet:
    """Immutable snapshot of the loaded models."""

    models: tuple[LoadedModel, ...] = ()
    _by_context: dict[str, tuple[LoadedModel, ...]] = field(default_factory=dict, compare=False)
    _raw_by_context: dict[str, dict[RawBytesSpec, RawTokenizer]] = field(
        default_factory=dict, compare=False
    )

    @classmethod
    def of(cls, models: list[LoadedModel]) -> ModelSet:
        by_context: dict[str, list[LoadedModel]] = {}
        for m in models:
            by_context.setdefault(m.entry.game_context, []).append(m)
        raw: dict[str, dict[RawBytesSpec, RawTokenizer]] = {}
        for m in models:
            if m.raw_spec is not None and m.tokenizer is not None:
                raw.setdefault(m.entry.game_context, {}).setdefault(m.raw_spec, m.tokenizer)
        return cls(tuple(models), {k: tuple(v) for k, v in by_context.items()}, raw)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.models)

    def for_context(self, game_context: str) -> tuple[LoadedModel, ...]:
        return self._by_context.get(game_context, ())

    def configs_for(self, game_context: str) -> frozenset[FeaturizerConfig]:
        """Featurizer windows of the aggregate / token-sequence models (raw-byte ones have their
        own windowing, see :meth:`raw_specs_for`)."""
        return frozenset(m.window for m in self.for_context(game_context) if m.raw_spec is None)

    def raw_specs_for(self, game_context: str) -> dict[RawBytesSpec, RawTokenizer]:
        """Distinct raw-byte windowings of the context with the tokenizer that serves them."""
        return self._raw_by_context.get(game_context, {})

    def matching(
        self, game_context: str, window: FeaturizerConfig | RawBytesSpec
    ) -> list[LoadedModel]:
        if isinstance(window, RawBytesSpec):
            return [m for m in self.for_context(game_context) if m.raw_spec == window]
        return [
            m for m in self.for_context(game_context) if m.raw_spec is None and m.window == window
        ]


def card_key(onnx_key: str) -> str:
    """The ``model_card.json`` next to the ONNX file."""
    return posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(onnx_key), MODEL_CARD_FILE)


def tokenizer_key(onnx_key: str) -> str:
    """The ``tokenizer.json`` of a raw-byte model (uploaded next to the ONNX file)."""
    return posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(onnx_key), TOKENIZER_FILE)


def spec_key(onnx_key: str) -> str:
    """The ``feature_spec.json`` that the eval export writes next to the ONNX files."""
    return posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(onnx_key), SPEC_FILE)


@dataclass
class SyncResult:
    loaded: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    unloaded: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    failed: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


class ModelManager:
    def __init__(
        self,
        catalog: ScoreCatalog,
        files: ModelFiles,
        factory: SessionFactory,
        cache_dir: Path,
        cpus: int,
        metrics: ScoreMetrics,
        p99_budget_ms: float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._catalog = catalog
        self._files = files
        self._factory = factory
        self._cache = cache_dir
        self._cpus = max(1, cpus)
        self._m = metrics
        self._budget_ms = p99_budget_ms
        self.current = ModelSet()
        self._rejected: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()  # (model id, onnx_key) that can never load
        self.last_sync_ok = False

    @property
    def pool_workers(self) -> int:
        """Size of the inference thread pool: one worker per CPU at most."""
        return self._cpus

    async def sync(self) -> SyncResult:
        """Poll the registry and swap in the new model set. Never raises."""
        result = SyncResult()
        try:
            entries = await self._catalog.active_models()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("model registry poll failed; keeping the loaded models")
            self._m.registry_polls.labels("error").inc()
            self.last_sync_ok = False
            return result
        self._m.registry_polls.labels("ok").inc()
        self.last_sync_ok = True

        intra, _ = plan_threads(self._cpus, len(entries))
        old = {m.id: m for m in self.current.models}
        keep: list[LoadedModel] = []
        for entry in entries:
            existing = old.get(entry.id)
            if (
                existing is not None
                and existing.entry.onnx_key == entry.onnx_key
                and existing.intra_op_threads == intra
            ):
                # same files; the stage (and thereby publishing) may have changed
                keep.append(
                    existing
                    if existing.entry == entry
                    else replace(existing, entry=entry, intra_op_threads=intra)
                )
                continue
            if (entry.id, entry.onnx_key) in self._rejected:
                continue
            try:
                keep.append(await self._load(entry, intra))
            except Exception as e:
                if isinstance(e, ModelRejectedError):
                    self._rejected.add((entry.id, entry.onnx_key))
                self._fail(
                    entry, "rejected" if isinstance(e, ModelRejectedError) else "load", e, result
                )
                if existing is not None:
                    keep.append(existing)  # keep serving the previous session of this model
            else:
                result.loaded.append(entry.id)

        new_ids = {m.id for m in keep}
        result.unloaded = [i for i in old if i not in new_ids]
        self.current = ModelSet.of(keep)  # atomic swap
        self._update_gauges()
        await asyncio.to_thread(self._prune_cache, {e.id for e in entries})
        return result

    # ----- loading --------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _fail(self, entry: ModelEntry, reason: str, exc: Exception, result: SyncResult) -> None:
        result.failed[entry.id] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        self._m.model_load_failures.labels(reason).inc()
        log.error(
            "model %s %s (%s) not loaded: %s: %s",
            entry.name,
            entry.version,
            entry.id,
            type(exc).__name__,
            exc,
        )

    async def _load(self, entry: ModelEntry, intra: int) -> LoadedModel:
        directory = await self._download(entry)
        return await asyncio.to_thread(self._open, entry, directory, intra)

    def _open(self, entry: ModelEntry, directory: Path, intra: int) -> LoadedModel:
        card = self._read_card(directory)
        try:
            spec = FeatureSpec.load(directory / SPEC_FILE, require_tokenizer=True)
            kind = declared_kind(card, spec)
        except FeatureSpecError as e:
            raise ModelRejectedError(str(e)) from e
        tokenizer = self._open_tokenizer(directory, spec, card) if spec.raw_bytes else None
        try:
            session = self._factory(directory / ONNX_FILE, intra)
        except Exception as e:
            raise ModelRejectedError(f"ONNX Runtime cannot load the model: {e}") from e
        if spec.raw_bytes is not None:
            check_raw_shape(session.input_shape, spec.raw_bytes)
            input_kind: InputKind = "raw_bytes"
            self._warn_budget(entry, spec.raw_bytes, intra)
        else:
            input_kind = input_kind_of(session.input_shape, spec)
            if kind is not None and kind != input_kind:
                raise ModelRejectedError(
                    f"model card says {kind}, the ONNX input {session.input_shape} is {input_kind}"
                )
        return LoadedModel(
            entry,
            spec,
            session,
            input_kind,
            intra,
            output_semantics(entry.candidate_type, card),
            tokenizer,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _open_tokenizer(
        directory: Path, spec: FeatureSpec, card: dict[str, object] | None
    ) -> RawTokenizer:
        """``tokenizer.json`` validated against the spec (hash, vocabulary size, layout)."""
        raw = spec.raw_bytes
        assert raw is not None
        tok_card = card.get("tokenizer") if isinstance(card, dict) else None
        if isinstance(tok_card, dict) and tok_card.get("sha256") not in (
            None,
            raw.tokenizer_sha256,
        ):
            raise ModelRejectedError(
                f"model card names tokenizer {tok_card.get('sha256')}, "
                f"the spec {raw.tokenizer_sha256}"
            )
        try:
            return RawTokenizer.load(directory, raw)
        except FeatureSpecError as e:
            raise ModelRejectedError(str(e)) from e
        except Exception as e:
            raise ModelRejectedError(f"tokenizer.json cannot be loaded: {e}") from e

    def _warn_budget(self, entry: ModelEntry, raw: RawBytesSpec, intra: int) -> None:
        anomaly = entry.candidate_type.startswith("raw_hier_anomaly")
        name = f"{entry.name}:{entry.version}"
        self._m.model_estimated_p99_ms.labels(name).set(
            estimate_p99_ms(raw.window.max_packets, intra, anomaly=anomaly)
        )
        message = budget_warning(
            name, raw.window.max_packets, intra, self._budget_ms, anomaly=anomaly
        )
        if message is not None:
            log.warning(message)

    @staticmethod
    def _read_card(directory: Path) -> dict[str, object] | None:
        try:
            doc = json.loads((directory / MODEL_CARD_FILE).read_text())
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return None
        return doc if isinstance(doc, dict) else None

    async def _download(self, entry: ModelEntry) -> Path:
        final = self._cache / entry.id
        if (final / ONNX_FILE).is_file() and (final / SPEC_FILE).is_file():
            return final
        onnx = await self._files.get(entry.onnx_key)
        spec = await self._files.get(spec_key(entry.onnx_key))
        try:  # optional: legacy models have no model card
            card: bytes | None = await self._files.get(card_key(entry.onnx_key))
        except Exception:
            card = None
        tokenizer = None
        if self._needs_tokenizer(spec, card):
            tokenizer = await self._files.get(tokenizer_key(entry.onnx_key))
        await asyncio.to_thread(self._publish_dir, final, onnx, spec, card, tokenizer)
        return final

    @staticmethod
    def _needs_tokenizer(spec: bytes, card: bytes | None) -> bool:
        """Raw-byte models ship ``tokenizer.json``; anything unparsable is left to validation."""
        try:
            card_doc = json.loads(card) if card is not None else None
            spec_doc = json.loads(spec)
        except ValueError:
            return False
        if isinstance(card_doc, dict) and card_doc.get("input_kind") == RAW_KIND:
            return True
        inputs = spec_doc.get("model_inputs") if isinstance(spec_doc, dict) else None
        return isinstance(inputs, dict) and isinstance(inputs.get("raw_bytes"), dict)

    def _publish_dir(
        self, final: Path, onnx: bytes, spec: bytes, card: bytes | None, tokenizer: bytes | None
    ) -> None:
        self._cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        tmp = self._cache / f".{final.name}.{uuid.uuid4().hex}.tmp"
        tmp.mkdir()
        try:
            (tmp / ONNX_FILE).write_bytes(onnx)
            (tmp / SPEC_FILE).write_bytes(spec)
            if card is not None:
                (tmp / MODEL_CARD_FILE).write_bytes(card)
            if tokenizer is not None:
                (tmp / TOKENIZER_FILE).write_bytes(tokenizer)
            shutil.rmtree(final, ignore_errors=True)
            os.replace(tmp, final)
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def _prune_cache(self, wanted: set[str]) -> None:
        if not self._cache.is_dir():
            return
        for child in self._cache.iterdir():
            if child.is_dir() and not child.name.startswith(".") and child.name not in wanted:
                shutil.rmtree(child, ignore_errors=True)

    def _update_gauges(self) -> None:
        for stage in ("shadow", "canary", "enforce"):
            n = sum(1 for m in self.current.models if m.entry.stage == stage)
            self._m.models_loaded.labels(stage).set(n)
        self._m.model_window_max_packets.clear()
        self._m.model_window_seconds.clear()
        for m in self.current.models:
            if m.raw_spec is not None:
                name = f"{m.entry.name}:{m.entry.version}"
                self._m.model_window_max_packets.labels(name).set(m.raw_spec.window.max_packets)
                self._m.model_window_seconds.labels(name).set(m.raw_spec.window.window_seconds)

```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/nats_io.py`:

```py
"""NATS JetStream adapters of the scoring service: partition consumer, score stream, publisher."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any

import nats
from nats.errors import TimeoutError as NatsTimeout
from nats.js.api import (
    AckPolicy,
    ConsumerConfig,
    DeliverPolicy,
    DiscardPolicy,
    RetentionPolicy,
    StorageType,
    StreamConfig,
)
from nats.js.errors import NotFoundError

from ..nats_source import NatsMessage, connect_options, ensure_stream, raise_replicas
from .partitions import filter_subjects
from .settings import ScoreSettings

log = logging.getLogger("corvus.score.nats")


def consumer_name(s: ScoreSettings, replica: int) -> str:
    return f"{s.score_consumer_prefix}-{replica}"


def consumer_config(s: ScoreSettings, replica: int) -> ConsumerConfig:
    """Durable pull consumer of one replica: its partitions, new messages only, explicit ack."""
    return ConsumerConfig(
        durable_name=consumer_name(s, replica),
        ack_policy=AckPolicy.EXPLICIT,
        deliver_policy=DeliverPolicy.NEW,
        ack_wait=float(s.score_ack_wait_s),
        max_ack_pending=s.score_max_ack_pending,
        filter_subjects=filter_subjects(replica, s.score_replicas, s.capture_partitions),
    )


def configured_filters(config: Any) -> set[str]:
    """The filter subjects of a consumer config (``filter_subjects`` or the single filter)."""
    subjects = getattr(config, "filter_subjects", None)
    if subjects:
        return set(subjects)
    single = getattr(config, "filter_subject", None)
    return {single} if single else set()


def needs_update(existing: Any, wanted: ConsumerConfig) -> bool:
    return configured_filters(existing) != configured_filters(wanted)


async def ensure_consumer(js: Any, s: ScoreSettings, replica: int) -> None:
    """Create the replica's consumer, or update its filters if they changed (new partition count
    or replica count). An unchanged consumer is left alone so it keeps its position."""
    wanted = consumer_config(s, replica)
    try:
        info = await js.consumer_info(s.nats_stream, consumer_name(s, replica))
    except NotFoundError:
        log.info("creating consumer %s", consumer_name(s, replica))
        await js.add_consumer(s.nats_stream, wanted)
        return
    if needs_update(info.config, wanted):
        log.info(
            "updating consumer %s: filters %s -> %s",
            consumer_name(s, replica),
            sorted(configured_filters(info.config)),
            sorted(configured_filters(wanted)),
        )
        await js.add_consumer(s.nats_stream, wanted)


def score_stream_config(s: ScoreSettings) -> StreamConfig:
    return StreamConfig(
        name=s.score_stream,
        subjects=[f"{s.score_subject_prefix}.>"],
        storage=StorageType.FILE,
        retention=RetentionPolicy.LIMITS,
        discard=DiscardPolicy.OLD,
        max_age=float(s.score_stream_max_age_s),
        num_replicas=s.nats_stream_replicas,
    )


async def ensure_score_stream(js: Any, s: ScoreSettings) -> None:
    """Create ``CORVUS_SCORE`` if missing; an existing stream is left alone (operators own it)."""
    try:
        info = await js.stream_info(s.score_stream)
    except NotFoundError:
        log.info("creating stream %s", s.score_stream)
        await js.add_stream(score_stream_config(s))
    else:
        await raise_replicas(js, info, s.nats_stream_replicas)


class NatsScoreIO:
    """One NATS connection serving as score source (capture consumer) and publisher."""

    def __init__(self, nc: Any, js: Any, sub: Any, settings: ScoreSettings) -> None:
        self._nc = nc
        self._js = js
        self._sub = sub
        self._s = settings

    @classmethod
    async def connect(cls, s: ScoreSettings, replica: int) -> NatsScoreIO:
        nc = await nats.connect(s.nats_url, **connect_options(s, f"corvus-score-{replica}"))
        js = nc.jetstream()
        await ensure_stream(js, s)
        await ensure_score_stream(js, s)
        await ensure_consumer(js, s, replica)
        sub = await js.pull_subscribe_bind(consumer_name(s, replica), stream=s.nats_stream)
        return cls(nc, js, sub, s)

    @property
    def connected(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self._nc.is_connected)

    async def fetch(self) -> list[Any]:
        try:
            msgs = await self._sub.fetch(self._s.fetch_batch, timeout=self._s.fetch_timeout_s)
        except NatsTimeout:
            return []
        return [NatsMessage(m) for m in msgs]

    async def publish(self, subject: str, data: bytes) -> None:
        await self._js.publish(subject, data)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._nc.drain()

```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/ort_session.py`:

```py
"""ONNX Runtime session factory (CPU, sequential, inter-op 1)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import onnxruntime as ort


class OrtSession:
    """An ``InferenceSession`` whose first input is ``x`` (batch axis dynamic)."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path, intra_op_threads: int) -> None:
        opts = ort.SessionOptions()
        opts.intra_op_num_threads = max(1, intra_op_threads)
        opts.inter_op_num_threads = 1
        opts.execution_mode = ort.ExecutionMode.ORT_SEQUENTIAL
        opts.log_severity_level = 3
        self._session = ort.InferenceSession(str(path), opts, providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
        first = self._session.get_inputs()[0]
        self._input = first.name
        self._shape: tuple[int | str | None, ...] = tuple(first.shape)
        self._outputs = tuple(o.name for o in self._session.get_outputs())

    @property
    def output_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return self._outputs

    @property
    def input_shape(self) -> tuple[int | str | None, ...]:
        return self._shape

    def run(self, x: np.ndarray) -> list[np.ndarray]:
        return list(self._session.run(None, {self._input: x}))


def create_session(path: Path, intra_op_threads: int) -> OrtSession:
    return OrtSession(path, intra_op_threads)
```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/partitions.py`:

```py
"""Partition ownership of a scorer replica and the JetStream filter subjects it implies.

The partition token format is the one of the plugin (``Partitioner.java``): decimal with at least
two digits; for more than 100 partitions the width grows to the digits of the highest partition.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re

_ORDINAL = re.compile(r"-(\d+)$")


def partition_token(partition: int, partitions: int) -> str:
    """The last subject token of ``partition`` (``00``..``15`` for 16, ``000``..``127`` for 128)."""
    if not 0 <= partition < partitions:
        raise ValueError(f"partition {partition} outside 0..{partitions - 1}")
    width = max(2, len(str(partitions - 1)))
    return f"{partition:0{width}d}"


def partition_of(session_id: bytes, partitions: int) -> int:
    """First 4 bytes of the session id, big-endian unsigned, modulo ``partitions``."""
    head = int.from_bytes(session_id[:4].ljust(4, b"\x00"), "big")
    return head % partitions


def owned_partitions(replica: int, replicas: int, partitions: int) -> list[int]:
    """Partitions ``p`` with ``p mod replicas == replica``."""
    if replicas < 1 or not 0 <= replica < replicas:
        raise ValueError(f"replica {replica} outside 0..{replicas - 1}")
    return [p for p in range(partitions) if p % replicas == replica]


def filter_subjects(
    replica: int, replicas: int, partitions: int, prefix: str = "corvus.capture.v1"
) -> list[str]:
    """``<prefix>.*.<pp>`` for every partition the replica owns (``*`` = proxy id)."""
    return [
        f"{prefix}.*.{partition_token(p, partitions)}"
        for p in owned_partitions(replica, replicas, partitions)
    ]


def replica_index(configured: int | None, replicas: int, hostname: str | None = None) -> int:
    """Configured index, else the ordinal suffix of a StatefulSet hostname.

    A standalone scorer (one replica) falls back to 0; with several replicas an index that cannot
    be determined is an error, because two replicas silently sharing an index would double-score.
    """
    if configured is not None:
        index = configured
    else:
        host = hostname if hostname is not None else os.environ.get("HOSTNAME", "")
        m = _ORDINAL.search(host)
        if m is None:
            if replicas > 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    "cannot determine the replica index: set CORVUS_SCORE_REPLICA_INDEX or use a "
                    "StatefulSet hostname ending in -<ordinal>"
                )
            return 0
        index = int(m.group(1))
    if index >= replicas:
        raise ValueError(f"replica index {index} must be below the replica count {replicas}")
    return index

```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/pgscores.py`:

```py
"""PostgreSQL adapter of the scoring catalog port (psycopg 3 async pool)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Any

from psycopg_pool import AsyncConnectionPool

from .ports import ModelEntry, ScoreRecord, SessionLookup

_UPSERT_LATEST = (
    "INSERT INTO corvus.scores_latest (pseudonym, game_context, domain, model_name, model_version,"
    " stage, score, smoothed, windows, session_id, segment, updated_at)"
    " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)"
    " ON CONFLICT (pseudonym, game_context, domain, model_name) DO UPDATE SET"
    "  model_version = EXCLUDED.model_version, stage = EXCLUDED.stage, score = EXCLUDED.score,"
    "  smoothed = EXCLUDED.smoothed, windows = EXCLUDED.windows,"
    "  session_id = EXCLUDED.session_id, segment = EXCLUDED.segment,"
    "  updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at"
    " WHERE EXCLUDED.updated_at >= corvus.scores_latest.updated_at"
)
_INSERT_HISTORY = (
    "INSERT INTO corvus.score_history (pseudonym, session_id, segment, game_context, domain,"
    " model_name, model_version, stage, score, smoothed, windows, window_start_offset_nanos,"
    " window_end_offset_nanos, scored_at)"
    " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)"
)


def latest_params(r: ScoreRecord) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
    return (
        r.pseudonym, r.game_context, r.domain, r.model_name, r.model_version, r.stage, r.score,
        r.smoothed, r.windows, r.session_id, r.segment, r.scored_at,
    )  # fmt: skip


def history_params(r: ScoreRecord) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
    return (
        r.pseudonym, r.session_id, r.segment, r.game_context, r.domain, r.model_name,
        r.model_version, r.stage, r.score, r.smoothed, r.windows, r.window_start_offset_nanos,
        r.window_end_offset_nanos, r.scored_at,
    )  # fmt: skip


class PgScoreCatalog:
    def __init__(self, pool: AsyncConnectionPool[Any]) -> None:
        self._pool = pool

    @classmethod
    async def open(cls, dsn: str, max_size: int) -> PgScoreCatalog:
        pool: AsyncConnectionPool[Any] = AsyncConnectionPool(
            dsn, min_size=1, max_size=max_size, open=False
        )
        await pool.open(wait=True, timeout=30)
        return cls(pool)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._pool.close()

    async def ping(self) -> None:
        async with self._pool.connection() as conn:
            await conn.execute("SELECT 1")

    async def lookup_session(self, session_id: bytes) -> SessionLookup | None:
        async with self._pool.connection() as conn:
            cur = await conn.execute(
                "SELECT s.pseudonym, p.key_id, s.observed_protocol, s.client_protocol"
                " FROM corvus.sessions s"
                " JOIN corvus.players p USING (pseudonym)"
                " WHERE s.session_id = %s AND NOT s.orphan AND p.erased_at IS NULL",
                (session_id,),
            )
            row = await cur.fetchone()
            if row is None:
                return None
            cur = await conn.execute(
                "SELECT segment, game_context FROM corvus.segments WHERE session_id = %s",
                (session_id,),
            )
            segments = {int(r[0]): str(r[1]) for r in await cur.fetchall()}
        return SessionLookup(session_id, bytes(row[0]), row[1], int(row[2]), segments, int(row[3]))

    async def active_models(self) -> list[ModelEntry]:
        async with self._pool.connection() as conn:
            cur = await conn.execute(
                "SELECT id::text, name, version, candidate_type, game_context, domain, stage,"
                " onnx_key FROM corvus.models WHERE stage IN ('shadow', 'canary', 'enforce')"
                " ORDER BY created_at, id"
            )
            return [ModelEntry(*r) for r in await cur.fetchall()]

    async def write_scores(
        self, latest: Sequence[ScoreRecord], history: Sequence[ScoreRecord]
    ) -> None:
        async with self._pool.connection() as conn, conn.transaction(), conn.cursor() as cur:
            if latest:
                await cur.executemany(_UPSERT_LATEST, [latest_params(r) for r in latest])
            if history:
                await cur.executemany(_INSERT_HISTORY, [history_params(r) for r in history])
```

```py
"""Ports of the scoring service; production adapters in ``pgscores``, ``nats_io``, ``ort_session``

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

# Stages that are loaded and scored; only the last two are published.
```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/raw.py`:

```py
"""Raw-byte models in the scorer: window container, frame mapping, batching and the latency guard.

The windowing itself is ``corvus_ml.raw.streaming`` (the same code that cuts the training
windows); this module only adapts it to the capture stream and to the micro-batch. Payloads reach
the scorer as plaintext frames; they are tokenized on arrival and only token ids are kept, for at
most one window (see ``SegmentWindower``). Nothing here persists or logs payload bytes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
from corvus_ml.raw.streaming import RawFrame


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RawWindow:
    """A completed raw-byte window: the model input of one window (or macro window).

    ``x`` is ``(packets, T + 1)`` or ``(macro, packets, T + 1)``; it holds token ids and packet
    times, never payload bytes. Quacks like ``CompletedWindow`` for what the scorer records.
    """

    session_id: bytes
    segment: int
    start_offset_nanos: int
    end_offset_nanos: int
    x: np.ndarray

    @property
    def n_packets(self) -> int:
        return int(self.x.shape[-2])


def raw_frame(frame: Any) -> RawFrame:
    """Capture proto ``Frame`` to the windower's frame; the payload is plaintext at this point."""
    payload = bytes(frame.payload) if frame.payload else None
    return RawFrame(
        seq=frame.seq,
        offset_nanos=frame.offset_nanos,
        direction=frame.direction,
        packet_type=frame.packet_type,
        payload=payload,
        payload_original_size=frame.payload_original_size,
    )


def stack_inputs(windows: Sequence[RawWindow]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Pad the windows to the longest packet count of the micro-batch and stack them.

    Padding packets are all zero (``[PAD]`` ids, time 0), which the model masks; the output of a
    window does not depend on how much padding follows it.
    """
    xs = [w.x for w in windows]
    p_max = max(x.shape[-2] for x in xs)
    first = xs[0]
    out = np.zeros((len(xs), *first.shape[:-2], p_max, first.shape[-1]), dtype=np.float32)
    for i, x in enumerate(xs):
        out[i, ..., : x.shape[-2], :] = x
    return out


# --- latency guard -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Measured with default-size models (d_model 64, 2 global layers), ONNX Runtime CPU, one window per
# call, one intra-op thread (docs/reference/raw-byte-tokenizer.md section 10): (packets, ms).
_CLASSIFIER_1T_MS = ((128, 3.8), (512, 17.0), (1024, 41.9))
_TWO_THREAD_FACTOR = 0.6  # 2.3/3.8, 10.0/17.0, 25.6/41.9; not extrapolated beyond two threads
_ANOMALY_FACTOR = 2.6  # the prediction heads of raw_hier_anomaly: 10.0/3.8, 44.7/17.0, 108.7/41.9
_P99_OVER_MEAN = 1.15  # 47.6 / 41.9


def estimate_p99_ms(max_packets: int, intra_op_threads: int, *, anomaly: bool = False) -> float:
    """Rough p99 latency of one window of ``max_packets`` packets for a default-size model.

    Piecewise linear through the measured points (proportional below the first, last slope above
    the last). A larger model needs more (``d_model`` 128 with 4 layers: about 1.6 times).
    """
    pts = _CLASSIFIER_1T_MS
    if max_packets <= pts[0][0]:
        ms = pts[0][1] * max_packets / pts[0][0]
    else:
        # the segment containing max_packets; above the last point the last segment continues
        (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = next(
            ((a, b) for a, b in zip(pts, pts[1:], strict=False) if max_packets <= b[0]),
            (pts[-2], pts[-1]),
        )
        ms = y0 + (y1 - y0) * (max_packets - x0) / (x1 - x0)
    if intra_op_threads > 1:
        ms *= _TWO_THREAD_FACTOR
    if anomaly:
        ms *= _ANOMALY_FACTOR
    return ms * _P99_OVER_MEAN


def budget_warning(
    name: str, max_packets: int, intra_op_threads: int, budget_ms: float | None, *, anomaly: bool
) -> str | None:
    """A message if the estimated p99 of a full window exceeds the budget, else None."""
    if budget_ms is None:
        return None
    est = estimate_p99_ms(max_packets, intra_op_threads, anomaly=anomaly)
    if est <= budget_ms:
        return None
    return (
        f"raw-byte model {name}: max_packets={max_packets} costs an estimated p99 of {est:.1f} ms "
        f"per full window on {intra_op_threads} thread(s), above the budget of {budget_ms:.1f} ms; "
        "retrain with a smaller max_packets or raise CORVUS_SCORE_P99_BUDGET_MS"
    )

```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/scorer.py`:

```py
"""Runs one micro-batch through the loaded models, smooths, publishes and persists the scores."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import re
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from concurrent.futures import Executor
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
from corvus_ml.features.featurizer import CompletedWindow
from corvus_ml.features.model_input import model_inputs

from ..clock import Clock
from .batching import Batch, PendingWindow
from .metrics import ScoreMetrics
from .models import LoadedModel, ModelSet, scores_from_outputs
from .ports import PUBLISHED_STAGES, ScorePublisher, ScoreRecord
from .raw import RawWindow, stack_inputs
from .score_proto import score_pb
from .smoothing import EmaTracker
from .writer import ScoreWriter

log = logging.getLogger("corvus.score.scorer")

_SUBJECT_UNSAFE = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]")
_STAGE = {
    "shadow": score_pb.Score.STAGE_SHADOW,
    "canary": score_pb.Score.STAGE_CANARY,
    "enforce": score_pb.Score.STAGE_ENFORCE,
}


def score_subject(prefix: str, game_context: str) -> str:
    """``<prefix>.<game_context>`` with characters that are not valid in a subject token
    (``.``, ``*``, ``>``, whitespace, ...) replaced by ``_``."""
    return f"{prefix}.{_SUBJECT_UNSAFE.sub('_', game_context)}"


def encode_score(record: ScoreRecord, key_id: str) -> bytes:
    msg = score_pb.Score(
        player_pseudonym=record.pseudonym,
        pseudonym_key_id=key_id,
        session_id=record.session_id,
        segment=record.segment,
        game_context=record.game_context,
        domain=record.domain,
        model_name=record.model_name,
        model_version=record.model_version,
        stage=_STAGE[record.stage],
        score=record.score,
        score_smoothed=record.smoothed,
        windows=record.windows,
        window_start_offset_nanos=record.window_start_offset_nanos,
        window_end_offset_nanos=record.window_end_offset_nanos,
        scored_at_unix_millis=int(record.scored_at.timestamp() * 1000),
    )
    return bytes(msg.SerializeToString())


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Hit:
    index: int  # position of the window in the batch
    model: LoadedModel
    score: float


def build_input(model: LoadedModel, windows: list[PendingWindow]) -> np.ndarray:
    """The model's input tensor: stacked token windows for raw-byte models, else the feature
    adapter shared with the evaluation harness."""
    kind = model.input_kind
    if kind == "raw_bytes":
        raws = [w.window for w in windows if isinstance(w.window, RawWindow)]
        if len(raws) != len(windows):
            raise TypeError("a raw-byte model was handed a window that is not a raw window")
        return stack_inputs(raws)
    feats = [w.window for w in windows if isinstance(w.window, CompletedWindow)]
    if len(feats) != len(windows):
        raise TypeError(f"a {kind} model was handed a raw window")
    x: np.ndarray = model_inputs(feats, kind, model.spec)
    return x


def infer(model: LoadedModel, windows: list[PendingWindow]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, float]:
    """Blocking: model input via the shared adapter, then ONNX Runtime. Runs in the thread pool."""
    started = time.perf_counter()
    x = build_input(model, windows)
    outputs = model.session.run(x)
    scores = scores_from_outputs(
        model.entry.candidate_type,
        outputs,
        getattr(model.session, "output_names", None),
        model.semantics,
    )
    if len(scores) != len(windows):
        raise ValueError(f"model returned {len(scores)} scores for {len(windows)} windows")
    return scores, time.perf_counter() - started


class Scorer:
    def __init__(
        self,
        models: Callable[[], ModelSet],
        pool: Executor,
        ema: EmaTracker,
        writer: ScoreWriter,
        publisher: ScorePublisher,
        subject_prefix: str,
        clock: Clock,
        metrics: ScoreMetrics,
    ) -> None:
        self._models = models
        self._pool = pool
        self._ema = ema
        self._writer = writer
        self._publisher = publisher
        self._prefix = subject_prefix
        self._clock = clock
        self._m = metrics

    async def score(self, batch: Batch) -> None:
        """Score ``batch``; never raises (failures are logged and counted)."""
        try:
            if batch.windows:
                await self._score_windows(batch.windows)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("scoring a batch of %d windows failed", len(batch.windows))
        finally:
            for session_id in batch.releases:
                self._ema.release_session(session_id)

    async def _score_windows(self, windows: list[PendingWindow]) -> None:
        self._m.batch_size.observe(len(windows))
        models = self._models()  # one snapshot for the whole batch: a swap never splits it
        groups: dict[str, tuple[LoadedModel, list[int]]] = {}
        for i, pw in enumerate(windows):
            matching = models.matching(pw.game_context, pw.config)
            if not matching:
                self._m.windows_skipped.labels("no_model").inc()
                continue
            for model in matching:
                groups.setdefault(model.id, (model, []))[1].append(i)

        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        jobs = [
            (model, idx, loop.run_in_executor(self._pool, infer, model, [windows[i] for i in idx]))
            for model, idx in groups.values()
        ]
        hits: list[_Hit] = []
        for model, idx, future in jobs:
            name = f"{model.entry.name}:{model.entry.version}"
            try:
                scores, seconds = await future
            except Exception:
                log.exception("model %s failed on a batch of %d windows", name, len(idx))
                self._m.inference_errors.labels(name).inc()
                continue
            self._m.inference_seconds.labels(name).observe(seconds)
            for i, s in zip(idx, scores.tolist(), strict=True):
                if s != s:  # NaN
                    self._m.inference_errors.labels(name).inc()
                    continue
                hits.append(_Hit(i, model, s))

        # Window order, so the smoothing of one (player, segment, model) sees its windows in order.
        hits.sort(key=lambda h: h.index)
        publishes: list[tuple[str, bytes, str]] = []
        for hit in hits:
            pw = windows[hit.index]
            record = self._record(pw, hit)
            self._writer.submit(record)
            self._m.windows_scored.labels(
                f"{hit.model.entry.name}:{hit.model.entry.version}", record.stage
            ).inc()
            if record.stage in PUBLISHED_STAGES:  # shadow is persisted, never published
                publishes.append(
                    (
                        score_subject(self._prefix, pw.game_context),
                        encode_score(record, pw.key_id),
                        record.stage,
                    )
                )
        await self._publish(publishes)

    def _record(self, pw: PendingWindow, hit: _Hit) -> ScoreRecord:
        w, entry = pw.window, hit.model.entry
        smoothed, count = self._ema.update(
            (pw.pseudonym, w.segment, entry.id), w.session_id, hit.score
        )
        return ScoreRecord(
            pseudonym=pw.pseudonym,
            session_id=w.session_id,
            segment=w.segment,
            game_context=pw.game_context,
            domain=entry.domain,
            model_name=entry.name,
            model_version=entry.version,
            stage=entry.stage,
            score=hit.score,
            smoothed=smoothed,
            windows=count,
            window_start_offset_nanos=w.start_offset_nanos,
            window_end_offset_nanos=w.end_offset_nanos,
            scored_at=self._clock(),
        )

    async def _publish(self, publishes: list[tuple[str, bytes, str]]) -> None:
        if not publishes:
            return
        results = await asyncio.gather(
            *(self._publisher.publish(subject, data) for subject, data, _ in publishes),
            return_exceptions=True,
        )
        for (subject, _, stage), result in zip(publishes, results, strict=True):
            if isinstance(result, BaseException):
                log.warning("publishing a score to %s failed: %s", subject, result)
                self._m.publish_failures.inc()
            else:
                self._m.published.labels(stage).inc()

```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/service.py`:

```py
"""The scoring pipeline: capture envelopes in, micro-batched scores out.

Per message: decode, keep the session/segment state, feed the frames into the incremental
featurizers, hand the completed windows to the micro-batcher and ack. Acks happen right after the
frames were fed (scoring never replays history, so there is nothing to redeliver for).

A session the scorer never saw start (the consumer delivers only new messages) is looked up in the
catalog, which ingest keeps up to date; if the catalog does not know it either the batch is skipped
and counted. Lookups that fail are remembered for a short time so a burst of batches does not hit
the database once per message.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
from collections import OrderedDict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

from corvus_ml.features.config import FeaturizerConfig
from google.protobuf.message import DecodeError

from ..clock import Clock
from ..ports import Message
from ..proto import pb
from .batching import Batch, MicroBatcher, PendingWindow
from .frames import feature_frame
from .metrics import ScoreMetrics
from .models import ModelSet
from .ports import ScoreCatalog, SessionLookup
from .raw import RawWindow, raw_frame
from .scorer import Scorer
from .sessions import ConfiguredWindow, SessionState, SessionTracker
from .settings import ScoreSettings

log = logging.getLogger("corvus.score")


class LookupFailedError(Exception):
    """The catalog could not be queried; the message is retried a few times, then skipped."""


def tick_end_hint(observed_protocol: int, min_protocol: int) -> bool | None:
    """Whether the run sends CLIENT_TICK_END, as far as it is known beforehand: clients below
    ``min_protocol`` cannot send it (False); newer ones may (None, inferred from the frames)."""
    return False if observed_protocol < min_protocol else None


class ScoringService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: ScoreSettings,
        catalog: ScoreCatalog,
        models: Any,
        tracker: SessionTracker,
        batcher: MicroBatcher,
        scorer: Scorer,
        clock: Clock,
        metrics: ScoreMetrics,
    ) -> None:
        self._s = settings
        self._catalog = catalog
        self._models = models  # ModelManager or anything with ``current: ModelSet``
        self._tracker = tracker
        self._batcher = batcher
        self._scorer = scorer
        self._clock = clock
        self._m = metrics
        self._missing: OrderedDict[bytes, datetime] = OrderedDict()  # session -> retry not before
        self._inflight: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None

    @property
    def model_set(self) -> ModelSet:
        current: ModelSet = self._models.current
        return current

    # ----- messages ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def handle(self, msg: Message) -> None:
        """Process and ack (or nak/term) one message. Never raises."""
        try:
            env = pb.Envelope.FromString(msg.data)
        except DecodeError:
            self._m.messages.labels("decode_error").inc()
            await self._settle(msg.term())
            return
        try:
            retry = await self._dispatch(env, msg)
        except LookupFailedError:
            retry = msg.delivery_count < self._s.unknown_session_max_deliver
            if not retry:
                self._m.unknown_session_skips.inc()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("failed to handle message %s", msg.msg_id)
            self._m.messages.labels("error").inc()
            retry = False
        if retry:
            self._m.messages.labels("retry").inc()
            await self._settle(msg.nak(self._s.nak_delay_s))
        else:
            await self._settle(msg.ack())
        self._dispatch_ready()

    @staticmethod
    async def _settle(op: Any) -> None:
        try:
            await op
        except Exception:
            log.warning("could not acknowledge a message", exc_info=True)

    async def _dispatch(self, env: Any, msg: Message) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the message should be redelivered later."""
        body = env.WhichOneof("body")
        if body == "session_start":
            self._on_session_start(env.session_start)
        elif body == "segment_start":
            return await self._on_segment_start(env.segment_start, msg)
        elif body == "batch":
            return await self._on_batch(env.batch, msg)
        elif body == "session_end":
            self._on_session_end(bytes(env.session_end.session_id))
        else:
            self._m.messages.labels("empty").inc()
            return False
        self._m.messages.labels(body).inc()
        return False

    def _on_session_start(self, s: Any) -> None:
        if bytes(s.session_id) in self._tracker:
            return  # redelivered SessionStart: keep the featurizer state
        state = SessionState(
            session_id=bytes(s.session_id),
            pseudonym=bytes(s.player_pseudonym),
            key_id=s.pseudonym_key_id,
            observed_protocol=s.observed_protocol_version,
            client_protocol=s.client_protocol_version,
        )
        self._track(state)

    async def _on_segment_start(self, s: Any, msg: Message) -> bool:
        sid = bytes(s.session_id)
        state = self._tracker.get(sid)
        if state is None:
            state = await self._resolve(sid)
            if state is None:
                return self._unknown()
        state.segments[s.segment] = s.game_context
        hint = tick_end_hint(state.observed_protocol, self._s.score_tick_end_min_protocol)
        self._queue(state, state.begin_segment(s.segment, hint))
        self._m.messages.labels("segment_start").inc()
        return False

    async def _on_batch(self, b: Any, msg: Message) -> bool:
        sid = bytes(b.session_id)
        state = self._tracker.get(sid)
        if state is None:
            state = await self._resolve(sid)
        if state is not None and b.segment not in state.segments:
            await self._refresh_segments(state)
        if state is None or b.segment not in state.segments:
            return self._unknown()
        game_context = state.segments[b.segment]
        models = self.model_set
        configs = models.configs_for(game_context)
        raw_specs = models.raw_specs_for(game_context)
        if not configs and not raw_specs:
            self._m.messages.labels("no_model").inc()
            return False
        completed: list[ConfiguredWindow] = []
        if configs:
            frames = [feature_frame(sid, b.segment, f) for f in b.frames]
            hint = tick_end_hint(state.observed_protocol, self._s.score_tick_end_min_protocol)
            completed += state.feed(b.segment, frames, configs, hint)
        if raw_specs:
            # plaintext payloads: tokenized on arrival, only token ids stay in the windower
            completed += state.feed_raw(
                b.segment,
                [raw_frame(f) for f in b.frames],
                raw_specs,
                game_context,
                self._s.score_raw_max_buffered_frames,
            )
            self._m.raw_frames_dropped.inc(state.raw_frames_dropped)
            state.raw_frames_dropped = 0
        self._m.frames_fed.inc(len(b.frames))
        self._queue(state, completed)
        self._m.messages.labels("batch").inc()
        return False

    def _on_session_end(self, session_id: bytes) -> None:
        state = self._tracker.pop(session_id)
        self._missing.pop(session_id, None)
        self._m.sessions_tracked.set(len(self._tracker))
        if state is not None:
            self._queue(state, state.flush())
        self._batcher.release(session_id)

    # ----- session state ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _track(self, state: SessionState) -> None:
        self._missing.pop(state.session_id, None)
        for evicted in self._tracker.put(state):
            self._evict(evicted, "lru")
        self._m.sessions_tracked.set(len(self._tracker))

    def _evict(self, state: SessionState, reason: str) -> None:
        self._m.session_evictions.labels(reason).inc()
        self._queue(state, state.flush())
        self._batcher.release(state.session_id)

    async def _resolve(self, session_id: bytes) -> SessionState | None:
        """Catalog fallback for a session the scorer did not see start."""
        retry_at = self._missing.get(session_id)
        if retry_at is not None and self._clock() < retry_at:
            return None
        lookup = await self._lookup(session_id)
        if lookup is None:
            self._m.catalog_fallbacks.labels("miss").inc()
            self._remember_missing(session_id)
            return None
        self._m.catalog_fallbacks.labels("hit").inc()
        state = SessionState(
            session_id,
            lookup.pseudonym,
            lookup.key_id,
            lookup.observed_protocol,
            dict(lookup.segments),
            lookup.client_protocol,
        )
        self._track(state)
        return state

    async def _lookup(self, session_id: bytes) -> SessionLookup | None:
        try:
            return await self._catalog.lookup_session(session_id)
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("catalog lookup of session %s failed: %s", session_id.hex(), e)
            self._m.catalog_fallbacks.labels("error").inc()
            raise LookupFailedError from e

    async def _refresh_segments(self, state: SessionState) -> None:
        """A segment the scorer did not see start: ingest may have written it by now."""
        key = state.session_id
        retry_at = self._missing.get(key)
        if retry_at is not None and self._clock() < retry_at:
            return
        lookup = await self._lookup(key)
        if lookup is None:
            self._remember_missing(key)
            return
        for segment, ctx in lookup.segments.items():
            state.segments.setdefault(segment, ctx)
        self._missing.pop(key, None)

    def _remember_missing(self, key: bytes) -> None:
        self._missing[key] = self._clock() + timedelta(seconds=self._s.score_lookup_retry_s)
        self._missing.move_to_end(key)
        while len(self._missing) > self._s.score_lookup_cache_max:
            self._missing.popitem(last=False)

    def _unknown(self) -> bool:
        self._m.unknown_session_skips.inc()
        self._m.messages.labels("unknown_session").inc()
        return False

    # ----- windows and batches ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def _queue(self, state: SessionState, completed: list[ConfiguredWindow]) -> None:
        items: list[PendingWindow] = []
        for cfg, window in completed:
            ctx = state.segments.get(window.segment)
            if ctx is None:
                self._m.windows_skipped.labels("no_context").inc()
                continue
            if isinstance(window, RawWindow):
                self._m.raw_window_packets.observe(window.n_packets)
            items.append(PendingWindow(window, cfg, state.pseudonym, state.key_id, ctx))
        if completed:
            self._m.windows_completed.inc(len(completed))
        if items:
            self._batcher.add(items)
            self._m.pending_windows.set(len(self._batcher))

    def tick(self) -> None:
        """Periodic: evict idle sessions and dispatch a batch whose wait elapsed."""
        for state in self._tracker.evict_idle():
            self._evict(state, "idle")
        self._m.sessions_tracked.set(len(self._tracker))
        self._dispatch_ready()

    def _dispatch_ready(self) -> None:
        """Start scoring the next batch if one is ready and none is running (single in-flight
        batch keeps the per-key smoothing order)."""
        if self._inflight is not None and not self._inflight.done():
            return
        if not self._batcher.ready():
            return
        batch = self._batcher.take()
        self._m.pending_windows.set(len(self._batcher))
        self._inflight = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._run_batch(batch))

    async def _run_batch(self, batch: Batch) -> None:
        await self._scorer.score(batch)

    async def backpressure(self) -> None:
        """Wait for the running batch if too many windows are queued behind it."""
        if len(self._batcher) >= self._s.score_pending_windows_max and self._inflight is not None:
            await asyncio.shield(self._inflight)

    async def drain(self) -> None:
        """Score every pending window (also those not yet due)."""
        while True:
            if self._inflight is not None and not self._inflight.done():
                await asyncio.shield(self._inflight)
                continue
            batch = self._batcher.take()
            if not batch:
                return
            self._m.pending_windows.set(len(self._batcher))
            await self._scorer.score(batch)

    # ----- introspection for the model set ----------------------------------------------------

    def configs(self, game_context: str) -> frozenset[FeaturizerConfig]:
        return self.model_set.configs_for(game_context)

```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/sessions.py`:

```py
"""Per-session featurizer state: a bounded LRU with idle eviction."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import OrderedDict
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

from corvus_ml.features.config import FeaturizerConfig
from corvus_ml.features.featurizer import CompletedWindow, SessionFeaturizer
from corvus_ml.features.frames import Frame
from corvus_ml.raw.spec import RawBytesSpec
from corvus_ml.raw.streaming import FrameEncoder, ModelWindow, RawFrame, SegmentWindower

from ..clock import Clock
from .raw import RawWindow

type ConfiguredWindow = tuple[FeaturizerConfig | RawBytesSpec, CompletedWindow | RawWindow]


@dataclass
class SessionState:
    """Everything the scorer keeps for one session."""

    session_id: bytes
    pseudonym: bytes
    key_id: str
    observed_protocol: int
    segments: dict[int, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # segment -> game_context
    # the protocol the client speaks (``sessions.client_protocol``): the raw-byte models' [PROTO_*]
    client_protocol: int | None = None
    last_seen: datetime = datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
    # one incremental featurizer per distinct window configuration of the models in use
    _featurizers: dict[FeaturizerConfig, SessionFeaturizer] = field(default_factory=dict)
    _fz_segment: dict[FeaturizerConfig, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # raw-byte models: one streaming windower per distinct windowing, for the current segment only
    _raw: dict[RawBytesSpec, SegmentWindower] = field(default_factory=dict)
    _raw_segment: int | None = None
    raw_frames_dropped: int = 0  # buffered frames lost to the cap since the last ``take``

    def begin_segment(self, segment: int, tick_end: bool | None) -> list[ConfiguredWindow]:
        """Start ``segment`` in every featurizer; returns the tail windows of the previous run."""
        out: list[ConfiguredWindow] = self.flush_raw()
        for cfg, fz in self._featurizers.items():
            out.extend((cfg, w) for w in fz.begin_segment(segment, tick_end))
            self._fz_segment[cfg] = segment
        return out

    def feed(
        self,
        segment: int,
        frames: Iterable[Frame],
        configs: Iterable[FeaturizerConfig],
        tick_end: bool | None,
    ) -> list[ConfiguredWindow]:
        """Feed frames of ``segment`` to the featurizer of every config in ``configs``."""
        batch = list(frames)
        out: list[ConfiguredWindow] = []
        for cfg in configs:
            fz = self._featurizers.get(cfg)
            if fz is None:
                fz = self._featurizers[cfg] = SessionFeaturizer(self.session_id, cfg)
            if self._fz_segment.get(cfg) != segment:
                out.extend((cfg, w) for w in fz.begin_segment(segment, tick_end))
                self._fz_segment[cfg] = segment
            for frame in batch:
                out.extend((cfg, w) for w in fz.feed(frame))
        return out

    def feed_raw(
        self,
        segment: int,
        frames: Sequence[RawFrame],
        specs: Mapping[RawBytesSpec, FrameEncoder],
        game_context: str,
        max_buffered: int | None,
    ) -> list[ConfiguredWindow]:
        """Feed plaintext frames of ``segment`` to the windower of every raw-byte windowing in
        ``specs``. Windows never cross a segment: a new segment first flushes the old windowers."""
        out: list[ConfiguredWindow] = []
        if self._raw_segment is not None and self._raw_segment != segment:
            out.extend(self.flush_raw())
        self._raw_segment = segment
        for spec in [s for s in self._raw if s not in specs]:
            del self._raw[spec]  # no model needs this windowing any more
        for spec, tokenizer in specs.items():
            w = self._raw.get(spec)
            if w is None:
                w = self._raw[spec] = SegmentWindower(
                    spec,
                    tokenizer,
                    self.session_id,
                    segment,
                    game_context,
                    self.client_protocol,
                    max_buffered,
                )
            before = w.stats.dropped_overflow
            out.extend((spec, self._to_raw(m)) for m in w.feed(frames))
            self.raw_frames_dropped += w.stats.dropped_overflow - before
        return out

    def _to_raw(self, m: ModelWindow) -> RawWindow:
        return RawWindow(self.session_id, m.segment, m.start_offset_nanos, m.end_offset_nanos, m.x)

    def flush_raw(self) -> list[ConfiguredWindow]:
        """Tail windows of the raw-byte windowers; frees their buffers."""
        out: list[ConfiguredWindow] = [
            (spec, self._to_raw(m)) for spec, w in self._raw.items() for m in w.flush()
        ]
        self._raw.clear()
        self._raw_segment = None
        return out

    def flush(self) -> list[ConfiguredWindow]:
        """Tail windows of every featurizer (session end or eviction); frees the featurizers."""
        out: list[ConfiguredWindow] = self.flush_raw()
        for cfg, fz in self._featurizers.items():
            out.extend((cfg, w) for w in fz.flush())
        self._featurizers.clear()
        self._fz_segment.clear()
        return out

    @property
    def featurizer_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self._featurizers)


class SessionTracker:
    """LRU of :class:`SessionState` bounded by count and idle time."""

    def __init__(self, max_sessions: int, idle: timedelta, clock: Clock) -> None:
        self._max = max_sessions
        self._idle = idle
        self._clock = clock
        self._states: OrderedDict[bytes, SessionState] = OrderedDict()

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._states)

    def __contains__(self, session_id: bytes) -> bool:
        return session_id in self._states

    def get(self, session_id: bytes) -> SessionState | None:
        state = self._states.get(session_id)
        if state is not None:
            state.last_seen = self._clock()
            self._states.move_to_end(session_id)
        return state

    def put(self, state: SessionState) -> list[SessionState]:
        """Insert (or replace); returns the states evicted to stay within the bound."""
        state.last_seen = self._clock()
        self._states[state.session_id] = state
        self._states.move_to_end(state.session_id)
        evicted: list[SessionState] = []
        while len(self._states) > self._max:
            _, oldest = self._states.popitem(last=False)
            evicted.append(oldest)
        return evicted

    def pop(self, session_id: bytes) -> SessionState | None:
        return self._states.pop(session_id, None)

    def evict_idle(self) -> list[SessionState]:
        """Remove and return the states not touched for longer than the idle limit."""
        cutoff = self._clock() - self._idle
        stale = [sid for sid, s in self._states.items() if s.last_seen < cutoff]
        return [self._states.pop(sid) for sid in stale]
```

```py
    score_tick_end_min_protocol: int = Field(default=768, ge=0)

    # and windowing (the oldest are dropped and counted).
    score_raw_max_buffered_frames: int = Field(default=16_384, ge=64)

    # it logs a warning at load time (the model is still served). Mirrors the registry gate
    # CORVUS_GATE_MAX_P99_LATENCY_MS; 0 disables the check.
    score_p99_budget_ms: float = Field(default=10.0, ge=0)

    # Models
    score_models_dir: Path = Path(

    )  # writable under a read-only root (chart mounts /tmp)

    score_write_interval_s: float = Field(default=1.0, gt=0)
    # score_history_retention_days (base Settings) is applied by corvus-housekeeping

    score_drain_timeout_s: float = Field(default=20.0, gt=0)
```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/smoothing.py`:

```py
"""Exponential moving average of window scores per (pseudonym, segment, model)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import OrderedDict
from dataclasses import dataclass

type EmaKey = tuple[bytes, int, str]  # pseudonym, segment, model id


@dataclass
class _Entry:
    value: float
    windows: int
    session_id: bytes


class EmaTracker:
    """``smoothed = alpha * score + (1 - alpha) * previous``; the first window is its own value.

    Bounded: the least recently updated entries are dropped beyond ``max_entries``. Entries of a
    finished session are released with :meth:`release_session`.
    """

    def __init__(self, alpha: float, max_entries: int = 100_000) -> None:
        if not 0.0 < alpha <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError("alpha must be in (0, 1]")
        self._alpha = alpha
        self._max = max_entries
        self._entries: OrderedDict[EmaKey, _Entry] = OrderedDict()
        self._by_session: dict[bytes, set[EmaKey]] = {}

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._entries)

    def update(self, key: EmaKey, session_id: bytes, score: float) -> tuple[float, int]:
        """Fold one score in; returns ``(smoothed, windows)``."""
        entry = self._entries.get(key)
        if entry is None:
            entry = _Entry(score, 1, session_id)
            self._entries[key] = entry
            self._by_session.setdefault(session_id, set()).add(key)
            self._trim()
        else:
            entry.value = self._alpha * score + (1.0 - self._alpha) * entry.value
            entry.windows += 1
            self._entries.move_to_end(key)
        return entry.value, entry.windows

    def release_session(self, session_id: bytes) -> int:
        keys = self._by_session.pop(session_id, set())
        for key in keys:
            self._entries.pop(key, None)
        return len(keys)

    def _trim(self) -> None:
        while len(self._entries) > self._max:
            key, entry = self._entries.popitem(last=False)
            keys = self._by_session.get(entry.session_id)
            if keys is not None:
                keys.discard(key)
                if not keys:
                    del self._by_session[entry.session_id]

```

`services/src/corvus_services/scoring/writer.py`:

```py
"""Batched, non-blocking persistence of scores.

The consumer loop only calls :meth:`ScoreWriter.submit`, which never waits. ``scores_latest`` rows
are coalesced per (pseudonym, game_context, domain, model) and therefore bounded by the number of
active keys; they are never dropped. ``score_history`` rows wait in a bounded queue: when it is
full the new history row is dropped and counted, the latest row is still upserted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import logging
from collections import deque

from .metrics import ScoreMetrics
from .ports import ScoreCatalog, ScoreRecord

log = logging.getLogger("corvus.score.writer")

type LatestKey = tuple[bytes, str, str, str]


def latest_key(r: ScoreRecord) -> LatestKey:
    return r.pseudonym, r.game_context, r.domain, r.model_name


class ScoreWriter:
    def __init__(
        self,
        catalog: ScoreCatalog,
        metrics: ScoreMetrics,
        queue_size: int,
        batch_size: int,
        interval_s: float,
    ) -> None:
        self._catalog = catalog
        self._m = metrics
        self._queue_size = queue_size
        self._batch = batch_size
        self._interval = interval_s
        self._latest: dict[LatestKey, ScoreRecord] = {}
        self._history: deque[ScoreRecord] = deque()
        self._wake = asyncio.Event()
        self._flush_lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self._stopping = False

    @property
    def queued(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """``(latest rows, history rows)`` waiting to be written."""
        return len(self._latest), len(self._history)

    def submit(self, record: ScoreRecord) -> None:
        """Queue one score. Never blocks and never raises."""
        key = latest_key(record)
        current = self._latest.get(key)
        if current is None or record.scored_at >= current.scored_at:
            self._latest[key] = record
        if len(self._history) < self._queue_size:
            self._history.append(record)
        else:
            self._m.history_dropped.inc()
        self._update_gauges()
        if len(self._latest) >= self._batch or len(self._history) >= self._batch:
            self._wake.set()

    async def flush(self) -> None:
        """Write everything queued, in batches. A failed batch is put back and ends the flush."""
        async with self._flush_lock:
            while self._latest or self._history:
                keys = list(self._latest)[: self._batch]
                latest = [self._latest.pop(k) for k in keys]
                history = [
                    self._history.popleft() for _ in range(min(self._batch, len(self._history)))
                ]
                self._update_gauges()
                try:
                    await self._catalog.write_scores(latest, history)
                except Exception:
                    log.exception(
                        "could not write %d latest / %d history scores", len(latest), len(history)
                    )
                    self._m.write_failures.inc()
                    self._restore(latest, history)
                    return

    def _restore(self, latest: list[ScoreRecord], history: list[ScoreRecord]) -> None:
        for r in latest:
            current = self._latest.get(latest_key(r))
            if current is None or r.scored_at > current.scored_at:
                self._latest[latest_key(r)] = r
        room = self._queue_size - len(self._history)
        keep = history[:room] if room > 0 else []
        self._history.extendleft(reversed(keep))
        if len(keep) < len(history):
            self._m.history_dropped.inc(len(history) - len(keep))
        self._update_gauges()

    async def run(self) -> None:
        """Flush whenever a batch is full or the interval elapsed, until :meth:`stop`."""
        while not self._stopping:
            with contextlib.suppress(TimeoutError):
                await asyncio.wait_for(self._wake.wait(), self._interval)
            self._wake.clear()
            await self.flush()

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stopping = True
        self._wake.set()

    def _update_gauges(self) -> None:
        self._m.write_queue.labels("latest").set(len(self._latest))
        self._m.write_queue.labels("history").set(len(self._history))

```

```py
"""In-memory fakes of the control-plane ports (no database, no network)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

FIXED_NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)


class MutableClock:
    def __init__(self, now: datetime = FIXED_NOW) -> None:
        self.now = now

    def __call__(self) -> datetime:
        return self.now

    def advance(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        self.now += timedelta(seconds=seconds)


def sequential_ids() -> Any:
    counter = count(1)
    return lambda: UUID(int=next(counter))


def _created_key(r: Any) -> tuple[datetime, str]:
    return r.created_at, str(r.id)


class FakePoolRepo:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.rows: dict[UUID, PoolRecord] = {}

    async def create(self, pool: PoolRecord) -> None:
        if any(p.name == pool.name for p in self.rows.values()):
            raise DuplicateError("name")
        self.rows[pool.id] = pool

    async def get(self, pool_id: UUID) -> PoolRecord | None:
        return self.rows.get(pool_id)

    async def list_page(self, req: PageRequest) -> Page[PoolRecord]:
        return paginate(list(self.rows.values()), req, _created_key)

    async def update(self, pool: PoolRecord) -> bool:
        if pool.id not in self.rows:
            return False
        if any(p.name == pool.name and p.id != pool.id for p in self.rows.values()):
            raise DuplicateError("name")
        self.rows[pool.id] = pool
        return True

    async def delete(self, pool_id: UUID) -> bool:
        return self.rows.pop(pool_id, None) is not None


class FakeCatalog:

        self.raw = RawPreview(0, 0, 0, {}, [])
        self.material = SnapshotMaterial([], [])
        self.filters: list[PoolFilter] = []

    async def preview(self, pool_filter: PoolFilter) -> RawPreview:
        self.filters.append(pool_filter)
        return self.raw

    async def snapshot_material(self, pool_filter: PoolFilter) -> SnapshotMaterial:
        self.filters.append(pool_filter)
```
